+#[test]
+fn surviving_aggregate_identity_wins_over_a_counter_only_dependency() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table aEntries:\n  key: int\n  public\nview aTotals: count aEntries by .key\n  public\ntable bEntries:\n  parent: aTotals\n  public\nview bTotals: count bEntries by .parent\n  public\ntable cEntries:\n  parent: bTotals\n  public\nview cTotals: count cEntries by .parent\n  public\ntable sequenced:\n  parent: bTotals\n  ordinal: sequence by parent\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
+    let digest_a = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(5)]);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("aEntries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("a".into())), ("key", Value::Int(5))])),
+        ("bEntries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("b".into())), ("parent", Value::Id(digest_a.clone()))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let legacy_a = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(5)]);
+    let digest_b = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(digest_a.clone())]);
+    let legacy_b = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Id(legacy_a.clone())]);
+    let dangling_b = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(legacy_a.clone())]);
+    let legacy_c = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Id(legacy_b.clone())]);
+    let digest_c = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(dangling_b.clone())]);
+    let redirected_c = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(digest_b.clone())]);
+    let schema = e.schema().clone();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.delete("aTotals", &schema.tables["aTotals"], &tx.get("aTotals", &digest_a).unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
+    tx.delete("aEntries", &schema.tables["aEntries"], &tx.get("aEntries", "a").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
+    let old_source = tx.get("bEntries", "b").unwrap().unwrap();
+    let mut next_source = old_source.clone();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next_source {
+        fields.insert("parent".into(), Value::Id(legacy_a.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("bEntries", &schema.tables["bEntries"], &next_source, Some(&old_source)).unwrap();
+    let mut target = tx.get("bTotals", &digest_b).unwrap().unwrap();
+    tx.delete("bTotals", &schema.tables["bTotals"], &target).unwrap();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut target {
+        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy_b.clone()));
+        fields.insert("parent".into(), Value::Id(legacy_a.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("bTotals", &schema.tables["bTotals"], &target, None).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("bTotals", &legacy_b, 7).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("cTotals", &legacy_c, 11).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert!(tx.get("bTotals", &dangling_b).unwrap().is_some());
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &legacy_b).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &dangling_b).unwrap(), 7, "counter custody follows the surviving rebuilt parent");
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &digest_b).unwrap(), 0, "the absent dependency cannot redirect custody");
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("cTotals", &legacy_c).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("cTotals", &digest_c).unwrap(), 11, "counter-only dependents inherit the authoritative surviving parent map");
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("cTotals", &redirected_c).unwrap(), 0);
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("next".into())), ("parent", Value::Id(dangling_b))]))], 2).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap()[0].field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(8)));
+}

# Rules

**Snapback 2 optimizes the edit-to-verified loop — the agent's building an app on it, and ours building it.**

Speed is the constraint. Everything below exists to keep the edit-to-verified loop short
and to stop this repository accreting apparatus faster than anyone can remove it. These
rules bind `snapback2/` and the LLPs numbered 1000 and up; Snapback 1 is baselined, not
exempt, and its numbers may only fall.

Each rule is **[check]** (enforced by `caps`) or **[review]** (enforced by a human).

## Budgets — every budget is a trade, not a limit

- **5 blocking checks, 60s total.** A sixth requires deleting one, in the same PR. **[check]**
- **59 documents in the working set** (`llp/current/`). Today's count. A 60th requires
  archiving one — which is just removing the link. Snapback 2 aims to leave this at 15;
  Snapback 1's links are archived at promotion. **[check]**
- **12 documents in the foundation** (`llp/foundation/`). **[check]**
- **This file: 700 words.** If it grows, something becomes a check or stops being a rule. **[check]**
- **1,500 lines per source file, baseline 204.** Generated files exempt — and generated
  files are built, not committed; so are benchmark run records under `benchmarks/runs/`,
  which are evidence, not source. The baseline is Snapback 1's oversize count on the day
  the rule landed; it may not grow, and `snapback2/` contributes zero to it. **[check]**

## Blocking checks

`caps` · `ref-check` · `snapback2/scripts/test.sh` · `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs --check` · `check-inventories`

## Loop shape

- **Every check reports all failures in one run.** Fail-fast is banned. **[check]**
- **Nothing blocks on anything slower than 60 seconds.** Slow verification runs on a
  schedule, attributed to the breaking commit, and files a bounded set of issues. **[review]**
- **Fix loops get 3 rounds.** Then stop: escalate to a human or descope. **[review]**

## Time budgets

Tracked every run of `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs` (appends `snapback2/metrics/loop.jsonl`).
A regression is a P0 with a name on it.

| | budget |
|---|---|
| Incremental rebuild after a one-line edit | 15s |
| Test what you just changed | 30s |
| Blocking gate suite | 60s |
| Full build, warm cache | 5 min |
| **`snapback2 check` on a program (the agent's product latency)** | **1s** |
| **`snapback2 doctor` boot-to-ready** | **0.5s** |

## Scope

- **`NOT-DOING.md` is binding.** Moving something onto the doing-list means writing why
  and taking something off. **[review]**
- **Delete; don't deprecate.** No compat shims or migration paths before promotion. **[review]**
- **Nothing is compiled, transpiled, or generated at runtime that could be built ahead of
  time.** **[review]**
- **A spec needs an implementer and a date, or it isn't written.** **[review]**
- **Only implemented specs bind.** A document with no running code behind it is a
  proposal, and a proposal cannot block a PR or justify a check. **[review]**

## Agents

- **Agents remove apparatus freely and add none.** An agent PR that adds a check, script,
  registry, config file, or design doc needs explicit human approval saying so. **[review]**
- **2026-09-06 session exception:** the user delegated the search implementation
  decisions; one `snapback2-core/build.rs` may generate pinned Unicode tables at
  build time, alongside the existing package build. No new gate, registry,
  runtime generator, or Unicode dependency is authorized by this exception. **[review]**
- **Snapback 2 LLPs are numbered 1000 and up**; `llp-create` must be told. **[review]**
- **Snapback 4 LLPs are numbered 3000 and up** (`snapback4/`, LLP 3000); it adopts these budgets
  and loop shape as its own and keeps its scope in `snapback4/NOT-DOING.md`. **[review]**

## Shared machines

- Warm, named lanes, one per stream of work. Never clone fresh; reuse the worktree.
- **Never `git stash`.** Use a temporary commit.
- Kill only PIDs you recorded at launch. Never by name or pattern.
# What Snapback 4 Does Not Do

Longer than the doing-list on purpose. Moving something off it means writing one
line naming what it unblocks and taking something off the doing-list in the same
change. Nothing comes off during slice one (LLP 3000 §3: the clock is four weeks).

## The bars

The bakeoff gates in [LLP 3000 §3](../llp/3000-snapback4.explainer.md) are the
bars: the loop bar, hub acquisition within 2× the measured floor, client bytes
under the competitor-anchored budgets, the six scenarios green in the simulator
on the hub fixture. Everything not required to pass them does not exist yet.

## Not building

- **A second authoring language.** Quarry, one spelling, copied from Snapback 2 (LLP 1004, LLP 1007 §4b). TypeScript is for seeds, journeys, effect bodies and the client.
- **Byte- and step-priced certification.** No closure, heap, output or step ceilings at `check`; the certificate certifies shape, uniformity, completeness class and prediction eligibility. Resources are metered at runtime (LLP 2000.000 §6).
- **A per-query result cache.** No range receipts, validators, halos, absence evidence, coverage spans, extent facts, held directories, fact integrity or swap journals. The client replicates declared partitions with one watermark each (LLP 2000.000 §7).
- **Engine-minted ids for client inserts, grants, ID slices.** Ids are client-minted, time-ordered, 128-bit; the engine mints for its own writes.
- **The `drain` protocol, follower-tab inbox rows, `defineItems`, `withHistory`, `mutationTarget`, `receipt.source`, `local.caughtUp`, `partial` reason codes.** The card (`packages/snapback4/src/contract.ts`) is the whole client vocabulary; `why` carries the rest.
- **`retain` as a receipt rule.** `until-revoked` and `delivered-history` survive as the client's leave policy on a scope tombstone.
- **JavaScript in the data plane.** Queries and mutations run in the Rust interpreter inside the SQLite transaction, and in the same interpreter on the client (host decided at week 3 by measurement, LLP 2000.000 §9). A *job* may be the app's own Rust, hosted as wasm through the interpreter's operations under the job's meter (LLP 3000.005, the Moves line below); a query or mutation may not.
- **An embedded JS engine for effects.** The data plane never calls out. `emit` writes the effect durably in the mutation's commit and an external worker holding a service token claims, performs and settles it over the wire (`snapback4/worker`); the four reference effects run on the builder's Node (LLP 2000.000 §10, decided 2026-09-13).
- **Committed generated code; an auth mode; a supervised bundler.** As Snapback 2 (`rules/NOT-DOING.md`): types by inference, personas not modes, `SNAPBACK_URL` is the client contract.
- **A TypeScript twin of the interpreter.** Retired by the author's ruling of 2026-09-13 (LLP 3000 §7): one implementation, in Rust, on every host — the core's SQLite under the native module, memory under wasm on the web with the host persisting each commit's changes. The web pays 312,924 B gzip before the diet where the twin's tier paid 16,842; the conformance obligation between two interpreters ends. Expo Go runs the online tier.
- **More than one hosted target, an admin console, media transcoding or thumbnails, push delivery itself (a worker's), cron syntax beyond `every N at HH:MM`, vector or relevance-ranked search (word-prefix search is in: `words(..)` and `matching`), federation, multi-region, device-to-device sync, at-rest encryption claims.** After the clock, on evidence.
- **General observability beyond `why`, `trace`, `logs`, `data`, `sql`, server operation latency, and bounded client subscription inspection.** The `sql` verb is read-only inspection of the developer's own store (LLP 3000.007 §8.8), never an application surface. Separately declared application SQL reads are admitted for increment D (LLP 3000.009 §6.2, §14.4; the 2026-09-16 Moves line below), not implemented by this inspection verb.
- **A guide corpus.** The compiler's facts, one language card and keyword cards, as Snapback 2; no freshness dates. Every card's Quarry is compiled by the suite and the language card is run, so a card cannot promise a form the parser refuses.

- **Partial union delivery, two group audiences, a public branch.** A union syncs principal-column branches and at most one group branch, each a whole disjunct of the read rule (LLP 3000.036.000.000); a branch with an extra condition, a second group or a `public` branch is refused with the rewrite, never partially delivered; service grants add no device audience (LLP 3000.007 §20.6). A union does not combine with delivered history, read-through children, synced or row-keyed views, owner keys, timelines, private field owners, acquisition windows or direct/inherited expiry on content or membership scopes.
- **Exact horizon maintenance.** The horizon bounds acquisition (a snapshot, a bootstrap); the log never evicts or back-fills to hold a device's group at exactly N rows. A local read past the acquired horizon by key says `complete: false`.

- **Clock expressions in rules.** A read rule compares with `=` and `!=` only; `.expiresAt > now` remains a mutation `require`. Stored lifetimes use `not before .col` for server-controlled opening and `expire at .col` for expiry. The engine publishes opening commits; devices receive no unopened payload. The supported compositions and explicit exclusions are in LLP 3000.036.003.
- **A jobs framework.** No priorities, worker pools or dead letters: one FIFO of runs, one chunk at a time, a refused chunk parked with its refusal. Actions, effects and scheduled actions carry per-operation retries, deadlines and cancellation, and a record per external step (LLP 3000.009 §5.2; the Moves line below). Missed period boundaries while a server is down fire once on return, not once per missed period.
- **Asset processing.** No transcoding, thumbnails, rungs or HEIC: the bytes are served as uploaded; JPEG, PNG, WebP and MP4 only; image dimensions and optional MP4 duration read from the header; MP4 dimensions are not extracted.
- **Search beyond word prefixes.** One tokenizer (NFC, lowercase, alphanumeric words), one index shape (`scope, words(cols), order.., id`), one read (`matching`): every term a prefix of some word, the first term's words merged as lanes, bounded by the meter in a uniform scope, at most 32 words in an admitted non-uniform scope. No stemming, no ranking by relevance, no phrase or mid-word matching, no per-language folding, no intersection index for the second term (it filters the page).
- **An identity provider.** Guests, password accounts, service seats, and sessions a service mints for accounts the application authenticated itself. No phone, OAuth, magic links or MFA in the engine: an application's worker verifies those and mints the session.
- **No multi-server presence, no presence history or last-seen storage, no broadcast event stream, no connection-bound rows.** `connected[p]` stays server-wide, counting held polls and their 35 s grace; a live query that may read it re-runs in the background about every 5 seconds to stay current (LLP 3000.018). Typing and viewing use short-lived, authorized ephemeral tables in one server process (LLP 3000.017); they never sync or decide durable invariants. A device does not know presence and says so.

## Process not doing

- **2026-09-28 — ordinary mixed search** (LLP 3000.028 §3.3, lane OS round 1).
  Admit the SDK's bounded merge of current server rows and certified Left images
  for the proved single time-ordered word page. This removes application-owned
  online/held selection for that shape. One server call per requested page;
  recomputation pays again from consumed positions. The coordinator shares the
  existing device read allowance. No durable search session, extra synced rows,
  new authority or additional allowance is admitted.

- **2026-09-28 — inferred current-scope word search** (LLP 3000.028 §3.3,
  lane OS). A single bare ordinary word page may derive the exact non-expiring
  membership audience for the existing compact server plan. This removes the
  requirement to repeat that audience predicate in this narrow server query.
  The compiler supplies a scoped words index when absent; it is an ordinary
  schema index, maintained on writes and on devices, with no extra synced rows
  or new authority. The device keeps its original bare scan. Round 0 left ordered composition
  and combined accounting outside its independent subset; round 1 above admits
  that bounded SDK composition. Durable search sessions remain excluded.
- **2026-10-12 — union sync audiences** (LLP 3000.036.000.000, workstream UNION, two blind review rounds). A table syncs to the union of principal-column audiences and one group audience; a device holds a row while any branch admits its viewer. What it unblocks: owner-or-team, buyer-or-seller and owner-or-staff tables offline for every reader, the shape three app farms asked for. Taken off: "one `sync` audience per table". Partial delivery, two groups and a public branch stay excluded (above).
- **2026-09-28 — explicit owner-key coverage** (LLP 3000.028 §3.4, Lane OK commission). A public window may opt into a compiler-owned, horizon-free principal key partition to answer ordinary own-key existence offline. Taken off: the exclusion of narrower platform key distribution beside one public window. General union audiences, full own-row replication and per-query absence caches remain excluded. The projection uses existing metered maintains, adoption and whole-partition publication; existing windows do not expand.
- **2026-09-26 — a live query keeps presence current** (LLP 3000.018). A 0.4.2 probe found an observed `connected[p]` reporting `fresh: true` while stale for over a minute, and a comparative builder polled around it. What it unblocks: online marks and presence-aware lists that stay current. Taken off: "a presence stream" as an exclusion for live queries; a presence API, last-seen storage and multi-server presence stay out. Under the author's standing authorization for reworks that make queries excellent (2026-09-25).

- **No drift registries, inventories, line-pinned diagnostics registries, claim digests or frozen-record gates.** Generated projections are built, not committed.
- **No gate bound to an exact commit; no push gated on a battery.** Five blocking checks in sixty seconds, run before push; everything slower on a schedule with bounded tickets.
- **No ceiling raised in slice one.** Budgets are anchored to a competitor's measured number and recorded once in the journal.
- **No standing panel** except the two blind reviews LLP 3000 decision 4 names (partition inversion; the meter's cut on non-uniform scans). The author explicitly commissioned the one-off LLP 3000.008 panel and disjoint Astra implementation lanes on 2026-09-14; its bounded disposition is recorded in that umbrella and LLP 3000 §7.
- **No new LLP number** without first extending LLP 3000 or LLP 2000.000; no spec without running code (`rules/RULES.md`: only implemented specs bind).
- **No second session on the core** during slice one; lanes take the periphery.
- **No test matrix as the primary harness.** The simulator is; real-browser and device witnesses cover only what it cannot reach.
- **No files over 1,500 lines**, including ones copied from Snapback 2. Split on
  the way in. The one exception is the package's published documents
  (`packages/snapback4/README.md` and its linked references): the rule exists to
  keep a *source* file reviewable, and the 0.2.25 calibration measured the cost of
  applying it to a document — splitting the README was that run's single largest
  scoring loss, because the builder then had four places to look instead of one
  (LLP 3000.007 §20.19). A published document is bounded by whether a builder can
  find one way in, not by a line count; the census that enforces this rule covers
  source, and says so.

## Deliberately worse

- No compatibility with Snapback 1 or Snapback 2 apps, packages or on-disk formats.
- No API stability before the clock; every publish is `0.0.x`.
- Sparse prose documentation; the diagnostics and the recipes carry the load.
- One hosted target, SQLite in the production CLI, one platform binary at a time. A separately enabled Postgres evaluation adapter is not a hosted/deployable target (Moves below).

## Moves

- **2026-10-13 — stored lower lifetimes (`not before`) are commissioned by PAGE2** (LLP 3000.036.003). This unblocks timed disclosure without an application publication job. Per-application jobs that flip a publication flag leave this admitted path; clock expressions in rules, captured lower lifetimes for read-through children, and boundary recounts for maintained data remain excluded. HS owns handshake transport; PAGE2 declares the new semantic capability.

- **2026-10-06 — exact Following history (FH delegated round-1 ruling).**
  Admit a Following-specific server traversal and bounded volatile frontier/replay
  state under LLP 3000.026 §9. The approved design reads exact history online
  from the first page; the SDK will own continuation. The first milestone is internal event metadata
  and the oracle, with no public completeness claim. Taken off: a blanket ban on
  state for this one expiring read. General result caches, resumable queries,
  device traversal, inbox coverage certificates and history-only blocks remain
  excluded. Existing inbox bytes and runtime ceilings remain unchanged.

- **2026-09-26 — server operation latency (LLP 3000.019 §3.7).** Calibration #22
  measured each read once and could not claim repeated p95/degradation testing.
  Unblocks percentile measurements of the application's own load without a
  custom timing harness. Taken off: a latency harness written by the builder;
  general metrics, tracing infrastructure and an admin console remain excluded.

- **2026-09-23 — Quarry states intent moves onto the doing-list** (Charlie:
  "if you need to try making *significant* architectural reworks in order to
  make the data modeling, queries, and scalability be excellent and elegant,
  you can experiment with that"; LLP 3000.013). Unblocks reads that state
  predicates and order, one `view` declaration for derived data, Following
  without caps, jobs and aggregates without author-chosen bounds, an app
  object and an offline web shell. Taken off: index names and author-chosen
  engine numbers on the paved path; the timeline's promotion, pull routes and
  caps; the "Time in rules" refusal is unchanged. Stands: one interpreter, no
  JavaScript in the data plane, no lowering Quarry to SQL, no relevance-ranked
  search.

- **2026-09-16 — the remaining general-purpose program moves onto the doing-list**
  (Charlie: "complete everything ... we'll remove services when we are done
  with the workroom test rather than wait to add them in ... use the fleet";
  LLP 3000.009 §14.7). Unblocks the §7 integrated-service baseline, C3 production
  Postgres, D's authorized database capabilities and measurement-led C2/E
  work while Workroom continues. Taken off: waiting for Workroom before
  starting services, and keeping production Postgres integration outside the
  current implementation program. The completed Workroom record drives a
  retain/remove pass. Stands: one interpreter and managed writer, no managed
  SQL writes, no JavaScript transactions, no SQL in the first Workroom cell,
  no invented performance/real-provider evidence, no expo-build-1000 load,
  and no new publication or managed-service deployment authority.

- **2026-09-16 — application SQL reads move onto the doing-list** (Charlie: "admit application SQL reads"; LLP 3000.009 §6.2, §14.4, increment D). Unblocks reporting and search over authorized projection inputs and declared database-owned tables, with authorization before selection, ordering and limits. Taken off in the same change: the inspection-only exclusion for application SQL and D's pending-author gate. Implementation and qualification remain pending; SQLite and Postgres halves ship together, channels follow candidates, and A1–A3 plus the fixture pack stay first. Stands: no SQL writes into managed data, no lowering Quarry to SQL, no SQL in the first Snapback brief cell, and no publication authorization.

- **2026-09-15 — a Postgres evaluation backend moves onto the doing-list** (author: "Build the evaluation prototype"). Unblocks concrete evaluation of storage agnosticism, interpreter/database round trips and transactional sync ordering. This bounded prototype replaces full CLI/deployment integration as the next backend task; those product surfaces remain off this increment's doing-list. It shares Quarry, rules, maintains and partition logic, but uses an experimental Postgres store. Native SQL exists only as an explicitly separate comparison workload, not an application escape hatch. SQLite remains the production and local-device store. See [the experiment](./experiments/postgres/README.md).

- **2026-09-15 — the server half of LLP 3000.009 moves onto the doing-list** (author: "begin implementation using astra xhigh to code"; LLP 3000.009 §10.2, increments A1–A3). Unblocks the online-only brief's invitation, webhook and scheduled journeys without a second application server: work records whose authority is bound at admission, ids bound to their operation and arguments, declared action results, a generated handler context with a durable record per external step, declared routes and webhooks, scheduled actions under service seats, and `serve` supervising the runtime. Taken off in the same change: "A jobs framework" narrows — actions, effects and scheduled actions get per-operation retries, deadlines and cancellation; priorities, worker pools and dead letters stay out — and the actions card's "supervise the worker as an ordinary Node process" leaves. Stands: no JavaScript in the data plane, no identity provider in the engine, and no `ctx.sql`, projections or SQL reads in this increment.

- **2026-09-15 — the Postgres access boundary moves onto the doing-list** (LLP 3000.009 §10.2, increment C1). Unblocks measuring Postgres behind a batched access boundary instead of row-at-a-time calls: transaction-scoped prefetch, a pipelined commit tail, one portable index-key bound checked on both stores, and the corpus, conformance and device suites on both stores. Taken off in the same change: the evaluation prototype's single-adapter framing, in which the only next step was an unbatched store. Stands: Postgres is not a hosted or deployable target; its refusals of assets, jobs, actions and schedules, and `serve`, `deploy` and backup on Postgres, wait for increment C3.

- **2026-09-13 — word search, effects, service seats and presence move onto the doing-list** (author: "add all the things we need for Clique and Interview"; the full-brief Clique record's remaining capability lines and Interview's adapter responsibilities). What it unblocks: Clique M5's three search scopes online and offline on one index, M6's push seam without connection leases hand-built in tables, M8's digest emitted rather than logged into a table, Interview's phone sign-in and model workers as a service that mints sessions instead of proxying every request, and the ranked feed of LLP 3000.004 on the `feeds` card. Taken off in the same change: "an embedded JS engine for effects, until measured" (the engine never calls out; a worker does), "word search" from the package's exclusions. Stands: no JavaScript in the data plane, no relevance ranking, no identity provider in the engine.
- **2026-09-12 — expiry, assets and jobs move onto the doing-list** (author: "complete snapback4 to the point where the entire clique benchmark can be run"). What it unblocks: the struck half of the Clique brief (M4 media, M5 view-once and expiry with no client open, M8's scheduled digest). Taken off in the same change: the "one photo path" and "cron syntax" exclusions above narrow to transcoding and to cron beyond `every N [at HH:MM]`; the "time in rules" exclusion stands, answered by `expire at .col` rather than a rule.
- **2026-09-13 — native jobs on (author: "write up an LLP about this and then implement").** Unblocks the scoring half of a feed — floats, vectors, real loops, a typed schema — without putting any of it into Quarry, and gives the model half of LLP 3000.004 a seat inside the bounds: one chunk per commit, the job ceilings, fuel, no I/O. Off the doing-list in the same change: the "external ranker with a service seat" of LLP 3000.004 §6.5 is no longer the only shape for compute over the store; it remains the shape for the network. Ranked and vector search, effects execution and an embedded JS engine stay above.
- **2026-09-13 — `sql`, a fifth named observability verb, moves onto the doing-list** (author ruling on LLP 3000.007 §14.10). Read-only SQL over generated per-table views of the developer's own store, under `dev` or against a `--release` directory; never rule-filtered, never an application surface. What it unblocks: the ground truth two Clique essays said Snapback lacked beside Postgres ("there is no underlying Postgres to query"), and the inspection the 0.2.6 Astra lane did by copying its SQLite file. Taken off in the same change: SQL reads as an application query surface (LLP 3000.007 §9.1) leave the doing-list until the reporting gap is measured after the language relaxations; reporting is Quarry's, inspection is `sql`'s. Stands: no JavaScript in the data plane, one authoring language.

- **2026-09-14 — the simulator witness is published for app builders (LLP 3000.007 §20.10, S30).** Unblocks native offline proof artifacts; replaces the repository-only Metro witness on the doing-list. Real-browser and device witnesses still cover only what the deterministic simulator cannot reach.

- **2026-09-14 — development clock control (S27, calibration F5)** moves onto the doing-list to unblock expiry and scheduled-digest tests without real-minute waits or backdated seeds; waiting on real time leaves the development test path, while production clock controls stay off the doing-list.

- **2026-09-25 — ephemeral tables enact the standing realtime line of LLP 3000.009 §12 (LLP 3000.017).** Unblocks typing and viewing without durable outbox traffic. Nothing leaves the doing-list: this enacts an already admitted scope. Last-seen storage, multi-server presence, a separate presence stream and ephemeral authority over durable invariants remain excluded.

- **2026-09-30 — bounded client subscription inspection (author's PR round-0 task)**
  moves onto the doing-list: query-group queue/in-flight/withdrawal counts and
  bounded latency/cause samples explain mounted screens flashing empty. Taken off
  the doing-list: builders must reconstruct this pressure from ad-hoc console
  instrumentation. General observability beyond the named verbs remains excluded;
  there is no telemetry transport or server admin console (LLP 3000.023 §10).

+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+type LegacyIdentities = Vec<(String, Vec<(String, Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>)>)>;
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+type LegacyIdentityMap = BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>>>;
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    value: &Value,
+    definitions: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<crate::schema::ColumnType>>,
+    identities: &mut LegacyIdentityMap,
+) {
+    match (kind, value) {
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(old)) => {
+            let Some(kinds) = definitions.get(table) else { return };
+            if identities.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| ids.contains_key(old)) { return; }
+            let Some(values) = crate::json_codec::from_text::<Vec<Value>>(old).ok()
+                .filter(|values| values.len() == kinds.len()) else { return };
+            let key: Vec<_> = kinds.iter().cloned().zip(values).collect();
+            identities.entry(table.clone()).or_default().insert(old.clone(), key.clone());
+            for (kind, value) in &key {
+                collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(kind, value, definitions, identities);
+            }
+        }
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) =>
+            collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(inner, value, definitions, identities),
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
+            for value in values { collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(of, value, definitions, identities); },
+        _ => {}
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn insert_sequence_identity(
+    target: &str,
+    old: String,
+    key: Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>,
+    definitions: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<crate::schema::ColumnType>>,
+    identities: &mut LegacyIdentityMap,
+) {
+    if identities.get(target).is_some_and(|ids| ids.contains_key(&old)) { return; }
+    identities.entry(target.to_owned()).or_default().insert(old, key.clone());
+    for (kind, value) in &key {
+        collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(kind, value, definitions, identities);
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn settle_legacy_maintained_ids(
+    legacy: &LegacyIdentities,
+    base: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>, RuntimeError> {
+    let mut ids = base.clone();
+    let identity_count = legacy.iter().map(|(_, rows)| rows.len()).sum::<usize>();
+    for _ in 0..=identity_count.saturating_add(1) {
+        let mut next_ids = base.clone();
+        for (target, rows) in legacy {
+            let target_ids = next_ids.entry(target.clone()).or_default();
+            for (old, key) in rows {
+                let key: Vec<_> = key.iter().map(|(kind, value)| {
+                    let mut value = value.clone();
+                    rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &mut value, &ids);
+                    value
+                }).collect();
+                let next = maintained_id(&key);
+                if old != &next { target_ids.insert(old.clone(), next); }
+            }
+        }
+        if next_ids == ids { return Ok(next_ids); }
+        ids = next_ids;
+    }
+    Err(RuntimeError::Schema("legacy aggregate identity references form a cycle".into()))
+}

+#[test]
+fn identity_adoption_rekeys_sequence_history_without_reusing_deleted_ordinals() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table entries:\n  bucket: int\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .bucket\n  public\ntable sequenced:\n  total: totals\n  ordinal: sequence by total\n  unique total, ordinal\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("e7".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(7))])),
+        ("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("e9".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(9))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let digest7 = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let digest9 = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(9)]);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("gone".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7.clone()))])),
+        ("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("kept".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7.clone()))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    e.seed_delete("sequenced", "gone").unwrap();
+
+    let legacy7 = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let legacy9 = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(9)]);
+    let schema = e.schema().clone();
+    let target = schema.tables["totals"].clone();
+    let entries = schema.tables["entries"].clone();
+    let sequenced = schema.tables["sequenced"].clone();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    let mut row = tx.get("totals", &digest7).unwrap().unwrap();
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &row).unwrap();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row {
+        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy7.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &row, None).unwrap();
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &tx.get("totals", &digest9).unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
+    tx.delete("entries", &entries, &tx.get("entries", "e9").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
+    let old = tx.get("sequenced", "kept").unwrap().unwrap();
+    let mut next = old.clone();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
+        fields.insert("total".into(), Value::Id(legacy7.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("sequenced", &sequenced, &next, Some(&old)).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy7, 7).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &digest7, 4).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy9, crate::value::I53_MAX).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &digest9, 12).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("ordinary", &legacy7, 11).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy7).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy9).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest7).unwrap(), 7, "the deleted allocating row and lower destination counter cannot lower the high-water mark");
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest9).unwrap(), crate::value::I53_MAX);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("ordinary", &legacy7).unwrap(), 11, "translation is scoped by parent table and id");
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    let kept = e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap().pop().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(kept.field("total").unwrap(), &Value::Id(digest7.clone()));
+    assert_eq!(kept.field("ordinal").unwrap(), &Value::Int(2));
+
+    e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("next".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7))]))], 2).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap().into_iter().find(|row| row.field("id") == Ok(&Value::Id("next".into()))).unwrap().field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(8)));
+    let error = e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("full".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest9.clone()))]))], 2).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(error.refusal().code, "E_SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED");
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest9).unwrap(), crate::value::I53_MAX, "overflow refusal must not change the migrated counter");
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}

+#[test]
+fn removing_an_aggregate_normalizes_retained_sequence_custody_before_marking_the_store() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table entries:\n  bucket: int\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .bucket\n  public\ntable sequenced:\n  total: totals\n  ordinal: sequence by total\n  unique total, ordinal\n  public\n";
+    const WITHOUT_AGGREGATE: &str = "table entries:\n  bucket: int\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
+    e.seed_at([("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(3))]))], 0).unwrap();
+    let digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(3)]);
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(3)]);
+    let target = e.schema().tables["totals"].clone();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    let mut row = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().unwrap();
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &row).unwrap();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row {
+        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &row, None).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy, 5).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    let removed = compile(WITHOUT_AGGREGATE);
+    e.adopt_at(removed.schema, removed.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest).unwrap(), 5);
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().meta(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META).unwrap().as_deref(), Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION));
+
+    let restored = compile(SOURCE);
+    e.adopt_at(restored.schema, restored.programs, 2).unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("next".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest))]))], 3).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap()[0].field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(6)));
+}

+#[test]
+fn counter_only_aggregate_reference_chains_rekey_to_the_final_digest() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table aEntries:\n  key: int\n  public\nview aTotals: count aEntries by .key\n  public\ntable bEntries:\n  parent: aTotals\n  public\nview bTotals: count bEntries by .parent\n  public\ntable sequenced:\n  parent: bTotals\n  ordinal: sequence by parent\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
+    let legacy_a = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(5)]);
+    let legacy_b = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Id(legacy_a.clone())]);
+    let digest_a = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(5)]);
+    let digest_b = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(digest_a)]);
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("bTotals", &legacy_b, 9).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &legacy_b).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &digest_b).unwrap(), 9, "the absent referenced aggregate identity must settle before its dependent counter key");
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}

+#[test]
+fn sequence_identity_rekey_rolls_back_with_the_adoption_writer() {
+    let mut store = Store::memory().unwrap();
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy, 11).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.rewrite_sequence_ids(&BTreeMap::from([(
+        "totals".into(),
+        BTreeMap::from([(legacy.clone(), digest.clone())]),
+    )])).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest).unwrap(), 11);
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy).unwrap(), 11);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest).unwrap(), 0);
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}

//! Aggregate deltas, derived rebuilds and the device overlay.
use super::runner::Runner;
use super::write::Origin;
use crate::error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError};
use crate::schema::{Maintain, MaintainKind, maintained_id};
#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
use crate::schema::materialize_optional_fields;
#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
use crate::rows::{Bounds, Dir};
use crate::value::{I53_MAX, I53_MIN, Value};
use crate::value::canonical_json;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

const GLOBAL: &str = "$global";

fn target_group_key(maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Vec<Value> {
    if maintain.by.is_empty() { vec![Value::Bool(true)] } else { key.to_vec() }
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
fn has_legacy_maintained_reference(
    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
) -> bool {
    match kind {
        crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table } => ids.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| !ids.is_empty()),
        crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner)
        | crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. }
        | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => has_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, ids),
        _ => false,
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(
    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
    value: &mut Value,
    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
) -> bool {
    match (kind, value) {
        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
            *id = next.clone();
            true
        }
        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, value, ids),
        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
        _ => false,
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
type LegacyIdentities = Vec<(String, Vec<(String, Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>)>)>;

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
type LegacyIdentityMap = BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>>>;

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
fn decode_legacy_sequence_identity(
    old: &str,
    kinds: &[crate::schema::ColumnType],
) -> Option<Vec<Value>> {
    let values = crate::json_codec::from_text::<Vec<Value>>(old).ok()?;
    (values.len() == kinds.len()
        && crate::value::canonical_json(&values) == old
        && kinds.iter().zip(&values).all(|(kind, value)|
            crate::engine::validate::fits(kind, Some(value))))
        .then_some(values)
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
fn collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(
    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
    value: &Value,
    definitions: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<crate::schema::ColumnType>>,
    identities: &mut LegacyIdentityMap,
) {
    match (kind, value) {
        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(old)) => {
            let Some(kinds) = definitions.get(table) else { return };
            if identities.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| ids.contains_key(old)) { return; }
            let Some(values) = decode_legacy_sequence_identity(old, kinds) else { return };
            let key: Vec<_> = kinds.iter().cloned().zip(values).collect();
            identities.entry(table.clone()).or_default().insert(old.clone(), key.clone());
            for (kind, value) in &key {
                collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(kind, value, definitions, identities);
            }
        }
        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) =>
            collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(inner, value, definitions, identities),
        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
            for value in values { collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(of, value, definitions, identities); },
        _ => {}
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
fn insert_sequence_identity(
    target: &str,
    old: String,
    key: Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>,
    definitions: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<crate::schema::ColumnType>>,
    identities: &mut LegacyIdentityMap,
) {
    if identities.get(target).is_some_and(|ids| ids.contains_key(&old)) { return; }
    identities.entry(target.to_owned()).or_default().insert(old, key.clone());
    for (kind, value) in &key {
        collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(kind, value, definitions, identities);
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
fn settle_legacy_maintained_ids(
    legacy: &LegacyIdentities,
    base: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>, RuntimeError> {
    let mut ids = base.clone();
    let identity_count = legacy.iter().map(|(_, rows)| rows.len()).sum::<usize>();
    for _ in 0..=identity_count.saturating_add(1) {
        let mut next_ids = base.clone();
        for (target, rows) in legacy {
            let target_ids = next_ids.entry(target.clone()).or_default();
            for (old, key) in rows {
                // A surviving aggregate row is the authoritative parent that
                // rebuild and row-reference rewriting will address. An
                // independently decoded counter-only dependency must not
                // redirect that map when a referenced target is absent.
                if base.get(target).is_some_and(|ids| ids.contains_key(old)) { continue; }
                let key: Vec<_> = key.iter().map(|(kind, value)| {
                    let mut value = value.clone();
                    rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &mut value, &ids);
                    value
                }).collect();
                let next = maintained_id(&key);
                if old != &next { target_ids.insert(old.clone(), next); }
            }
        }
        if next_ids == ids { return Ok(next_ids); }
        ids = next_ids;
    }
    Err(RuntimeError::Schema("legacy aggregate identity references form a cycle".into()))
}

impl Runner<'_> {
    // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — no predicted delta enters receipt-derived state.
    pub(super) fn defer_receipt_maintain(&self, m: &Maintain) -> bool {
        self.device && self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target)
    }

    // Cache ordinary group keys once per target/query. Predicates and receipt
    // fields are never evaluated; unknown/computed keys conservatively freeze
    // the target. An unpinned read is incomplete if any group is dirty, while
    // each returned row still decides independently whether to recount.
    #[inline(never)]
    pub(super) fn receipt_maintain_pending(&mut self, m: &Maintain, group: Option<&[Value]>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        if !self.defer_receipt_maintain(m) { return Ok(false); }
        if !self.receipt_pending_groups.contains_key(&m.target) {
            let fields = if let Some(k) = &m.row_key { vec![k.source_key.clone()] }
                else { m.by.iter().map(|f| m.aliases.get(f).unwrap_or(f).clone()).collect() };
            let mut groups = self.receipt_overlay_groups(&m.source, &fields, !m.computed.is_empty())?;
            if let Some(k) = &m.row_key {
                let member = self.receipt_overlay_groups(&k.table, std::slice::from_ref(&k.member_key), false)?;
                groups = groups.zip(member).map(|(mut source, member)| { source.extend(member); source });
            }
            self.receipt_pending_groups.insert(m.target.clone(), groups);
        }
        let dirty = self.receipt_pending_groups[&m.target].as_ref().is_none_or(|keys|
            group.map_or(!keys.is_empty(), |group| keys.iter().any(|key| key == group)));
        if dirty {
            self.value_source_incomplete = true;
            self.components.note(|frame| frame.pending = true);
        }
        Ok(dirty)
    }

    fn receipt_overlay_groups(&self, table: &str, fields: &[String], computed: bool) -> Result<Option<Vec<Vec<Value>>>, RuntimeError> {
        if !self.tx.has_provisional(table)? { return Ok(Some(Vec::new())); }
        if computed || fields.iter().any(|f| self.schema.receipt_dependencies.get(table).is_some_and(|owned| owned.contains(f))) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        self.tx.provisional_groups(table, fields)
    }

    // Recover a read's parent/group from the pinned index. A member point uses
    // one ordinary-key lookup; a scan without the parent stays conservative.
    pub(super) fn receipt_read_group(&mut self, m: &Maintain, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> Result<Option<Vec<Value>>, RuntimeError> {
        if !self.defer_receipt_maintain(m) { return Ok(None); }
        let columns = self.schema.tables[&m.target].indexes[index].columns();
        let pinned = |field: &str| columns.iter().position(|c| c == field).and_then(|i| key.get(i)).cloned();
        if let Some(k) = &m.row_key {
            if let Some(parent) = pinned(&k.member_key) { return Ok(Some(vec![parent])); }
            if let Some(id) = pinned("member").or_else(|| pinned("id")) {
                let row = self.metered_scan(|r, scope| r.tx.get(scope, &k.table, id.as_str()?))?;
                return Ok(row.and_then(|row| row.field(&k.member_key).ok().cloned()).map(|v| vec![v]));
            }
            return Ok(None);
        }
        Ok(m.by.iter().map(|f| pinned(f)).collect())
    }

    pub(super) fn maintain(&mut self, source: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.receipt_pending_groups.clear();
        // Inserts ordinarily charge their actual aggregate work. A deferred
        // predicate cannot select that work on a device, so use the same public
        // worst-case reservation as update/delete before skipping it. Already
        // prepaid writes must not pay twice.
        if self.device && !self.maintain_prepaid && self.schema.maintains.iter().any(|m|
            m.source == source && m.private.is_none() && m.row_key.is_none() && (self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target) || self.schema.tables[&m.target].sync.is_none())) {
            self.reserve_maintains(source, &self.schema.tables[source])?;
        }
        self.maintain_row_views(source, old, new)?;
        let maintains = self.schema.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.source == source && maintain.row_key.is_none());
        for maintain in maintains {
            if self.defer_receipt_maintain(maintain) || (self.device && self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].sync.is_none()) { continue; }
            let source_bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]);
            let target = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.target];
            let bytes = source_bytes.saturating_mul(2).saturating_add(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(target).saturating_mul(16 + 4 * target.indexes.len() as u64));
            let prepaid = self.maintain_prepaid;
            if maintain.private.is_some() && self.column_prepaid { self.maintain_prepaid = true; }
            let result = self.maintain_scratch(bytes, |runner| runner.maintain_one(maintain, old, new));
            self.maintain_prepaid = prepaid;
            result?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — reserve interpreted images, both keys, targets and index buffers before allocation; release transient ownership on every exit.
    pub(super) fn maintain_scratch<T>(&mut self, bytes: u64, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
        if self.maintain_prepaid { return work(self); }
        self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
        let result = work(self);
        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = self.meter.used.heap_bytes.saturating_sub(bytes);
        result
    }

    fn maintain_one(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let table = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
        let mut changes: Vec<(Vec<Value>, i128)> = Vec::new();
        for (image, direction) in [(old, -1), (new, 1)] {
            let Some(image) = image else { continue };
            self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
            let image = crate::schema::row_image(image, table);
            if !maintain.selected(&image) { continue; }
            let key = maintain.source_key(&image);
            let change = delta(maintain, &image, direction)?;
            if let Some(existing) = changes.iter_mut().find(|(k, _)| *k == key) { existing.1 += change; }
            else { changes.push((key, change)); }
        }
        for (key, change) in changes {
            if let Some(retiring) = self.retiring.as_mut() {
                let entry = retiring.aggregates.entry((maintain.target.clone(), canonical_json(&key))).or_insert_with(|| (key, 0));
                entry.1 = entry.1.checked_add(change).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?;
                continue;
            }
            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Apply a retirement's net aggregate changes, one per target row, in
    /// key order. Only a total the commit really ends with can overflow.
    pub(super) fn apply_retired_aggregates(&mut self, changes: BTreeMap<(String, String), (Vec<Value>, i128)>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        for ((target, _), (key, change)) in changes {
            let maintain = schema.maintain_for(&target).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing maintain for {target}")))?;
            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, None)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    pub(crate) fn rebuild_maintain_reported(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, report: &mut crate::store::adoption_report::AdoptionReport) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
        self.rebuilt_source_rows = 0;
        self.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
        let rows = self.rebuilt_source_rows;
        report.views.push(crate::store::adoption_report::ViewBuild { name: maintain.label(), rows, elapsed: started.elapsed() });
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Derive every legacy-to-digest aggregate id map to a fixed point, then
    /// rewrite typed references before rebuilding the target rows. The fixed
    /// point matters when one aggregate groups by a reference to another.
    /// Every pass is inside the adoption writer transaction, so no reader can
    /// observe a dangling intermediate reference.
    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&mut self, maintains: &[Maintain], previous: Option<&crate::schema::Schema>, activation_tx: Option<&crate::store::Tx<'_>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        let mut legacy: LegacyIdentities = Vec::new();
        let mut definitions = BTreeMap::<String, Vec<crate::schema::ColumnType>>::new();
        for maintain in maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
            let target = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.target];
            definitions.insert(maintain.target.clone(), maintain.group_fields().into_iter()
                .map(|field| target.columns[&field].clone()).collect());
        }
        if let Some(previous) = previous {
            for maintain in previous.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
                let target = &previous.tables[&maintain.target];
                definitions.insert(maintain.target.clone(), maintain.group_fields().into_iter()
                    .map(|field| target.columns[&field].clone()).collect());
            }
        }
        let mut sequence_identity_map = LegacyIdentityMap::new();
        for maintain in maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
            // The durable legacy address is the predecessor's canonical
            // logical group tuple. Decode that address with predecessor types:
            // candidate projection may already have removed predecessor group
            // columns when adoption also changes the maintain declaration.
            let identity_schema = previous.unwrap_or(self.schema);
            let identity_maintain = identity_schema.maintain_for(&maintain.target)
                .filter(|old| old.private.is_none() && old.row_key.is_none())
                .unwrap_or(maintain);
            let identity_target = identity_schema.table(&maintain.target)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| &self.schema.tables[&maintain.target]);
            let fields: Vec<_> = identity_maintain.group_fields().into_iter().map(|field| {
                let kind = identity_target.columns.get(&field).expect("validated maintain group").clone();
                (field, kind)
            }).collect();
            let mut rows = Vec::new();
            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
            loop {
                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
                if page.is_empty() { break; }
                for (row, encoded) in page {
                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
                    let old = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
                    let address = crate::json_codec::from_text::<Vec<Value>>(&old).ok()
                        .filter(|key| key.len() == fields.len());
                    let values = match address {
                        Some(key) => key,
                        None => fields.iter().map(|(field, _)| Ok(row.field(field)?.clone()))
                            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, RuntimeError>>()?,
                    };
                    let key: Vec<_> = fields.iter().zip(values).map(|((_, kind), value)| (kind.clone(), value)).collect();
                    rows.push((old, key));
                }
            }
            legacy.push((maintain.target.clone(), rows));
            for old in self.tx.sequence_ids(&maintain.target)? {
                let kinds: Vec<_> = fields.iter().map(|(_, kind)| kind.clone()).collect();
                let values = decode_legacy_sequence_identity(&old, &kinds);
                if let Some(values) = values {
                    let key = fields.iter().zip(values).map(|((_, kind), value)| (kind.clone(), value)).collect();
                    insert_sequence_identity(&maintain.target, old, key, &definitions, &mut sequence_identity_map);
                }
            }
        }

        // A removed aggregate can leave parent-counter history even after its
        // derived rows and every allocating row are gone. The store marker
        // covers that retained custody too: translate it from predecessor
        // types now so reintroducing the same maintained target cannot revive
        // a legacy address under a current marker.
        if let Some(previous) = previous {
            for maintain in previous.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain|
                maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()
                    && !maintains.iter().any(|current| current.target == maintain.target)) {
                let target = &previous.tables[&maintain.target];
                let fields: Vec<_> = maintain.group_fields().into_iter().map(|field|
                    (field.clone(), target.columns[&field].clone())).collect();
                for old in self.tx.sequence_ids(&maintain.target)? {
                    let kinds: Vec<_> = fields.iter().map(|(_, kind)| kind.clone()).collect();
                    let values = decode_legacy_sequence_identity(&old, &kinds);
                    if let Some(values) = values {
                        let key = fields.iter().zip(values).map(|((_, kind), value)| (kind.clone(), value)).collect();
                        insert_sequence_identity(&maintain.target, old, key, &definitions, &mut sequence_identity_map);
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        // Row references retain the established contract: only a stored
        // aggregate target proves an old address. Sequence custody is broader;
        // its parent key persists after target/source/child deletion, so its
        // independently decoded legacy tuple joins the same fixed point.
        let ids = settle_legacy_maintained_ids(&legacy, &BTreeMap::new())?;
        let sequence_legacy: LegacyIdentities = sequence_identity_map.into_iter()
            .map(|(target, rows)| (target, rows.into_iter().collect())).collect();
        let sequence_ids = settle_legacy_maintained_ids(&sequence_legacy, &ids)?;

        // Sequence counters are keyed by the referenced parent table and id,
        // independently of any surviving allocating row. Translate them from
        // the same target-specific maps before rows are rebuilt; colliding
        // old/current counters retain the larger high-water value.
        // @ref LLP 3000.007.003#3.0 — digest adoption re-keys dependent sequence custody in the same transaction.
        let mut rewritten = self.tx.rewrite_sequence_ids(&sequence_ids)?;

        // Release retention is part of the store: a hidden row or column may
        // still name an aggregate target that remains active through adoption.
        // Rewrite its image and reference ledger in this transaction too.
        rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(match activation_tx {
            Some(tx) => crate::store::dormant::rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(tx, &ids)?,
            None => 0,
        });

        let references: Vec<_> = self.schema.tables.iter().filter_map(|(name, table)| {
            let columns: Vec<_> = table.columns.iter().filter_map(|(column, kind)|
                has_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &ids).then(|| (column.clone(), kind.clone())))
                .collect();
            (!columns.is_empty()).then(|| (name.clone(), table.clone(), columns))
        }).collect();
        for (name, table, columns) in references {
            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
            loop {
                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &name, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
                if page.is_empty() { break; }
                for (old, encoded) in page {
                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
                    let mut next = old.clone();
                    let mut changed = false;
                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
                        for (column, kind) in &columns {
                            let Some(value) = fields.get_mut(column) else { continue };
                            changed |= rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, value, &ids);
                        }
                    }
                    if changed {
                        self.tx.put(&name, &table, &next, Some(&old))?;
                        rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(rewritten)
    }

    /// Build one aggregate from the rows in the store: the target's rows go,
    /// then every source row contributes once. A schema change that adds or
    /// redefines a `maintain` calls this, so a count over existing rows is
    /// right from its first read (day two, LLP 2000.000 §11.2).
    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    pub(crate) fn rebuild_maintain(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let heap = self.meter.used.heap_bytes;
        let saved = self.column_rebuild;
        self.column_rebuild |= maintain.private.is_some();
        let result = self.rebuild_maintain_inner(maintain);
        self.column_rebuild = saved;
        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = heap;
        result
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    fn rebuild_maintain_inner(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        if maintain.row_key.is_some() { return self.rebuild_row_view(maintain); }
        let target = self.schema.table(&maintain.target).expect("validated");
        let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
        let target_bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(target).saturating_mul(16 + 4 * target.indexes.len() as u64);
        self.meter.heap(target_bytes.saturating_mul(256))?;
        loop {
            let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
            if page.is_empty() { break; }
            for (existing, key) in page {
                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
                self.refuse_timeline_write(&maintain.target, crate::schema::Effect::Delete)?;
                let entries = self.tx.delete(&maintain.target, target, &existing)?;
                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
                self.row_changed(&maintain.target, Some(&existing), None, Origin::Maintained)?;
            }
        }
        let source = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
        self.meter.heap(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(source).saturating_mul(256))?;
        let mut totals: BTreeMap<String, (Vec<Value>, i128)> = BTreeMap::new();
        bounds = Bounds::default();
        loop {
            let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.source, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
            if page.is_empty() { break; }
            for (mut image, key) in page {
                self.rebuilt_source_rows += 1;
                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
                materialize_optional_fields(&mut image, source);
                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
                if !maintain.selected(&image) { continue; }
                // @ref LLP 3000.028#6 — a total unique owner key has one contribution; backfill streams bounded pages instead of retaining all lifetime keys in a totals map.
                if maintain.own_keys.is_some() {
                    let heap = self.meter.used.heap_bytes;
                    self.meter.heap(target_bytes)?;
                    self.apply_aggregate(maintain, maintain.source_key(&image), 1, Some(true))?;
                    self.meter.used.heap_bytes = heap;
                    continue;
                }
                self.meter.heap(target_bytes)?;
                let key = maintain.source_key(&image);
                let change = delta(maintain, &image, 1)?;
                let entry = match totals.entry(canonical_json(&key)) {
                    std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Occupied(entry) => {
                        self.meter.used.heap_bytes -= target_bytes;
                        entry.into_mut()
                    }
                    std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Vacant(entry) => entry.insert((key, 0)),
                };
                entry.1 = entry.1.checked_add(change).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?;
            }
        }
        for (_, (key, change)) in totals {
            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, Some(true))?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn live_sum(&self, maintain: &Maintain) -> bool {
        matches!(maintain.kind, MaintainKind::Sum { .. }) && self.schema.table(&maintain.source).is_some_and(|source| source.is_expiring())
    }

    /// A zero sum is still a group while source rows remain: one signed
    /// contribution may expire before the other. Keep its candidate row so
    /// a scan, snapshot and offline replica can discover the later live sum.
    fn aggregate_source_present(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        // One returned source image and its encoded key (MemoryRows also materializes count_prefix).
        let bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]).saturating_mul(2);
        self.maintain_scratch(bytes, |runner| {
            let source = &runner.schema.tables[&maintain.source];
            let index = maintain.contribution_index();
            if !source.indexes.contains_key(&index) { return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("maintain {} needs its contribution index", maintain.target))); }
            runner.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
            let present = runner.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.count_prefix(allowance, &maintain.source, &index, key, 1))? != 0;
            // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — a local positive witness keeps zero; absence needs complete, currently held source coverage.
            if !present && runner.device && !runner.aggregate_source_complete(maintain, key)? {
                runner.unknown_fact(&maintain.source, &index, key, "zero-sum occupancy");
                return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("the zero-sum group's source occupancy is not known locally; queued without a predicted row".into()));
            }
            Ok(present)
        })
    }

    fn aggregate_source_complete(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        let source = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.source];
        if source.sync.as_ref().is_none_or(|sync| sync.horizon.is_some()) || self.schema.maintain_subset_unknown(&maintain.target) { return Ok(false); }
        // The target has the same bare audience keys, but no source horizon.
        if !self.upsert_absence_proven(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &target_group_key(maintain, key))? { return Ok(false); }
        for (name, index) in &source.indexes {
            let values = index.columns().iter().map_while(|column| maintain.by.iter().position(|field| field == column).map(|n| key[n].clone())).collect::<Vec<_>>();
            if self.retained_group(&maintain.source, name, &values)? { return Ok(false); }
        }
        Ok(true)
    }

    fn apply_aggregate(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: Vec<Value>, change: i128, source_present: Option<bool>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        if self.schema.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.owns(&maintain.target)) {
            return Err(super::timeline::refusal("E_TIMELINE_OWNED", "timeline-owned tables cannot be aggregate targets; maintain a mapped application table instead"));
        }
        let id = maintained_id(&key);
        let target = self.schema.table(&maintain.target).expect("validated");
        self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
        let existing = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, &maintain.target, &id))?;
        let target_key = target_group_key(maintain, &key);
        if self.device && existing.is_none() && !self.upsert_absence_proven(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &target_key)? {
            self.unknown_fact(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &target_key, "aggregate base");
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("the affected aggregate value or its absence is not known locally; queued without a predicted row".into()));
        }
        let old_value = existing.as_ref().and_then(|row| row.field("value").ok()).map(Value::as_int).transpose()?.unwrap_or(0);
        let next = i128::from(old_value) + change;
        if !(I53_MIN as i128..=I53_MAX as i128).contains(&next) {
            return Err(aggregate_overflow(maintain));
        }
        let keep_zero = next == 0 && self.live_sum(maintain) && match source_present {
            Some(present) => present,
            None => self.aggregate_source_present(maintain, &key)?,
        };
        if next == 0 && !keep_zero {
            if let Some(existing) = existing {
                self.refuse_timeline_write(&maintain.target, crate::schema::Effect::Delete)?;
                let entries = self.tx.delete(&maintain.target, target, &existing)?;
                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
                self.row_changed(&maintain.target, Some(&existing), None, Origin::Maintained)?;
            }
            self.mirror_column(maintain, &key, 0)?;
            return Ok(());
        }
        let mut row = crate::small_map::collect([("id".to_owned(), Value::Id(id.clone())), ("value".to_owned(), Value::Int(next as i64))]);
        for (field, value) in maintain.group_fields().iter().zip(key.iter().cloned()) {
            row.insert(field.clone(), value);
        }
        // @ref LLP 3000.013.001#3-global-maintained-view-representation — stores index the one logical empty group by a hidden constant.
        if maintain.by.is_empty() { row.insert(GLOBAL.into(), Value::Bool(true)); }
        let row = Value::Row(row.into());
        if existing.as_ref() == Some(&row) { return Ok(()); }
        let entries = self.tx.put(&maintain.target, target, &row, existing.as_ref())?;
        self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
        self.row_changed(&maintain.target, existing.as_ref(), Some(&row), Origin::Maintained)?;
        self.mirror_column(maintain, &key, next as i64)
    }
}

pub(super) fn delta(maintain: &Maintain, source: &Value, direction: i64) -> Result<i128, RuntimeError> {
    Ok(match &maintain.kind {
        MaintainKind::Count => i128::from(direction),
        MaintainKind::Sum { of } => i128::from(direction).checked_mul(i128::from(source.field(of)?.as_int()?)).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?,
    })
}

// @ref LLP 3000.007#17 — an internal sum names its maintain and column, never a retained contribution or computed value.
pub(super) fn aggregate_overflow(maintain: &Maintain) -> RuntimeError {
    RuntimeError::AggregateOverflow { maintain: maintain.private.as_ref().map_or_else(|| maintain.target.clone(), |o|o.table.clone()), column: maintain.private.as_ref().map_or_else(|| "value".into(), |o|o.column.clone()) }
}

#[cfg(all(test, feature = "sqlite"))]
mod timeline_tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn timeline_owned_tables_cannot_be_maintain_targets() {
        let schema = crate::engine::timeline_authority::write_tests::schema();
        let mut store = crate::Store::memory().unwrap(); store.install(&schema).unwrap();
        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &schema, crate::Context::system().at(1), crate::meter::Meter::new(crate::Ceilings::unbounded(),crate::meter::Cut::Abort),0);
        let mut guard = runner.timeline_scope(crate::engine::timeline_authority::Authority::Transition("feed".into()));
        for suffix in crate::schema::timeline::OWNED_SUFFIXES {
            let maintain = Maintain { own_keys: None, row_key: None, parent_key: None, aliases: Default::default(), target: format!("feed{suffix}"), source: "follows".into(), by: vec!["readerId".into()],
                kind: MaintainKind::Count, filter: None, computed: Default::default(), residency: Default::default(), readable: None, private: None };
            let result = guard.apply_aggregate(&maintain, vec![Value::Id("reader".into())], 1, None);
            assert_eq!(result.unwrap_err().code(), "E_TIMELINE_OWNED");
        }
    }
}
