//! Atomic adoption of the maintained-row address function in the evaluation
//! adapter. The marker and generation publish in the same writer transaction
//! as the target rebuild, so no writer can observe mixed legacy/digest ids.
use super::*;

pub(super) fn install(
    tx: &store::Tx<'_>,
    schema: &Schema,
    creating: bool,
    generation: u64,
) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    let current = tx.query(
        "SELECT maintained_identity_version FROM _backend WHERE singleton",
        &[],
    )?[0].get::<_, Option<&str>>(0).map(str::to_owned);
    if current.as_deref() == Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION) {
        return Ok(generation);
    }

    let aggregates: Vec<_> = schema.maintains.iter()
        .filter(|maintain| maintain.row_key.is_none())
        .cloned()
        .collect();
    if !creating && !aggregates.is_empty() {
        let mut runner = Runner::new(
            tx,
            schema,
            Context::system().at(crate::now_ms()),
            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
            tx.next_seq()?,
        );
        runner.event_free = true;
        runner.rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&aggregates, None, None)?;
        for maintain in &aggregates {
            runner.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
        }
        // The narrow maintained-column shape admitted by this adapter keeps
        // its private target out of the public rows but still shares the same
        // identity upgrade. Rebuild every target before publishing the marker,
        // then restore its authoritative value into each live parent.
        // @ref LLP 3000.007.001#3.11 — activation is rebuild, then mirror, before the generation barrier.
        for maintain in aggregates.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_some()) {
            runner.mirror_column_pass(maintain)?;
        }
    }

    let generation = if creating || aggregates.is_empty() {
        generation
    } else {
        generation.checked_add(1)
            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?
    };
    tx.execute(
        "UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=$1, generation=$2 WHERE singleton",
        &[&crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION, &store::signed(generation)?],
    )?;
    Ok(generation)
}

@@ -170,6 +170,21 @@ target stays opaque, preserving the existing dangling-reference contract.
 Removing the aggregate itself retires its derived target rows; a dormant
 reference to that retired target receives no map and keeps the ordinary
 restore refusal against acquiring a newly created parent lifetime.
+
+Persisted `sequence by` custody is part of the same identity migration even
+when no allocating row, source row, or aggregate target row survives. Adoption
+decodes canonical legacy counter ids with the predecessor aggregate's typed
+group definition, recursively settles any aggregate-reference components, and
+re-keys `_sequences(parent, id, value)` through the resulting target-specific
+map. If legacy and digest keys both exist, their maximum high-water value wins;
+the legacy key is removed and an exhausted counter remains exhausted. Counters
+for other parent tables and legacy strings that do not decode as a canonical

+normalized before the current identity marker publishes, so later
+reintroduction cannot revive legacy custody under that marker. Counter rewrites
+and their rollback share the adoption transaction with row-reference rewrites,
+target rebuilds, marker and generation.

+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+type LegacyIdentities = Vec<(String, Vec<(String, Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>)>)>;
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+type LegacyIdentityMap = BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>>>;
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    value: &Value,
+    definitions: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<crate::schema::ColumnType>>,
+    identities: &mut LegacyIdentityMap,
+) {
+    match (kind, value) {
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(old)) => {
+            let Some(kinds) = definitions.get(table) else { return };
+            if identities.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| ids.contains_key(old)) { return; }
+            let Some(values) = crate::json_codec::from_text::<Vec<Value>>(old).ok()
+                .filter(|values| values.len() == kinds.len()) else { return };
+            let key: Vec<_> = kinds.iter().cloned().zip(values).collect();
+            identities.entry(table.clone()).or_default().insert(old.clone(), key.clone());
+            for (kind, value) in &key {
+                collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(kind, value, definitions, identities);
+            }
+        }
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) =>
+            collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(inner, value, definitions, identities),
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
+            for value in values { collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(of, value, definitions, identities); },
+        _ => {}
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn insert_sequence_identity(
+    target: &str,
+    old: String,
+    key: Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>,
+    definitions: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<crate::schema::ColumnType>>,
+    identities: &mut LegacyIdentityMap,
+) {
+    if identities.get(target).is_some_and(|ids| ids.contains_key(&old)) { return; }
+    identities.entry(target.to_owned()).or_default().insert(old, key.clone());
+    for (kind, value) in &key {
+        collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(kind, value, definitions, identities);
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn settle_legacy_maintained_ids(
+    legacy: &LegacyIdentities,
+    base: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>, RuntimeError> {
+    let mut ids = base.clone();
+    let identity_count = legacy.iter().map(|(_, rows)| rows.len()).sum::<usize>();
+    for _ in 0..=identity_count.saturating_add(1) {
+        let mut next_ids = base.clone();
+        for (target, rows) in legacy {
+            let target_ids = next_ids.entry(target.clone()).or_default();
+            for (old, key) in rows {
+                let key: Vec<_> = key.iter().map(|(kind, value)| {
+                    let mut value = value.clone();
+                    rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &mut value, &ids);
+                    value
+                }).collect();
+                let next = maintained_id(&key);
+                if old != &next { target_ids.insert(old.clone(), next); }
+            }
+        }
+        if next_ids == ids { return Ok(next_ids); }
+        ids = next_ids;
+    }
+    Err(RuntimeError::Schema("legacy aggregate identity references form a cycle".into()))
+}

+            for row in rows {
+                let old = row.get::<_, &str>(0);
+                let value = row.get::<_, i64>(1);
+                let next = parent_ids.get(old).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| old.to_owned());
+                parent_rewritten = parent_rewritten.saturating_add(u64::from(next != old));
+                merged.entry(next).and_modify(|current| *current = (*current).max(value)).or_insert(value);
+            }
+            if parent_rewritten == 0 || merged.is_empty() { continue; }
+            self.execute("DELETE FROM _sequences WHERE parent=$1", &[parent])?;
+            for (id, value) in merged {
+                self.execute("INSERT INTO _sequences(parent,id,value) VALUES ($1,$2,$3)", &[parent, &id, &value])?;
+            }
+            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(parent_rewritten);
+        }
+        Ok(rewritten)
+    }

+    fn sequence_ids(&self, parent: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, RuntimeError> {
+        if !self.has_sequence_table()? { return Ok(Vec::new()); }
+        Ok(self.conn().prepare_cached("SELECT id FROM _sequences WHERE parent=?1 ORDER BY id")?
+            .query_map([parent], |row| row.get(0))?.collect::<Result<_, _>>()?)

+    fn rewrite_sequence_ids(&self, ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
+        if !self.has_sequence_table()? { return Ok(0); }
+        let mut rewritten = 0u64;
+        for (parent, parent_ids) in ids.iter().filter(|(_, ids)| !ids.is_empty()) {
+            let rows: Vec<(String, i64)> = self.conn().prepare_cached(
+                "SELECT id,value FROM _sequences WHERE parent=?1 ORDER BY id"
+            )?.query_map([parent], |row| Ok((row.get(0)?, row.get(1)?)))?
+                .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
+            let mut merged = BTreeMap::<String, i64>::new();
+            let mut parent_rewritten = 0u64;
+            for (old, value) in rows {
+                let next = parent_ids.get(&old).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| old.clone());
+                parent_rewritten = parent_rewritten.saturating_add(u64::from(next != old));
+                merged.entry(next).and_modify(|current| *current = (*current).max(value)).or_insert(value);
+            }
+            if parent_rewritten == 0 || merged.is_empty() { continue; }
+            self.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _sequences WHERE parent=?1", [parent])?;
+            let mut insert = self.conn().prepare_cached("INSERT INTO _sequences(parent,id,value) VALUES (?1,?2,?3)")?;
+            for (id, value) in merged { insert.execute(params![parent, id, value])?; }
+            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(parent_rewritten);
+        }
+        Ok(rewritten)
+    }

+#[test]
+fn identity_adoption_rekeys_sequence_history_without_reusing_deleted_ordinals() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table entries:\n  bucket: int\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .bucket\n  public\ntable sequenced:\n  total: totals\n  ordinal: sequence by total\n  unique total, ordinal\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("e7".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(7))])),
+        ("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("e9".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(9))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let digest7 = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let digest9 = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(9)]);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("gone".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7.clone()))])),
+        ("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("kept".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7.clone()))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    e.seed_delete("sequenced", "gone").unwrap();
+
+    let legacy7 = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let legacy9 = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(9)]);
+    let schema = e.schema().clone();
+    let target = schema.tables["totals"].clone();
+    let entries = schema.tables["entries"].clone();
+    let sequenced = schema.tables["sequenced"].clone();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    let mut row = tx.get("totals", &digest7).unwrap().unwrap();
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &row).unwrap();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row {
+        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy7.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &row, None).unwrap();
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &tx.get("totals", &digest9).unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
+    tx.delete("entries", &entries, &tx.get("entries", "e9").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
+    let old = tx.get("sequenced", "kept").unwrap().unwrap();
+    let mut next = old.clone();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
+        fields.insert("total".into(), Value::Id(legacy7.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("sequenced", &sequenced, &next, Some(&old)).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy7, 7).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &digest7, 4).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy9, crate::value::I53_MAX).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &digest9, 12).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("ordinary", &legacy7, 11).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy7).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy9).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest7).unwrap(), 7, "the deleted allocating row and lower destination counter cannot lower the high-water mark");
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest9).unwrap(), crate::value::I53_MAX);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("ordinary", &legacy7).unwrap(), 11, "translation is scoped by parent table and id");
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    let kept = e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap().pop().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(kept.field("total").unwrap(), &Value::Id(digest7.clone()));
+    assert_eq!(kept.field("ordinal").unwrap(), &Value::Int(2));
+
+    e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("next".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7))]))], 2).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap().into_iter().find(|row| row.field("id") == Ok(&Value::Id("next".into()))).unwrap().field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(8)));
+    let error = e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("full".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest9.clone()))]))], 2).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(error.refusal().code, "E_SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED");
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest9).unwrap(), crate::value::I53_MAX, "overflow refusal must not change the migrated counter");
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}

+#[test]
+fn removing_an_aggregate_normalizes_retained_sequence_custody_before_marking_the_store() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table entries:\n  bucket: int\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .bucket\n  public\ntable sequenced:\n  total: totals\n  ordinal: sequence by total\n  unique total, ordinal\n  public\n";
+    const WITHOUT_AGGREGATE: &str = "table entries:\n  bucket: int\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
+    e.seed_at([("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(3))]))], 0).unwrap();
+    let digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(3)]);
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(3)]);
+    let target = e.schema().tables["totals"].clone();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    let mut row = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().unwrap();
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &row).unwrap();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row {
+        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &row, None).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy, 5).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    let removed = compile(WITHOUT_AGGREGATE);
+    e.adopt_at(removed.schema, removed.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest).unwrap(), 5);
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().meta(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META).unwrap().as_deref(), Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION));
+
+    let restored = compile(SOURCE);
+    e.adopt_at(restored.schema, restored.programs, 2).unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("next".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest))]))], 3).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap()[0].field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(6)));
+}

+#[test]
+fn counter_only_aggregate_reference_chains_rekey_to_the_final_digest() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table aEntries:\n  key: int\n  public\nview aTotals: count aEntries by .key\n  public\ntable bEntries:\n  parent: aTotals\n  public\nview bTotals: count bEntries by .parent\n  public\ntable sequenced:\n  parent: bTotals\n  ordinal: sequence by parent\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
+    let legacy_a = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(5)]);
+    let legacy_b = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Id(legacy_a.clone())]);
+    let digest_a = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(5)]);
+    let digest_b = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(digest_a)]);
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("bTotals", &legacy_b, 9).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &legacy_b).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &digest_b).unwrap(), 9, "the absent referenced aggregate identity must settle before its dependent counter key");
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn sequence_identity_rekey_rolls_back_with_the_adoption_writer() {
+    let mut store = Store::memory().unwrap();
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy, 11).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.rewrite_sequence_ids(&BTreeMap::from([(
+        "totals".into(),
+        BTreeMap::from([(legacy.clone(), digest.clone())]),
+    )])).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest).unwrap(), 11);
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy).unwrap(), 11);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest).unwrap(), 0);
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}

+#[test]
+#[ignore = "requires frozen 0.4.28 binary via SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN"]
+fn a_0_4_28_store_preserves_counter_only_sequence_history() {
+    let baseline = PathBuf::from(
+        std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN")
+            .expect("set SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN to the frozen 0.4.28 snapback4 binary"),
+    );
+    assert!(baseline.is_file(), "SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN is not a file: {}", baseline.display());
+    let dir = Temp::new(SEQUENCE_SOURCE);
+    let legacy = snapback4_core::value::canonical_json(&[snapback4_core::Value::Int(7)]);
+    let run = |binary: &Path, operation: &str, args: serde_json::Value, now: &str| {
+        let output = Command::new(binary).current_dir(&dir.0)
+            .args(["run", operation, &args.to_string(), "--as", "alice", "--now", now, "--json"])
+            .output().unwrap();
+        assert!(output.status.success(), "{operation}: stdout={} stderr={}",
+            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout), String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr));
+        output
+    };
+    run(&baseline, "addEntry", serde_json::json!({"id":"entry-old","bucket":7}), "1");
+    for n in 1..=3 {
+        run(&baseline, "addOrder", serde_json::json!({"id":format!("order-{n}"),"total":legacy}), "1");
+    }
+    for n in 1..=3 {
+        run(&baseline, "removeOrder", serde_json::json!({"id":format!("order-{n}")}), "1");
+    }
+    run(&baseline, "removeEntry", serde_json::json!({"id":"entry-old"}), "1");
+
+    let store = dir.0.join(".snapback4/store.sqlite");
+    let conn = Connection::open(&store).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(conn.query_row("SELECT value FROM _sequences WHERE parent='totals' AND id=?1", [&legacy], |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0)).unwrap(), 3);
+    assert_eq!(conn.query_row("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM r JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=r.t WHERE c.name IN ('entries','totals','ordered')", [], |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0)).unwrap(), 0);
+    drop(conn);
+
+    let current = Path::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_snapback4"));
+    run(current, "addEntry", serde_json::json!({"id":"entry-new","bucket":7}), "2");
+    let digest = snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&[snapback4_core::Value::Int(7)]);

+        [], |row| row.get(0),

+    let row: snapback4_core::Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).unwrap();

+}

+/-! Persisted `sequence by` counters are server custody keyed by the parent
+table and physical parent id. They outlive allocating rows. This small model
+does not model SQL or the device protocol; it states the adoption invariant
+for one target-specific legacy-to-digest key. -/
+
+def sequenceHighWater (id : List Nat) (counters : List (List Nat × Nat)) : Nat :=
+  counters.foldl (fun high counter =>
+    if counter.1 = id then max high counter.2 else high) 0
+
+/-- If a partially upgraded store already has both keys, adoption merges them
+at their maximum. No child-row population participates in this value. -/
+def adoptedSequenceHighWater (legacy digest : List Nat)
+    (counters : List (List Nat × Nat)) : Nat :=
+  max (sequenceHighWater legacy counters) (sequenceHighWater digest counters)
+
+theorem adoptedSequence_preserves_legacy (legacy digest counters) :
+    sequenceHighWater legacy counters ≤ adoptedSequenceHighWater legacy digest counters :=
+  Nat.le_max_left _ _
+
+theorem adoptedSequence_preserves_digest (legacy digest counters) :
+    sequenceHighWater digest counters ≤ adoptedSequenceHighWater legacy digest counters :=
+  Nat.le_max_right _ _
+
+example : adoptedSequenceHighWater [91, 55, 93] (maintainedIdV1 [.int 7])
+    [([91, 55, 93], 9), (maintainedIdV1 [.int 7], 4)] = 9 := by decide
+

 Spellings are illustrative. None of the blocks below is a compiling example.
 
+### 3.0 Aggregate target identity and migration
+
+Every ordinary maintained aggregate row has one internal identity function:
+64 lowercase hexadecimal characters from SHA-256 over the domain
+`snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1` and the typed canonical group-key vector.
+The checker therefore admits the largest legal group key against a fixed-size
+identity, and synthetic check rows, incremental writes, point reads and
+adoption rebuilds all call the same function. The group key remains the public
+address; programs do not read or supply this internal id.
+
+The store metadata marker `maintained_id_version = sha256-v1` binds persisted
+aggregate targets to that function. Opening or adopting a store without the
+marker — including a 0.4.28 store whose ids were the unbounded canonical JSON
+of the group key — atomically clears and rebuilds every ordinary aggregate
+target from its source rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic
+generation. A failure rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation
+together. Adoption advice counts that rebuild even when schema/program bytes
+are unchanged. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
+`maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
+it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
+zero.
+
 ### 3.1 F1: maintained columns

+/// id. Domain separation makes future encodings explicit migrations.
+// @ref LLP 3000.007.003#30-aggregate-target-identity-and-migration — every aggregate writer, synthetic check row and adoption rebuild shares this bounded identity.
 pub fn maintained_id(key: &[Value]) -> String {
-    crate::value::canonical_json(&key)
+    crate::value::digest(&("snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1", key))
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn maintained_identity_is_fixed_size_and_domain_separated() {
+    let short = maintained_id(&[Value::String("x".into())]);
+    let long = maintained_id(&[Value::String("x".repeat(100_000))]);
+    assert_eq!(short.len(), 64);
+    assert_eq!(long.len(), 64);
+    assert_ne!(short, long);
+    assert_ne!(short, crate::value::digest(&[Value::String("x".into())]));
 }

+#[test]
+fn missing_identity_marker_rebuilds_a_principal_reference_and_max_text_group() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table parents:\n  public\ntable entries:\n  owner: principal\n  parent: parents\n  token: text <=64\n  amount: int\n  public\nview totals: sum entries of .amount by .owner, .parent, .token\n  public\n";

+    let mut e = Engine::new_at(Store::memory().unwrap(), initial.schema, initial.programs, 0).unwrap();
+    let owner = format!("user:{}", "o".repeat(59));
+    let parent = "p".repeat(64);
+    let token = "t".repeat(64);
+    assert_eq!((owner.len(), parent.len(), token.len()), (64, 64, 64));
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("parents".into(), object([("id", Value::Id(parent.clone()))])),
+        ("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("owner", Value::Id(owner.clone())),
+            ("parent", Value::Id(parent.clone())), ("token", Value::String(token.clone())), ("amount", Value::Int(7))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let expected = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(owner), Value::Id(parent), Value::String(token)]);
+    let before = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(before.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected.clone()));
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(7));
+    assert_eq!(expected.len(), 64);
+
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    assert_eq!(preview(&mut e, &next.schema).aggregate_rows, 1);
+    let generation = e.generation();
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    assert!(e.generation() > generation);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().meta(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META).unwrap().as_deref(), Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION));
+    let after = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(after.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected));

+#[test]
+fn aggregate_identity_capability_upgrades_legacy_wire_and_fences_old_devices() {
+    let schema = compile("table entries:\n  group: text <=64\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .group\n  public\n");
+    assert!(schema.required_capabilities().contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"));
+
+    // A pre-migration stored schema may already have a carrier for unrelated
+    // capabilities. Decode it once, then stamp the digest identity capability
+    // on every newly published schema/projection.
+    let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&schema).unwrap();
+    for table in legacy["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
+        for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
+            if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
+                names.retain(|value| value != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    let upgraded: Schema = serde_json::from_value(legacy).unwrap();
+    let encoded = serde_json::to_string(&upgraded).unwrap();
+    assert!(encoded.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"));
+
+    let required = snapback4_core::device_protocol::compatibility(&upgraded.public_projection());
+    let mut old = snapback4_core::device_protocol::DeviceEngine::current();
+    old.version = "0.4.28".into();
+    old.capabilities.retain(|capability| capability != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+    let refusal = snapback4_core::device_protocol::check(Some(&old), &required).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_DEVICE_VERSION");
+    assert!(refusal.message.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"), "{refusal:?}");
+}

+  parent: parents on delete cascade
+  public 'cascadeChildren'

+#[test]
+fn authoritative_memory_sweeps_resume_and_wrap_past_restricted_roots() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+table cascadeKids:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'cascade kids'
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+table blockers:
+  root: roots
+  public 'blockers'
+"#;
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let mut store = snapback4_device::memory::MemoryStore::new();
+    store.activate_server_at(bound.schema, 0).unwrap();
+    store.seed_server_at([
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("a-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("b-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("c-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("z-free")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("cz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("nz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("ba")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("bb")), ("root", id("b-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("bc")), ("root", id("c-blocked"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let wrapped_removed: u64 = (0..4).map(|_| store.sweep_server_at(10, 1).unwrap()).sum();
+    assert_eq!(wrapped_removed, 1, "continuation reaches the free root within one bounded turn per due root");
+    assert!(store.raw_rows("cascadeKids").is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(store.raw_rows("nullableKids")[0].field("root").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Null);
+
+    // The cursor is after z. A lower new key is found after the scan wraps;
+    // each restricted root still consumes one bounded visit.
+    store.seed_server_at([("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", id("aa-free")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10)),
+    ]))], 0).unwrap();
+    let wrapped_removed: u64 = (0..4).map(|_| store.sweep_server_at(10, 1).unwrap()).sum();
+    assert_eq!(wrapped_removed, 1, "a wrapped scan reaches the new lower key within one bounded turn per due root");
+    assert!(!store.raw_rows("roots").iter().any(|row| row.field("id").unwrap() == &id("aa-free")));
+}

+//! Expiry is a physical delete trigger for referential actions (LLP 3000.039
+//! §3). These cases cover scheduled cleanup, commit-end retirement and
+//! same-id replacement of an expired row against the real engine.
+use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, WriteState, value::object};
+use std::collections::BTreeMap;
+
+fn id(value: &str) -> Value { Value::Id(value.into()) }
+
+fn engine(source: &str) -> Engine {
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap()
+}
+
+const SWEEP: &str = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+  sync public
+table cascadeKids:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'cascade kids'
+  sync public
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+  sync public
+table blockers:
+  root: roots
+  public 'blockers'
+  sync public
+"#;
+
+#[test]
+fn sweep_applies_every_action_and_advances_past_a_restricted_root() {
+    let mut e = engine(SWEEP);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("a-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("b-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("c-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("z-free")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("ca")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("cz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("nz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("ba")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("bb")), ("root", id("b-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("bc")), ("root", id("c-blocked"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+
+    for expected in [0, 0, 0, 1] {
+        assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 1).unwrap(), expected, "a one-row sweep must advance its physical scan position");
+    }
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().iter().map(|r| r.field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["a-blocked", "b-blocked", "c-blocked"]);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().iter().map(|r| r.field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["ca"]);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+
+    for blocker in ["ba", "bb", "bc"] { e.seed_delete("blockers", blocker).unwrap(); }
+    assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 10).unwrap(), 3);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn a_late_cascade_refusal_rolls_back_earlier_set_null_writes() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 1 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+table children:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 1 by root
+  public 'children'
+table grandchildren:
+  child: children
+  read through .child
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("p")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("n")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+        ("children".into(), object([("id", id("c")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+        ("grandchildren".into(), object([("id", id("g")), ("child", id("c"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+
+    let error = e.sweep_expired(10, 10).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", "{error:?}");
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &id("p"), "the prior set-null write rolled back");
+    for table in ["roots", "children", "grandchildren"] {
+        assert_eq!(e.store().rows(table).unwrap().len(), 1, "{table}");
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn commit_retirement_and_expired_same_id_replacement_apply_actions() {
+    let source = format!(r#"{SWEEP}
+mutation bornExpired():
+  insert roots {{id: 'born', expiresAt: now}}
+  insert cascadeKids {{id: 'born-c', root: 'born'}}
+  insert nullableKids {{id: 'born-n', root: 'born'}}
+  return null
+mutation bornRestricted():
+  insert roots {{id: 'blocked', expiresAt: now}}
+  insert blockers {{id: 'blocked-b', root: 'blocked'}}
+  return null
+mutation replaceExpired():
+  insert roots {{id: 'old', expiresAt: null}}
+  return null
+"#);
+    let mut e = engine(&source);
+    let sent = e.mutate("bornExpired", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(sent.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", sent.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+
+    let refused = e.mutate("bornRestricted", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(refused.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == "E_REFERENCED"), "{:?}", refused.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty(), "the refused birth and its blocker roll back together");
+    assert!(e.store().rows("blockers").unwrap().is_empty());
+
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("old")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(1))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("old-c")), ("root", id("old"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let replaced = e.mutate("replaceExpired", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(replaced.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", replaced.state);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap()[0].field("expiresAt").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty(), "same-id cleanup cannot orphan the expired predecessor's child");
+}
diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..c6754a981f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,175 @@
+//! A store written by the frozen 0.4.28 binary adopts digest-addressed
+//! aggregate rows before the current engine serves it.
+use rusqlite::Connection;
+use std::{
+    fs,
+    path::{Path, PathBuf},
+    process::Command,
+};
+
+const SOURCE: &str = r#"use personas alice
+table entries:
+  group: text <=256
+  amount: int
+  insert <- allow
+  public
+view totals: sum entries of .amount by .group
+  public
+mutation add(group: text <=256, amount: int):
+  insert entries {group, amount}
+query total(group: text <=256):
+  return totals[group]
+"#;
+
+struct Temp(PathBuf);
+impl Temp {
+    fn new() -> Self {
+        let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
+            "snapback4-maintained-id-{}-{}",
+            std::process::id(),
+            std::time::SystemTime::now()
+                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
+                .unwrap()
+                .as_nanos()
+        ));
+        fs::create_dir_all(path.join("snapback")).unwrap();
+        fs::write(path.join("snapback/schema.q"), SOURCE).unwrap();
+        Self(path)
+    }
+}
+impl Drop for Temp {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
+    }
+}
+
+fn aggregate_id(store: &Path) -> String {
+    Connection::open(store)
+        .unwrap()
+        .query_row(
+            "SELECT r.id FROM r JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=r.t WHERE c.name='totals'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+}
+
+#[test]
+#[ignore = "requires frozen 0.4.28 binary via SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN"]
+fn a_0_4_28_store_rebuilds_legacy_aggregate_ids_and_fences_old_devices() {
+    let baseline = PathBuf::from(
+        std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN")
+            .expect("set SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN to the frozen 0.4.28 snapback4 binary"),
+    );
+    assert!(
+        baseline.is_file(),
+        "SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN is not a file: {}",
+        baseline.display()
+    );
+    let version = Command::new(&baseline).arg("--version").output().unwrap();
+    assert!(version.status.success());
+    assert!(
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&version.stdout).contains("0.4.28"),
+        "unexpected baseline: {:?}",
+        version
+    );
+
+    let dir = Temp::new();
+    let group = "x".repeat(200);
+    let args = serde_json::json!({"group": group, "amount": 7}).to_string();
+    let written = Command::new(&baseline)
+        .current_dir(&dir.0)
+        .args(["run", "add", &args, "--as", "alice", "--now", "1", "--json"])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        written.status.success(),
+        "{}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&written.stderr)
+    );
+    let store = dir.0.join(".snapback4/store.sqlite");
+    let legacy = aggregate_id(&store);
+    assert!(
+        legacy.len() > snapback4_core::rows::MAX_ID_BYTES,
+        "the frozen binary must have written the oversized legacy address"
+    );
+    let before: u64 = Connection::open(&store)
+        .unwrap()
+        .query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='generation'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get::<_, String>(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+        .parse()
+        .unwrap();
+
+    let opened = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_snapback4"))
+        .current_dir(&dir.0)
+        .args([
+            "run",
+            "total",
+            &serde_json::json!({"group": group}).to_string(),
+            "--as",
+            "alice",
+            "--now",
+            "2",
+            "--json",
+        ])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        opened.status.success(),
+        "stdout={} stderr={}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&opened.stdout),
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&opened.stderr)
+    );
+    let answer: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&opened.stdout).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(answer["data"]["value"], 7, "{answer}");
+
+    let digest = aggregate_id(&store);
+    assert_eq!(digest.len(), 64);
+    assert_ne!(digest, legacy);
+    let conn = Connection::open(&store).unwrap();
+    let (after, marker): (u64, String) = (
+        conn.query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='generation'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get::<_, String>(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+        .parse()
+        .unwrap(),
+        conn.query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key=?1",
+            [snapback4_core::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META],
+            |row| row.get(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap(),
+    );
+    assert!(
+        after > before,
+        "identity adoption must publish a new device generation"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(marker, snapback4_core::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION);
+
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), SOURCE.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let required =
+        snapback4_core::device_protocol::compatibility(&bound.schema.public_projection());
+    assert!(
+        required
+            .capabilities
+            .contains(&"maintained-id-sha256-v1".to_owned())
+    );
+    let mut old = snapback4_core::device_protocol::DeviceEngine::current();
+    old.version = "0.4.28".into();
+    old.capabilities
+        .retain(|capability| capability != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+    let refusal = snapback4_core::device_protocol::check(Some(&old), &required).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_DEVICE_VERSION");
+    assert!(
+        refusal.message.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"),
+        "{refusal:?}"
+    );
+}

+#[test]
+fn aggregate_identity_generator_checks_bounded_digest_shape_outside_oracle_verdicts() {
+    // Maintained-view evaluation is outside the Lean oracle. Exercise its
+    // physical identity as an explicit generator invariant, so these cases
+    // cannot be counted as oracle passes merely because they are unsupported.
+    use snapback4_core::Value;
+    let mut rng = snapback4_difftest::generate::Rng::new(0x3000_0070_0030_0001);
+    let mut ids = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
+    for n in 0..256 {
+        let key = if n == 0 {
+            vec![]
+        } else {
+            let principal = format!("p{:063}", rng.next());
+            let reference = format!("r{:063}", rng.next());
+            let len = rng.pick(65) as usize;
+            let token = format!("{:016x}", rng.next()).repeat(4)[..len].to_owned();
+            vec![Value::Id(principal), Value::Id(reference), Value::String(token),
+                 Value::Int((rng.next() & ((1 << 53) - 1)) as i64)]
+        };
+        let id = snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&key);
+        assert_eq!(id.len(), 64, "seeded case {n}: {key:?}");
+        assert!(id.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_hexdigit() && !byte.is_ascii_uppercase()));
+        assert!(snapback4_core::value::identity_fits(&id));
+        assert_eq!(id, snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&key));
+        assert!(ids.insert(id), "unexpected digest collision in generated corpus");
+    }
+}

+#[test]
+fn generated_composite_aggregate_groups_keep_fixed_digest_identities() {
+    let source = r#"table parents:
+  insert <- allow
+  read <- allow
+table entries:
+  owner: principal
+  parent: parents
+  token: text <=64
+  amount: int
+  insert <- allow
+  read <- allow
+view totals: sum entries of .amount by .owner, .parent, .token
+  read <- allow
+mutation add(row: id, owner: principal, parent: parents, token: text <=64):
+  insert entries {id: row, owner, parent, token, amount: 1}
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    let principal = "p".repeat(64);
+    let parent = "r".repeat(64);
+    e.seed([("parents".into(), object([("id", Value::Id(parent.clone()))]))]).unwrap();
+    for n in 0..32 {
+        let token = format!("{n:02}{}", "x".repeat(62));
+        let result = e.mutate("add", None, Context::new(&principal, BTreeMap::from([
+            ("row".into(), Value::Id(format!("e{n}"))),
+            ("owner".into(), Value::Id(principal.clone())),
+            ("parent".into(), Value::Id(parent.clone())),
+            ("token".into(), Value::String(token)),
+        ]))).unwrap();
+        assert!(matches!(result.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{result:?}");
+    }
+    let rows = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(rows.len(), 32);
+    for row in rows {
+        let Value::Id(id) = row.field("id").unwrap() else { panic!("aggregate id") };
+        assert_eq!(id.len(), 64);
+        assert!(snapback4_core::value::identity_fits(id));
+        assert_eq!(id, &snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&[
+            row.field("owner").unwrap().clone(), row.field("parent").unwrap().clone(),
+            row.field("token").unwrap().clone(),
+        ]));
+    }
+}

diff --git a/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Maintained.lean b/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Maintained.lean
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..241876980a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Maintained.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+import Quarry.Store
+
+/-!
+# Maintained aggregate identity
+
+The executable engine uses SHA-256 over a domain-separated canonical group
+tuple. This independent model deliberately does not reproduce that
+cryptographic implementation. It models the properties the language and
+store protocols rely on: versioned domain separation, a 64-character
+lowercase-hex identity for every logical group (including the empty tuple),
+and adoption as one state transition that replaces every legacy physical
+identity while publishing the new version.
+-/
+
+namespace Quarry
+
+/-- The protocol domain whose change requires another store capability and
+migration. -/
+def maintainedIdDomainV1 : List Nat := cps "snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1"
+
+/-- A small independent digest abstraction. Its contents are intentionally
+not the engine's SHA-256; only its versioned input and fixed hex shape belong
+to this logical model. -/
+def maintainedIdV1 (key : Key) : List Nat :=
+  (List.range 64).map fun i =>
+    let nibble := (maintainedIdDomainV1.length + (encKey key).length + i) % 16
+    if nibble < 10 then 48 + nibble else 87 + nibble
+
+theorem maintainedIdV1_length (key : Key) : (maintainedIdV1 key).length = 64 := by
+  simp [maintainedIdV1]
+
+/-- The canonical tagged-id overhead is nine bytes and lowercase ASCII is one
+byte per character, so every maintained identity fits the 144-byte id bound. -/
+theorem maintainedIdV1_fits (key : Key) : 9 + (maintainedIdV1 key).length ≤ 144 := by
+  rw [maintainedIdV1_length]
+  omega
+
+def maintainedRowV1 (key : Key) (cols : List (String × Scalar)) : Row :=
+  { id := maintainedIdV1 key, cols }
+
+structure MaintainedState where
+  version : Nat
+  rows : List Row
+
+/-- Adoption rebuilds all reconstructible aggregate rows and publishes the
+identity version in the same pure state result. `old` is an input so the model
+states explicitly that legacy physical ids are never retained. -/
+def adoptMaintainedV1 (_old : MaintainedState)
+    (groups : List (Key × List (String × Scalar))) : MaintainedState :=
+  { version := 1, rows := groups.map fun group => maintainedRowV1 group.1 group.2 }
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_version (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).version = 1 := rfl
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_ids (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.id = groups.map fun group => maintainedIdV1 group.1 := by
+  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_values (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.cols = groups.map Prod.snd := by
+  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
+
+example : (maintainedIdV1 []).length = 64 := maintainedIdV1_length []
+example : (maintainedIdV1 [.id (List.replicate 64 97), .text (List.replicate 64 120)]).length = 64 :=
+  maintainedIdV1_length _
+
+end Quarry

diff --git a/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Store.lean b/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Store.lean
index 629bc9ed03..38c1275945 100644
--- a/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Store.lean
+++ b/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Store.lean
@@ -215,11 +215,31 @@ def opened (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
     | .int opens => opens <= now
     | _ => false
 
-/-- The physical store with future rows removed. Rule probes use this store too,
-so an unopened row cannot act as an authorization witness. -/
+/-- Whether a row remains before its table's upper read lifetime. Null has no
+upper bound; the checked schema guarantees that a non-null value is a time. -/
+-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#3-semantics — upper read lifetimes filter every logical read before physical cleanup.
+def unexpired (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
+  match td.expire with
+  | none => true
+  | some c => match r.get c with
+    | .null => true
+    | .int closes => now < closes
+    | _ => false
+
+def live (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool := opened td now r && unexpired td now r
+
+/-- Referential actions ignore expired child images but still govern a child
+whose lower read lifetime has not opened yet, matching the physical engine. -/
+def unexpiredStore (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store := fun t =>
+  match sch.table? t with
+  | some td => (s t).filter (unexpired td now)
+  | none => []
+

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/program/aggregate_facts.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/program/aggregate_facts.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..10002e01ee
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/program/aggregate_facts.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,166 @@
+//! Exact non-empty facts established by successful count guards.
+
+use super::*;
+use std::collections::BTreeSet;
+
+pub(super) const NONEMPTY: &str = "$aggregateNonempty";
+/// Capture marker for a local whose current value is an exact `count(domain)`
+/// observation. It lives on the result and every domain root: ordinary
+/// rebinding, a write, an authority edge, or a control-flow meet therefore
+/// destroys stale provenance without repurposing diagnostic `origins`.
+pub(super) const COUNT_CAPTURE: &str = "$aggregateCountCapture";
+
+impl Binder<'_> {
+    /// A non-empty observation survives evaluation of its guard only when the
+    /// complete condition is write-free. Unlike point facts, aggregate facts
+    /// deliberately admit filters and seeks because those are part of the
+    /// exact domain identity recorded below.
+    pub(super) fn aggregate_guard_safe(&self, value: &A) -> bool {
+        match value {
+            A::Name { .. } | A::Focal { .. } | A::Literal { .. } => true,
+            A::Array { items, .. } => items.iter().all(|item| self.aggregate_guard_safe(item)),
+            A::Object { fields, .. } => fields.iter().all(|field| field.value.as_ref().is_none_or(|value| self.aggregate_guard_safe(value))),
+            A::Unary { value, .. } | A::Assert { value, .. } | A::ShapeUse { base: value, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(value),
+            A::Binary { left, right, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(left) && self.aggregate_guard_safe(right),
+            A::Member { base, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(base),
+            A::Call { name, args, .. } => self.catalog.functions.get(name).is_none_or(|function|
+                self.pure_functions.get(&function.name) == Some(&true))
+                && args.iter().all(|arg| self.aggregate_guard_safe(arg)),
+            A::Read(read) | A::Exists { read, .. } | A::Created { read, .. } => {
+                read.computed.values().all(|value| self.aggregate_guard_safe(value))
+                    && read.keys.iter().all(|key| self.aggregate_guard_safe(&key.value))
+                    && read.seeks.iter().all(|seek| self.aggregate_guard_safe(&seek.value))
+                    && read.filter.as_deref().is_none_or(|filter| self.aggregate_guard_safe(filter))
+                    && read.matching.as_deref().is_none_or(|matching| self.aggregate_guard_safe(matching))
+                    && read.range.as_ref().and_then(|range| range.cursor.as_deref()).is_none_or(|cursor| self.aggregate_guard_safe(cursor))
+            }
+            A::Shape { base, fields, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(base)
+                && fields.iter().all(|field| match field {
+                    ShapeField::Field { value, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(value),
+                    ShapeField::Spread { .. } | ShapeField::NamedSpread { .. } | ShapeField::Bare { .. } => true,
+                }),
+            A::If { then, condition, otherwise, .. } => self.aggregate_guard_safe(then)
+                && self.aggregate_guard_safe(condition)
+                && self.aggregate_guard_safe(otherwise),
+            A::Merge(_) | A::Walk { .. } | A::Write { .. } => false,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Record only implications that follow from count's nonnegative range.
+    /// The common authored form is `require n > 0`, where `n` was bound from
+    /// `count(domain)`; direct count calls use the same identity.
+    // @ref LLP 3000.013.001#4-non-empty-domain-proof — the fact belongs to the exact domain roots and transaction state.
+    pub(super) fn record_aggregate_nonempty(&mut self, condition: &A, truth: bool) {
+        if !truth { return; }
+        let A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } = condition else { return };
+        let (candidate, threshold, op) = if let Some(n) = literal_int(right) {
+            (left.as_ref(), n, op.as_str())
+        } else if let Some(n) = literal_int(left) {
+            let reversed = match op.as_str() { "<" => ">", "<=" => ">=", ">" => "<", ">=" => "<=", other => other };
+            (right.as_ref(), n, reversed)
+        } else { return };
+        let proves_positive = match op {
+            ">" => threshold >= 0,
+            ">=" | "=" => threshold >= 1,
+            "!=" => threshold == 0,
+            _ => false,
+        };
+        if !proves_positive { return; }
+        let Some((key, roots)) = self.count_key(candidate) else { return };
+        for root in roots {
+            let Some(mut binding) = self.binding(&root).cloned() else { return };
+            binding.fields.insert(key.clone(), Ty::Bool);
+            self.scopes.last_mut().expect("a scope").insert(root, binding);
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn aggregate_nonempty(&self, read: &ReadExpr) -> bool {
+        self.aggregate_key(read).is_some_and(|(key, roots)| roots.iter().all(|root|
+            self.binding(root).is_some_and(|binding| binding.fields.get(&key) == Some(&Ty::Bool))))
+    }
+
+    /// Resolve count provenance before rebinding `name`: a count domain may
+    /// itself refer to the old value of that local. Such a self-dependent
+    /// capture cannot be represented by the post-assignment binding and is
+    /// therefore deliberately not narrowed.
+    pub(super) fn count_capture(&self, name: &str, value: &A) -> Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)> {
+        let A::Call { name: call, args, .. } = value else { return None };
+        if call != "count" || args.len() != 1 || self.catalog.functions.contains_key(call)
+            || !self.aggregate_guard_safe(value) { return None; }
+        let read = args.first().and_then(|arg| self.aggregate_domain(arg))?;
+        let (aggregate, roots) = self.aggregate_key(&read)?;
+        if roots.contains(name) { return None; }
+        let capture = vec![COUNT_CAPTURE.into(), aggregate[1].clone()];
+        Some((capture, roots))
+    }
+
+    /// Attach pre-resolved capture-time provenance after assigning `name`.
+    /// `origins` remains diagnostic history; this field fact is the reaching
+    /// definition proof used by a later `require name > 0`.
+    pub(super) fn record_count_capture(&mut self, name: &str, capture: Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)>) {
+        let Some((capture, mut owners)) = capture else { return };
+        owners.insert(name.to_owned());
+        for owner in owners {
+            let Some(mut binding) = self.binding(&owner).cloned() else { return };
+            binding.fields.insert(capture.clone(), Ty::Bool);
+            self.scopes.last_mut().expect("a scope").insert(owner, binding);
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn count_key(&self, value: &A) -> Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)> {
+        let (count_arg, captured_name) = match value {
+            A::Call { name, args, .. } if name == "count" && args.len() == 1
+                && !self.catalog.functions.contains_key(name) => args.first(),
+            A::Name { name, .. } => self.binding(name)?.origins.iter().rev().find_map(|(_, origin)| match origin {
+                A::Call { name, args, .. } if name == "count" && args.len() == 1
+                    && !self.catalog.functions.contains_key(name) => args.first(),
+                _ => None,
+            }),
+            _ => None,
+        }.map(|arg| (arg, match value { A::Name { name, .. } => Some(name.as_str()), _ => None }))?;
+        let result = self.aggregate_key(&self.aggregate_domain(count_arg)?)?;
+        if let Some(name) = captured_name {
+            let capture = vec![COUNT_CAPTURE.into(), result.0[1].clone()];
+            if self.binding(name)?.fields.get(&capture) != Some(&Ty::Bool)
+                || !result.1.iter().all(|root| self.binding(root)
+                    .is_some_and(|binding| binding.fields.get(&capture) == Some(&Ty::Bool)))
+            {
+                return None;
+            }
+        }
+        Some(result)
+    }
+
+    fn aggregate_key(&self, read: &ReadExpr) -> Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)> {
+        if read.range.is_some() || read.matching.is_some() { return None; }
+        let mut roots = BTreeSet::new();
+        let keys = read.keys.iter().map(|key| Some(format!("{:?}:{}", key.column,
+            self.aggregate_value(&key.value, &mut roots)?))).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?;
+        let seeks = read.seeks.iter().map(|seek| Some(format!("{}:{}:{}", seek.column, seek.op,
+            self.aggregate_value(&seek.value, &mut roots)?))).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?;
+        let filter = match read.filter.as_deref() {
+            Some(value) => Some(self.aggregate_value(value, &mut roots)?),
+            None => None,
+        };
+        if roots.is_empty() { roots.insert(pure_calls::CONSTANTS.into()); }
+        let identity = format!("{:?}:{:?}:{:?}:{keys:?}:{seeks:?}:{filter:?}", read.table, read.index, read.order_keys);
+        Some((vec![NONEMPTY.into(), identity], roots))
+    }
+
+    fn aggregate_value(&self, value: &A, roots: &mut BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<String> {
+        match value {
+            A::Focal { .. } => Some("focal".into()),
+            A::Member { base, name, .. } if matches!(base.as_ref(), A::Focal { .. }) => Some(format!("focal.{name}")),
+            A::Literal { .. } | A::Name { .. } | A::Member { .. } => self.stable_value(value, roots).map(|value| value.key()),
+            A::Unary { op, value, .. } => Some(format!("unary:{op}:{}", self.aggregate_value(value, roots)?)),
+            A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } => Some(format!("binary:{op}:{}:{}", self.aggregate_value(left, roots)?, self.aggregate_value(right, roots)?)),
+            A::Call { name, args, .. } => {
+                let function = self.catalog.functions.get(name)?;
+                if self.pure_functions.get(&function.name) != Some(&true) { return None; }
+                Some(format!("call:{name}:{:?}", args.iter().map(|arg| self.aggregate_value(arg, roots)).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?))
+            }
+            A::Array { items, .. } => Some(format!("array:{:?}", items.iter().map(|item| self.aggregate_value(item, roots)).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?)),
+            _ => None,
+        }
+    }
+}

@@ -462,6 +464,14 @@ impl Binder<'_> {
 
     /// After `require x != null` or inside `if x != null:`, `x` is present.
     pub(super) fn narrow(&mut self, condition: &A, then_branch: bool) {
+        // Aggregate facts may describe filtered domains, so they have a
+        // slightly wider write-free admission check than point facts. Record
+        // them once for the whole, already-evaluated condition: recursively
+        // recording a safe left operand would be stale when a later operand
+        // calls a writeful helper.
+        if self.aggregate_guard_safe(condition) {
+            self.record_aggregate_nonempty(condition, then_branch);
+        }
         self.narrow_inner(condition, then_branch, self.point_guard_safe(condition));
     }

+#[test]
+fn ungrouped_view_is_a_scalar_with_one_hidden_physical_group() {
+    let bound = compile(r#"view total: count posts
+  read <- allow
+  online only
+query totalPosts():
+  return total
+"#);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    assert_eq!(bound.programs[0].result, snapback4_lang::types::Ty::Int);
+    let maintain = &bound.schema.maintains[0];
+    assert!(maintain.by.is_empty());
+    let target = &bound.schema.tables["total"];
+    assert_eq!(target.columns.get("$global"), Some(&snapback4_core::schema::ColumnType::Bool));
+    assert_eq!(target.indexes["byGroup"].columns(), ["$global"]);
+    let encoded = serde_json::to_value(&bound.programs[0].program).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(encoded["body"][0]["return"]["get"]["index"], "byGroup");
+    assert_eq!(encoded["body"][0]["return"]["get"]["key"], serde_json::json!([true]));
+}
+
 #[test]
 fn maintain_refusals_point_to_the_expression_and_offer_a_rewrite() {
     for head in [
diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/wave12_semantics.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/wave12_semantics.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..a589ba9349
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/wave12_semantics.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,381 @@
+use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, WriteState};
+use snapback4_lang::{compile, types::Ty};
+use std::collections::BTreeMap;
+
+fn checked(source: &str) -> snapback4_lang::Bound {
+    let bound = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    bound
+}
+
+fn engine(source: &str) -> Engine {
+    let bound = checked(source);
+    Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|program| program.program)).unwrap()
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn global_count_is_zero_then_tracks_inserts_and_deletes() {
+    let source = r#"
+table entries:
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  delete <- allow
+  online only
+table moderators:
+  principal: principal
+  unique principal
+  read <- .principal = viewer
+  online only
+view total: count entries
+  read <- allow
+  online only
+view privateTotal: count entries
+  read <- exists moderators[viewer]
+  online only
+mutation add(id: id):
+  return insert entries { id }
+mutation remove(id: entries):
+  delete entries[id]
+  return null
+query totalEntries():
+  return total
+query privateEntries():
+  return privateTotal
+"#;
+    let bound = checked(source);
+    let generated = snapback4_lang::emit::typescript(&bound);
+    let native = snapback4_lang::emit::rust::rust(&bound);
+    assert!(!generated.contains("$global") && !native.contains("$global"),
+        "the physical discriminator leaked into generated application types");
+    for expression in ["total first 1 by .id", "total[true]"] {
+        let bound = compile(&[("bad.q".into(), format!("{source}\nquery bad(c: cursor ?):\n  return {expression}\n"))]);
+        assert!(bound.diagnostics.iter().any(|diagnostic| diagnostic.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE"
+            && diagnostic.message.contains("global maintained scalar")), "{expression}: {:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    }
+    let mut engine = engine(source);
+    let query = |engine: &mut Engine| engine.query("totalEntries", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap().data;
+    let private = |engine: &mut Engine, viewer| engine.query("privateEntries", Context::new(viewer, BTreeMap::new())).unwrap().data;
+    assert_eq!(query(&mut engine), Value::Int(0));
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "alice"), Value::Null, "an unauthorized empty global stays hidden");
+    engine.seed([("moderators".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", Value::Id("mod".into())), ("principal", Value::Id("alice".into())),
+    ]))]).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "alice"), Value::Int(0), "authorized absence is the count identity");
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Null, "a hidden absence is not zero");
+    for id in ["a", "b"] {
+        let outcome = engine.mutate("add", None, Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("id".into(), Value::Id(id.into()))]))).unwrap();
+        assert!(matches!(outcome.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{outcome:?}");
+    }
+    assert_eq!(query(&mut engine), Value::Int(2));
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "alice"), Value::Int(2));
+    assert_eq!(private(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Null, "a hidden stored scalar remains null");
+    engine.mutate("remove", None, Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("id".into(), Value::Id("a".into()))]))).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(query(&mut engine), Value::Int(1));
+    engine.mutate("remove", None, Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("id".into(), Value::Id("b".into()))]))).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(query(&mut engine), Value::Int(0));
+    assert!(engine.store().rows("total").unwrap().is_empty(), "zero deletes the physical aggregate row");
+    assert!(engine.store().rows("privateTotal").unwrap().is_empty(), "private zero also has no physical row");
+}

+#[test]
+fn matching_count_guard_narrows_only_the_same_required_projection_until_a_write() {
+    let schema = r#"
+table entries:
+  owner: principal
+  score: int
+  optionalScore: int ?
+  by byOwner: owner, id
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  delete <- allow
+  online only
+"#;
+    let sound = checked(&format!(r#"{schema}
+query stats(owner: principal):
+  n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)
+  require n > 0 else EMPTY
+  return {{ low: min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score), high: max(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score), total: sum(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) }}
+query filtered(owner: principal):
+  require count(entries where .owner = owner) > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(entries where .owner = owner, .score) + 1
+mutation freshAfterWrite(owner: principal, victim: entries):
+  delete entries[victim]
+  n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)
+  require n > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1
+"#));
+    let result = &sound.programs.iter().find(|program| program.program.name == "stats").unwrap().result;
+    assert!(matches!(result, Ty::Object(fields) if fields.values().all(|ty| ty == &Ty::Int)), "{result:?}");
+    assert_eq!(sound.programs.iter().find(|program| program.program.name == "filtered").unwrap().result, Ty::Int);
+
+    for (name, body) in [
+        ("different", "n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  return min(entries['other'] by byOwner, .score) + 1"),
+        ("optional", "n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .optionalScore) + 1"),
+        ("written", "n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  delete entries[victim]\n  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1"),
+        ("stale_binding", "n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)\n  delete entries[victim]\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1"),
+        ("rebound", "n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)\n  n = 1\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1"),
+        ("joined", "n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)\n  if flag:\n    n = 1\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1"),
+        ("root_rebound", "who = owner\n  n = count(entries[who] by byOwner)\n  who = next\n  require n > 0 else EMPTY\n  return min(entries[who] by byOwner, .score) + 1"),
+    ] {
+        let args = match name {
+            "written" | "stale_binding" => "owner: principal, victim: entries",
+            "joined" => "owner: principal, flag: bool",
+            "root_rebound" => "owner: principal, next: principal",
+            _ => "owner: principal",
+        };
+        let kind = if matches!(name, "written" | "stale_binding") { "mutation" } else { "query" };
+        let bound = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!("{schema}{kind} {name}({args}):\n  {body}\n"))]);
+        assert!(bound.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")), "{name}: {:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    }
+
+    let helper = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!(r#"{schema}
+fn remove(victim: entries):
+  delete entries[victim]
+  return true
+mutation staleHelper(owner: principal, victim: entries):
+  n = count(entries[owner] by byOwner)
+  removed = remove(victim)
+  require n > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1
+"#))]);
+    assert!(helper.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")), "{:#?}", helper.diagnostics);
+
+    let authority = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!(r#"{schema}
+job staleAuthority():
+  for row in entries:
+    n = count(entries[row.owner] by byOwner)
+    as row.owner:
+      require n > 0 else EMPTY
+      narrowed = min(entries[row.owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1
+"#))]);
+    assert!(authority.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")), "{:#?}", authority.diagnostics);
+
+    let self_dependent = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), r#"
+table buckets:
+  bucket: int
+  score: int
+  by byBucket: bucket, id
+  public
+  online only
+query staleSelfDependent():
+  bucket = 1
+  bucket = count(buckets[bucket] by byBucket)
+  require bucket > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(buckets[bucket] by byBucket, .score) + 1
+"#.into())]);
+    assert!(self_dependent.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")),
+        "a count result must not inherit the old value's domain provenance: {:#?}", self_dependent.diagnostics);
+
+    let pure_domain = checked(&format!(r#"{schema}
+fn sameOwner(owner: principal):
+  return owner
+query pureDomain(owner: principal):
+  n = count(entries[sameOwner(owner)] by byOwner)
+  require n > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(entries[sameOwner(owner)] by byOwner, .score) + 1
+"#));
+    assert_eq!(pure_domain.programs.iter().find(|program| program.program.name == "pureDomain").unwrap().result, Ty::Int);
+
+    let impure_domain = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!(r#"{schema}
+fn changingOwner(owner: principal, victim: entries):
+  delete entries[victim]
+  return owner
+mutation staleDomain(owner: principal, victim: entries):
+  n = count(entries[changingOwner(owner, victim)] by byOwner)
+  require n > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(entries[changingOwner(owner, victim)] by byOwner, .score) + 1
+"#))]);
+    assert!(impure_domain.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")),
+        "writeful domains must never be replayed as aggregate proof: {:#?}", impure_domain.diagnostics);
+
+    let shadowed = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!(r#"{schema}
+fn count(owner: principal):
+  return 1
+query shadowedCount(owner: principal):
+  n = count(owner)
+  require n > 0 else EMPTY
+  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1
+"#))]);
+    assert!(shadowed.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")),
+        "a user helper named count must not create builtin provenance: {:#?}", shadowed.diagnostics);
+}

+#[test]
+fn matching_role_guard_narrows_only_the_authorized_keyed_total() {
+    let source = r#"
+table entries:
+  owner: principal
+  public
+  online only
+table staff:
+  principal: principal
+  role: enum('finance')
+  unique principal, role
+  read <- .principal = viewer
+  delete <- .principal = viewer
+  online only
+view totals: count entries by .owner
+  read <- exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance']
+  online only
+query raw(owner: principal):
+  return totals[owner]
+query guarded(owner: principal):
+  require exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance'] else NOT_FINANCE
+  return totals[owner] + 1
+"#;
+    let bound = checked(source);
+    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|program| program.program.name == "raw").unwrap().result, Ty::Int.optional());
+    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|program| program.program.name == "guarded").unwrap().result, Ty::Int);
+    let mut engine = Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|program| program.program)).unwrap();
+    engine.seed([("entries".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", Value::Id("one".into())), ("owner", Value::Id("bob".into())),
+    ]))]).unwrap();
+    let raw = |engine: &mut Engine, owner: &str| engine.query("raw", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
+        ("owner".into(), Value::Id(owner.into())),
+    ]))).unwrap().data;
+    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Null, "a hidden stored total is not disclosed");
+    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "nobody"), Value::Null, "a hidden miss is indistinguishable from a hidden hit");
+    engine.seed([("staff".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", Value::Id("finance".into())), ("principal", Value::Id("alice".into())),
+        ("role", Value::String("finance".into())),
+    ]))]).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Int(1));
+    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "nobody"), Value::Int(0), "an authorized keyed miss has the count identity");
+    assert_eq!(engine.query("guarded", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
+        ("owner".into(), Value::Id("nobody".into())),
+    ]))).unwrap().data, Value::Int(1));
+
+    let stale = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!(r#"{source}
+mutation stale(owner: principal, grant: staff):
+  require exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance'] else NOT_FINANCE
+  delete staff[grant]
+  return totals[owner] + 1
+"#))]);
+    assert!(stale.diagnostics.iter().any(|diagnostic| diagnostic.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE"
+        && diagnostic.message.contains("int ?")), "a write must invalidate the role proof: {:#?}", stale.diagnostics);
+}

+#[test]
+fn email_format_is_one_shared_ascii_contract() {
+    let source = r#"
+table contacts:
+  email: text 3..254 format email
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  online only
+query echo(email: text 3..254 format email):

+"#;
+    let mut engine = engine(source);
+    for email in ["a@example.com", "first.last+tag@sub.example", "x@localhost"] {
+        let result = engine.query("echo", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("email".into(), Value::String(email.into()))]))).unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(result.data, Value::String(email.into()));

+    for email in ["a..b@example.com", ".a@example.com", "a@-example.com", "a@example..com", "a@пример.рф", "a@@example.com"] {
+        let error = engine.query("echo", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("email".into(), Value::String(email.into()))]))).unwrap_err();
+        assert_eq!(error.code, "E_INPUT", "{email}: {error:?}");
+    }
+}
