//! Referential actions: what deleting a referenced row does to the rows that
//! name it (`on delete restrict | cascade | set null`).
// @ref LLP 3000.039#2 — every reference between ordinary durable tables carries one action; restrict is the default.
use super::*;
pub use reservations::Price;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub enum OnDelete {
    Restrict,
    Cascade,
    SetNull,
    /// The referencing row stays and names a deleted row (the pre-0.5 meaning),
    /// declared on purpose: history, audit trails, contributions that outlive
    /// their target.
    Keep,
}

impl OnDelete {
    pub fn words(self) -> &'static str {
        match self { Self::Restrict => "on delete restrict", Self::Cascade => "on delete cascade", Self::SetNull => "on delete set null", Self::Keep => "on delete keep" }
    }
    /// The actions that write the children, bounded by a cap on the reference.
    pub fn writes(self) -> bool { matches!(self, Self::Cascade | Self::SetNull) }
    /// The actions a delete must consult (every one but `keep`).
    pub fn acts(self) -> bool { self != Self::Keep }
}

/// One action-carrying reference `child.column -> parent`.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Referencing<'a> {
    pub child: &'a str,
    pub table: &'a Table,
    pub column: &'a str,
    pub action: OnDelete,
}

/// The prefix of the reference index a live child of `parent` is found under.
pub const REFERENCE_INDEX_PREFIX: &str = "$reference:";
pub fn reference_index_name(column: &str) -> String { format!("{REFERENCE_INDEX_PREFIX}{column}") }

/// Heap a closure keeps per reached row: its table and id (an id is at most
/// 144 canonical bytes) and the set and queue entries holding them.
pub const CLOSURE_IDENTITY_BYTES: u64 = 384;
/// Child rows a cascade or set-null walk reads per seek (LLP 3000.039 §5.1).
pub const REFERENCE_PAGE: usize = 4;

impl Schema {
    /// Whether rows of `name` take part in referential actions, as child or
    /// parent: an ordinary durable application table. Ephemeral rows, engine
    /// derivations and receipt/timeline bookkeeping keep their own lifetimes.
    pub fn actionable(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        let Some(table) = self.table(name) else { return false };
        table.ephemeral.is_none() && self.maintain_for(name).is_none() && self.private_owner(name).is_none()
            && !self.is_recount_work(name) && !self.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.owns(name))
            && !self.receipts.iter().any(|f| [&f.scope, &f.members, &f.runs].iter().any(|t| t.as_str() == name))
    }

    /// Every reference into `parent` a delete consults (all but `keep`), in
    /// (child, column) order.
    pub fn referencing<'a>(&'a self, parent: &str) -> Vec<Referencing<'a>> {
        // A plain loop into a vector: iterator adapters monomorphize per call site on the web device.
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for (child, table) in &self.tables {
            for (column, action) in &table.on_delete {
                if action.acts() && matches!(table.columns.get(column).map(ColumnType::required), Some(ColumnType::Ref { table: target }) if target == parent) {
                    out.push(Referencing { child, table, column, action: *action });
                }
            }
        }
        out
    }

    /// A delete of a `parent` row consults its referencing rows, so it needs
    /// read authority on that row (LLP 3000.039 §3 step 1).
    pub fn is_referenced(&self, parent: &str) -> bool { !self.referencing(parent).is_empty() }

    /// The index a reference is probed through: its column first, then the
    /// child's deadline column when the child can expire, so one seek skips an
    /// expired backlog. A `read through` reference uses its child index.
    pub fn reference_index(&self, child: &str, column: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        let table = self.table(child)?;
        if table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == column) {
            return table.indexes.contains_key(through::CHILDREN).then_some(through::CHILDREN);
        }
        // The effective deadline: a read-through child's `$deadline`, else `expire at`.
        let deadline = table.expiry_column();
        table.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| {
            let columns = index.columns();
            index.is_plain() && columns.first().map(String::as_str) == Some(column)
                && deadline.is_none_or(|deadline| columns.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some(deadline))
        }).map(|(name, _)| name.as_str())
    }

    /// The cap bounding a reference's children: `cap N by <column>` exactly,
    /// or one when the reference itself is a plain unique key. A nullable
    /// reference may have many nulls, but a parent delete probes one non-null
    /// parent id, whose unique group still has at most one row.
    pub fn reference_cap(&self, child: &str, column: &str) -> Option<u32> {
        let table = self.table(child)?;
        let declared = table.constraints.iter().find_map(|c| match c {
            Constraint::Cap { by, max } if by.len() == 1 && by[0] == column => Some(*max),
            _ => None,
        });
        let unique = table.indexes.values().any(|index| index.unique && index.is_plain() && index.columns() == [column]).then_some(1);
        declared.into_iter().chain(unique).min()
    }

    /// Whether `cap` on `table` skips a group whose reference is null: only a
    /// `set null` reference's own cap does (a null reference has no parent).
    pub fn cap_skips_null(&self, table: &Table, by: &[String], group: &[Value]) -> bool {
        by.iter().zip(group).any(|(column, value)| *value == Value::Null && table.on_delete.get(column) == Some(&OnDelete::SetNull))
    }

    /// The tables a delete of a `parent` row may write through its writing
    /// actions, and the tables its actions read. A function of the schema, so
    /// a commit's touched set never says which of them a delete reached.
    pub fn action_tables(&self, parent: &str) -> ActionTables {
        let mut out = ActionTables::default();
        let mut queue = vec![parent.to_owned()];
        let mut visited = BTreeSet::new();
        while let Some(table) = queue.pop() {
            if !visited.insert(table.clone()) { continue; }
            for r in self.referencing(&table) {
                out.read.insert(r.child.to_owned());
                if r.action.writes() { out.written.insert(r.child.to_owned()); }
                if r.action == OnDelete::Cascade { queue.push(r.child.to_owned()); }
            }
        }
        // What a write of each of those tables writes in turn: the derived
        // destinations `row_changed` names (aggregate targets, maintained-column
        // owners, row-keyed views).
        let derived: Vec<String> = self.maintains.iter().filter(|m| out.written.contains(&m.source) || m.row_key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k| out.written.contains(&k.table)))
            .flat_map(|m| [Some(m.target.clone()), m.private.as_ref().map(|owner| owner.table.clone())]).flatten().collect();
        out.written.extend(derived);
        out.written.retain(|name| self.visible(name));
        // Private derivations disappear from the device's projection; their
        // event envelope is exported with each direct source's write price.
        let sources: Vec<String> = out.written.iter().cloned().collect();
        for source in sources {
            if let Some(events) = self.write_reservation(&source).and_then(|plan| plan.action_events) { out.written.extend(events.tables); }
        }
        out
    }

    /// The order a delete's closure is removed in: a row before any table it
    /// must not outlive — its cascade parent, and its `read through` parent.
    /// A cycle through those edges has no valid order and is refused.
    pub fn deletion_precedes(&self, child: &str, parent: &str) -> bool {
        self.table(child).is_some_and(|t| t.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|through| through.parent == parent))
            || self.referencing(parent).into_iter().any(|r| r.child == child && r.action == OnDelete::Cascade)
    }

    /// A table that reaches itself through cascade and `read through` edges.
    pub fn deletion_cycle(&self) -> Option<String> {
        fn visit<'a>(schema: &'a Schema, name: &'a str, path: &mut Vec<&'a str>, done: &mut BTreeSet<&'a str>) -> Option<String> {
            if path.contains(&name) { return Some(name.to_owned()); }
            if !done.insert(name) { return None; }
            path.push(name);
            for (child, _) in &schema.tables {
                if schema.deletion_precedes(child, name) && let Some(cycle) = visit(schema, child, path, done) { return Some(cycle); }
            }
            path.pop();
            None
        }
        let mut done = BTreeSet::new();
        self.tables.keys().find_map(|name| if self.tables[name].on_delete.values().any(|a| *a == OnDelete::Cascade) || self.is_referenced(name) {
            let mut path = Vec::new();
            visit(self, name, &mut path, &mut done)
        } else { None })
    }

    /// Whether `name` is a table a timeline orders the writes of.
    pub fn timeline_member(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.owns(name) || t.maps(name) || t.authors.first().is_some_and(|a| a == name))
    }

    /// The most rows of each table one delete of a `parent` row can reach
    /// through its cascades (its closure), the root included: each cascade
    /// edge multiplies by its cap, and edges into a table add up. `None` when
    /// the cascade graph from `parent` is cyclic or a cascade lacks its cap.
    pub fn closure_bounds(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Vec<(String, u64)>> {
        // Vectors, not maps: the web device pays for every new collection type.
        let mut reach: Vec<String> = vec![parent.to_owned()];
        let mut edges: Vec<(usize, usize, u64)> = Vec::new();
        let mut at = 0;
        while at < reach.len() {
            let table = reach[at].clone();
            for r in self.referencing(&table) {
                if r.action != OnDelete::Cascade { continue; }
                let cap = u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?);
                let child = reach.iter().position(|t| t == r.child).unwrap_or_else(|| { reach.push(r.child.to_owned()); reach.len() - 1 });
                edges.push((at, child, cap));
            }
            at += 1;
        }
        // Kahn's order over the reached cascade subgraph; a leftover table is a cycle.
        let mut indegree = vec![0_usize; reach.len()];
        for &(_, child, _) in &edges { indegree[child] += 1; }
        let mut bounds = vec![0_u64; reach.len()];
        bounds[0] = 1;
        let mut ready: Vec<usize> = (0..reach.len()).filter(|&t| indegree[t] == 0).collect();
        let mut done = 0;
        while let Some(table) = ready.pop() {
            done += 1;
            for &(from, child, cap) in edges.iter().filter(|(from, _, _)| *from == table) {
                bounds[child] = bounds[child].saturating_add(bounds[from].saturating_mul(cap));
                indegree[child] -= 1;
                if indegree[child] == 0 { ready.push(child); }
            }
        }
        (done == reach.len()).then(|| reach.into_iter().zip(bounds).collect())
    }

    /// The fixed charge a delete of a `parent` row reserves before it probes,
    /// cascades or clears any row, over every meter: the closure's rows and
    /// their identities, every restrict probe (one seek per closure row, plus
    /// the closure rows it skips), every set-null row, and one engine write of
    /// each, priced from the source-write plan the engine already exports. A
    /// function of the schema only — caps, the reference graph, each table's
    /// indexes and row size, and the exported plans — so a meter, an `E_BOUND`
    /// abort or the physical allowance never depends on how many (hidden) rows
    /// exist, and every host charges alike: a device's projection keeps every
    /// table that can carry an action and every exported price. `None` when the
    /// closure is unbounded (a cycle or a missing cap) or a written table has no
    /// fixed write price. Heap is the closure's identity scratch plus the largest
    /// single row's transient work, plus event images retained until commit.
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#5.1 — the reservation is schema-fixed; LLP 3000.015 §2's law for work shaped by hidden rows.
    pub fn delete_reservation(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Price> {
        let bounds = self.closure_bounds(parent)?;
        let mut price = [0_u64; 7];
        let mut heap = 0_u64;
        let mut identities = 0_u64;
        let mut gathered = 0_u64;
        let rows_of = |name: &str| bounds.iter().find(|(t, _)| t == name).map_or(0, |(_, n)| *n);
        for (table, n) in &bounds {
            let n = *n;
            if table != parent {
                // Fetched by the closure walk and again, current, before its delete.
                let unit = self.unit_write(table)?;
                heap = heap.max(unit[4]);
                add(&mut price, [unit[0], unit[1], unit[2] + 1, unit[3], 0, unit[5], unit[6]].map(|v| v.saturating_mul(n)));
                identities = identities.saturating_add(n);
                // Before any set-null write, each reached cascade row proves
                // that no physically retained read-through child lies outside
                // the closure. Each child table can skip every reached
                // identity from that table and then inspect one outside
                // witness. Execution performs
                // these probes under reference_prepaid, so their complete
                // schema bound belongs in this outer admission reservation.
                let through_children: Vec<_> = self.children(table).collect();
                let probes_per_row = through_children.iter()
                    .map(|(child, _, _)| rows_of(child).saturating_add(1))
                    .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
                let probes = n.saturating_mul(probes_per_row);
                add(&mut price, [probes, 0, probes, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
                let outside_heap = through_children.iter()
                    .map(|(name, child, _)| crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(child).saturating_mul(rows_of(name).saturating_add(1)))
                    .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
                heap = heap.max(outside_heap);
            }
            for r in self.referencing(table) {
                // A capped walk holds one page of child images per seek.
                let row = crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(r.table);
                heap = heap.max(row.saturating_mul(REFERENCE_PAGE as u64));
                let seeks = if r.table.expiry_column().is_some() && r.table.through.as_ref().is_none_or(|t| t.reference != r.column) { 2 } else { 1 };
                // A walk over a capped group: a seek per page, and a last, short page per range.
                let walk = |cap: u64| seeks * n + cap.saturating_mul(n) / REFERENCE_PAGE as u64;
                // Every reached row runs the lifetime hook for every through
                // child, including children the closure already cascaded away.
                let through = r.table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == r.column);
                if through && table != parent { add(&mut price, [3_u64, 0, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0].map(|v| v.saturating_mul(n))); }
                match r.action {
                    // A read-through child's probe: three seeks per closure row (LLP 3000.014 §6).
                    OnDelete::Restrict if through => {},
                    // One probe per closure row, a row per seek: it may skip the closure
                    // rows that name it (each names one target per reference), then stops
                    // at its first outside witness.
                    OnDelete::Restrict => {
                        let probe = seeks * n + rows_of(r.child) + n;
                        add(&mut price, [2 * probe, probe, seeks * n + rows_of(r.child) + n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
                    }
                    OnDelete::Cascade => {
                        let pages = walk(u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?));
                        add(&mut price, [2 * pages, pages, seeks * n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
                    }
                    OnDelete::SetNull => {
                        let cap = u64::from(self.reference_cap(r.child, r.column)?);
                        gathered = gathered.max(cap);
                        let cleared = cap.saturating_mul(n);
                        let unit = self.unit_write(r.child)?;
                        heap = heap.max(unit[4]);
                        let pages = walk(cap);
                        add(&mut price, [2 * pages, pages, seeks * n, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
                        add(&mut price, [unit[0], unit[1], unit[2] + 1, unit[3], 0, unit[5], unit[6]].map(|v| v.saturating_mul(cleared)));
                    }
                    OnDelete::Keep => {}
                }
            }
        }
        // The root is read again, current, before its own removal.
        price[2] = price[2].saturating_add(1);
        // The closure's identities (table and id) are held until the last
        // delete, with the root's and one page of child ids.
        // A set-null group is gathered whole (at most its cap) before it is cleared.
        price[4] = heap.saturating_add(identities.saturating_add(1 + REFERENCE_PAGE as u64 + gathered).saturating_mul(CLOSURE_IDENTITY_BYTES));
        let mut receiver_steps = 0;
        for (table, _) in &bounds {
            for reference in self.referencing(table) {
                if reference.action.writes() { receiver_steps = receiver_steps.max(self.write_reservation(reference.child)?.action_events?.steps_per_write); }
            }
        }
        price[0] = price[0].saturating_add(price[3].saturating_mul(receiver_steps));
        price[4] = price[4].saturating_add(self.retained_action_heap(parent, price[3])?);
        Some(price)
    }

    /// Diagnostic recipe price: action work plus the root's ordinary write.
    /// Execution retains its existing separate charges for these two terms.
    pub fn delete_total_reservation(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Price> {
        let mut total = self.delete_reservation(parent)?;
        add(&mut total, self.unit_write(parent)?);
        Some(total)
    }

    /// Event images remain live until commit, after action scratch is released.
    pub fn delete_event_heap(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<u64> {
        self.retained_action_heap(parent, self.delete_reservation(parent)?[3])
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.039#5.1 — two event images per priced row write, plus bounded keys and audience transitions, retained for the request lifetime.
    fn retained_action_heap(&self, parent: &str, writes: u64) -> Option<u64> {
        let mut per_write = 0;
        for (table, _) in self.closure_bounds(parent)? {
            for reference in self.referencing(&table) {
                if reference.action.writes() {
                    let events = self.write_reservation(reference.child)?.action_events?;
                    per_write = per_write.max(events.heap_per_write);
                }
            }
        }
        Some(writes.saturating_mul(per_write))
    }

    /// One engine write (delete or set-null update) of a `table` row: fetch and
    /// write it, its index entries (a `words(..)` index at its token bound), a
    /// row copy, and the source-write price the engine exports for the table.
    fn unit_write(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Price> {
        let table = self.table(name)?;
        let plan = self.write_reservation(name)?;
        if plan.server_only { return None; }
        let entries = table.indexes.values().map(|index| match index.word_component() {
            Some((_, fields)) => fields.iter().filter_map(|f| table.columns.get(f)).map(|kind| match kind.required() {
                ColumnType::Text { max } => u64::from(*max), _ => 0,
            }).sum::<u64>().min(crate::words::MAX_TOKENS_PER_ROW as u64),
            None => 1,
        }).fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
        let row = crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(table);
        // The row copy and every phase's heap are held together until the
        // write's attempt ends (an asset phase beside a column recount): a sum.
        let mut unit = [4 + 2 * entries, 2 * entries, 1, 1, row.saturating_mul(4), 0, 0];
        for phase in 0..=reservations::VIEW_READ {
            add(&mut unit, plan.price(phase));
        }
        // The lifetime hook reserves all child-table witnesses while source
        // phases are still held. Device verification additionally holds the
        // parent and a child scratch image; every host prices the same peak.
        let mut lifetime = 0_u64;
        let mut child_peak = 0_u64;
        for (_, child, _) in self.children(name) {
            let scratch = crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(child).saturating_mul(3);
            lifetime = lifetime.saturating_add(scratch);
            child_peak = child_peak.max(scratch);
        }
        if lifetime > 0 { unit[4] = unit[4].saturating_add(lifetime).saturating_add(child_peak).saturating_add(row); }
        Some(unit)
    }
}

/// The tables a delete's actions may write or read (`Schema::action_tables`).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct ActionTables {
    pub written: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub read: BTreeSet<String>,
}

/// Whether any rule of any table, or the child's own sync, reads `column` of
/// `child` — directly, as a probe key or equality on `child`, or as a hop.
fn carries_authority(schema: &Schema, child: &str, column: &str) -> bool {
    fn term_reads(term: &RuleTerm, own: bool, child: &str, column: &str) -> bool {
        match term {
            RuleTerm::Field(f) | RuleTerm::OldField(f) | RuleTerm::NextField(f) => own && f == column,
            RuleTerm::Reference { .. } | RuleTerm::ReferenceChain { .. } => {
                (own && term.reference_source().is_some_and(|(c, _)| c == column))
                    || term.references().any(|(table, field)| table == child && field == column)
            }
            RuleTerm::Viewer | RuleTerm::Literal(_) => false,
        }
    }
    fn rule_reads(schema: &Schema, rule: &RuleExpr, own: bool, child: &str, column: &str) -> bool {
        match rule {
            RuleExpr::Public { .. } | RuleExpr::Allow | RuleExpr::Deny => false,
            RuleExpr::Eq(a, b) | RuleExpr::Ne(a, b) | RuleExpr::Compare(_, a, b) => term_reads(a, own, child, column) || term_reads(b, own, child, column),
            RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| rule_reads(schema, item, own, child, column)),
            RuleExpr::Not(inner) => rule_reads(schema, inner, own, child, column),
            RuleExpr::Exists { table, index, key, equalities, .. } | RuleExpr::Created { table, index, key, equalities, .. } => {
                let probes_column = table == child && (equalities.iter().any(|(field, _)| field == column)
                    || schema.table(child).and_then(|t| t.index(index)).is_some_and(|i| i.columns().iter().take(key.len()).any(|c| c == column)));
                probes_column || key.iter().chain(equalities.iter().map(|(_, t)| t)).any(|term| term_reads(term, own, child, column))
            }
        }
    }
    schema.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| {
        let own = name == child;
        [&table.rules.read, &table.rules.insert, &table.rules.update, &table.rules.delete].iter().any(|rule| rule_reads(schema, rule, own, child, column))
            || table.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { table: target, index, key }
                if (target == child && schema.table(child).and_then(|t| t.index(index)).is_some_and(|i| i.columns().iter().take(key.len()).any(|c| c == column)))
                    || key.iter().any(|term| term_reads(term, own, child, column))))
    })
}

/// Why `column` cannot be cleared by its parent's delete, if it cannot: a
/// value that carries authority or meaning beyond "which parent this row has".
// @ref LLP 3000.039#2.2 — set null never changes any rule's verdict, moves a row between audiences, or rewrites a fact resolved through the reference.
pub fn set_null_refusal(schema: &Schema, name: &str, table: &Table, column: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let audience = table.sync.as_ref().is_some_and(|sync| std::iter::once((&sync.audience, sync.horizon.as_ref()))
        .chain(sync.also.iter().map(|arm| (&arm.audience, arm.horizon.as_ref())))
        .any(|(audience, horizon)| match audience {
        Audience::Public => false,
        Audience::Column(c) => c == column,
        Audience::Target { prefix, .. } => prefix.iter().any(|c| c == column),
    } || horizon.is_some_and(|h| table.index(&h.by).is_some_and(|i| i.uses_column(column)))));
    let maintained = schema.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.source == name && m.by.iter().any(|by| by.trim_start_matches('.').starts_with(&format!("{column}."))));
    if !table.columns.get(column).is_some_and(ColumnType::is_optional) { Some("the reference is required; declare it optional (`?`) or choose cascade".into()) }
    else if table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == column) { Some("a read-through reference is required and immutable".into()) }
    else if table.immutable_fields().any(|f| f == column) { Some("the column is immutable".into()) }
    else if table.written_by.contains_key(column) { Some("the column is written by its field owner".into()) }
    else if table.sequences.values().any(|p| p == column) { Some("a sequence counts within it".into()) }
    else if table.recorded.values().any(|r| r.reference == column) || maintained { Some("a recorded or maintained path resolves through it".into()) }
    else if carries_authority(schema, name, column) { Some("a rule reads it, so clearing it would change that rule's verdict; a reference that carries authority chooses cascade, restrict or keep".into()) }
    else if audience { Some("the sync audience or horizon uses it, so clearing it would move the row between partitions".into()) }
    else if table.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::Cap { by, .. } if by.iter().any(|b| b == column) && by.len() != 1)) { Some(format!("a cap groups by it with other columns; its only cap is `cap N by {column}`")) }
    else { None }
}

/// Why rows of `name` cannot be deleted or cleared by another row's delete.
pub fn write_target_refusal(schema: &Schema, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let table = schema.table(name)?;
    if table.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::AppendOnly)) { Some(format!("{name} is append only")) }
    else if !table.written_by.is_empty() { Some(format!("{name} has field-owned (`written by`) columns, whose owners the schema singled out")) }
    else if schema.maintains.iter().filter(|m| m.source == name || m.row_key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k| k.table == name))
        .flat_map(|m| [Some(m.target.as_str()), m.private.as_ref().map(|owner| owner.table.as_str())]).flatten()
        .any(|destination| schema.table(destination).is_some_and(|t| t.sync.is_some() && t.written_by.values().any(|authority| !authority.audience))) {
        Some(format!("{name}'s derived writes deliver private fields, whose recipient authorization has no fixed action price"))
    }
    else if schema.timeline_member(name) { Some(format!("a timeline orders {name}'s writes")) }
    else if schema.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.row_key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k| k.table == name)) { Some(format!("{name} is a row-keyed view's member table, whose writes may recount a group outside any fixed price")) }
    else if schema.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.source == name && matches!(m.kind, MaintainKind::Sum { .. })) { Some(format!("{name} feeds a maintained sum: system work can delete rows despite `delete <- deny`, and a cascade from another parent can reach them; a hidden contribution could push the sum out of range, so whether the delete commits would depend on rows the deleter cannot see")) }
    else if schema.write_reservation(name).is_none_or(|plan| plan.server_only) { Some(format!("{name}'s writes have no fixed price, so a cascade into it cannot be reserved")) }
    else { None }
}

fn add(to: &mut Price, price: Price) {
    for (to, price) in to.iter_mut().zip(price) { *to = to.saturating_add(price); }
}

/// Structural admission of `on_delete` (the compiler states each refusal first).
pub fn validate(schema: &Schema) -> Vec<SchemaIssue> {
    let mut issues = Vec::new();
    for (name, table) in &schema.tables {
        for (column, action) in &table.on_delete {
            let path = format!("tables.{name}.onDelete.{column}");
            let mut fail = |message: String| issues.push(SchemaIssue { path: path.clone(), message });
            let Some(ColumnType::Ref { table: parent }) = table.columns.get(column).map(ColumnType::required) else {
                fail(format!("on delete names {column}, which is not a reference column")); continue;
            };
            if table.written_by.contains_key(column) {
                fail(format!("{name}.{column} is field-owned; a private value carries no delete action"));
                continue;
            }
            if !schema.actionable(name) || !schema.actionable(parent) {
                fail(format!("{name}.{column} -> {parent} cannot carry a delete action: ephemeral, engine-owned and receipt or timeline bookkeeping tables keep their own lifetimes"));
                continue;
            }
            let through = table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| &t.reference == column);
            if action.acts() && schema.reference_index(name, column).is_none() {
                fail(format!("{name}.{column} needs its reference index (leading with {column})"));
            }
            if action.writes() {
                if schema.reference_cap(name, column).is_none() {
                    fail(format!("E_CASCADE_BOUND: {} on {name}.{column} needs `cap N by {column}`", action.words()));
                }
                if let Some(reason) = write_target_refusal(schema, name) {
                    fail(format!("{} on {name}.{column}: {reason}", action.words()));
                }
            }
            match action {
                OnDelete::Keep if through => fail(format!("on delete keep on read-through {name}.{column}: a read-through child lives within its parent")),
                OnDelete::SetNull => if let Some(reason) = set_null_refusal(schema, name, table, column) { fail(format!("on delete set null on {name}.{column}: {reason}")); },
                OnDelete::Cascade if through && table.is_expiring() => fail(format!("on delete cascade on read-through {name}.{column} needs a child that never expires")),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
    if let Some(table) = schema.deletion_cycle() {
        issues.push(SchemaIssue { path: format!("tables.{table}"), message: format!("{table} reaches itself through on delete cascade and read through: no order can delete those rows") });
    }
    for name in schema.tables.keys() {
        if schema.is_referenced(name) && schema.delete_reservation(name).is_none()
            && schema.action_tables(name).written.iter().all(|t| write_target_refusal(schema, t).is_none())
            && schema.referencing(name).into_iter().all(|r| !r.action.writes() || schema.reference_cap(r.child, r.column).is_some()) {
            issues.push(SchemaIssue { path: format!("tables.{name}"), message: format!("on delete cascade from {name} reaches {name} again; a cascade cannot be cyclic") });
        }
    }
    issues
}

    59	  reservation cannot fit its program's ceilings (`E_CASCADE_BOUND`). There is
    60	  no runtime overflow path and no background sweep (§5.3 says why).
    61	- **What the caller can observe is fixed by the schema**, except the one
    62	  bit `restrict` exists to give: the meter, the touched tables and change
    63	  footprints a commit publishes, the reply's event count and the physical
    64	  authorization allowance never depend on how many (possibly hidden) rows a
    65	  cascade reached (§4.2).
    66	- **A device predicts a parent delete only when it holds every referencing
    67	  row** of the whole closure (the existing held-group proof). Otherwise the
    68	  call queues and the server decides; a predicted delete never predicts half
    69	  its cascade.
    70	
    71	## 1. The problem and the decision being amended
    72	
    73	- **Evidence.** Wave 5 lane 081 (`delete screenings[s]` kept RSVPs; the
    74	  roster listed them and `screeningCard` was null). Wave 6 lanes 029, 032,
    75	  036, 095 and 085 each wrote a zero-count guard or a cleanup loop by hand
    76	  (LLP 3000.036 §16.2). The booking recipe's `removeSlot` exists only to
    77	  refuse while bookings exist. SQL, Prisma, Rails and Django all give a
    78	  per-relation `ON DELETE`; Convex and Firebase give nothing, and their
    79	  users write the cleanup the farm wrote.
    80	- **The decision of 2026-09-13** (LLP 3000 §7) says a reference validates the
    81	  id's value; insert, update and upsert do not read the target; and
    82	  "deleting it neither cascades nor refuses because references remain". This
    83	  RFC replaces the last clause and keeps the rest: **a reference is still not
    84	  an existence check at write time.** A row may be inserted naming an id that
    85	  does not exist, is hidden, or lives in another partition, exactly as today;
    86	  `require exists t[ref] else CODE` remains the explicit form (§4.4 says what
    87	  this leaves open). What changes is what happens to the rows that reference
    88	  a row **at the moment it is deleted**.
    89	
    90	The integrity claim is therefore precise and modest: **when a delete of row
    91	`p` executes, every live row that references `p` at that moment through a
    92	`restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` reference is refused for, deleted, or
    93	cleared.** It is not "no dangling reference ever exists": a later statement,
    94	even in the same mutation, may insert a row naming `p`, and a `keep`
    95	reference, an excluded reference kind (§2.1) or an expired parent still
    96	leaves the referencing row in place.
    97	
    98	## 2. The form
    99	
   100	```
   101	column: <table> [?] [on delete restrict | on delete cascade | on delete set null | on delete keep] [default …] [written by …]
   102	```
   103	
   104	`on delete` follows the type (and its `?`). One spelling; no `on update`
   105	(ids are immutable).
   106	
   107	### 2.1 Which references carry an action
   108	
   109	A reference **carries an action** when both ends are ordinary durable
   110	tables: the child (the table declaring the column) and the parent (the
   111	table it names) are neither ephemeral nor engine-owned (maintained views,
   112	private maintained state, timeline-owned tables, and a receipt family's
   113	scope, members and runs tables). Every reference that carries an action has
   114	one: the declared one, or `restrict`.
   115	
   116	A reference that does not carry an action keeps today's meaning (the row
   117	stays) and declaring `on delete` on it is `E_REFERENCE_ACTION`:
   118	
   119	| Child or parent | Why no action |
   120	|---|---|
   121	| ephemeral child or parent | ephemeral rows live for seconds and are retired by the engine on its own clock; probing or cascading them would make durable deletes depend on presence |
   122	| engine-owned child or parent | the engine derives or orders these rows; no program writes or deletes them on its own (a receipt scope is deletable only by the system) |
   123	| a field-owned column (`written by`) | its value belongs to its writers' audience, not to the table's rules; probing, clearing or cascading through it would disclose or write a field only its owner may (LLP 3000.007's field authority), so the binder gives it no reference index |
   124	
   125	The integrity of §1 and the migration of §8 therefore cover every reference
   126	**that carries an action**. A field-owned reference keeps today's meaning,
   127	as a reference into an ephemeral table does: it may name a deleted row, and a
   128	read must treat its target as possibly absent.
   129	
   130	### 2.2 Eligibility of each action
   131	
   132	| Action | Requires | Refused |
   133	|---|---|---|
   134	| `restrict` | nothing | — |
   135	| `keep` | nothing | — (no index, no probe, no read gate) |
   136	| `cascade` | `cap N by <column>` on the child (exactly that column), or a plain single-column `unique <column>` key (an inferred effective bound of one) | without either bound: `E_CASCADE_BOUND`. A composite unique key does not bound one reference group. With `E_REFERENCE_ACTION`: a cycle in the cascade graph, including a self-reference, or in the union of cascade and `read through` edges (§3 step 6); a child that is `append only`, has any field-owned (`written by`) column, has a derived synced destination that delivers private fields to their owners, feeds a maintained `sum` (view or column), plays any role in a timeline (owned, mapped or authors), is a row-keyed view's member table (its writes may recount a group outside any fixed price), or whose source writes have no fixed price (a `server_only` reservation plan, LLP 3000.022 §14.3); a `read through` reference whose child can carry a finite effective deadline (§6.1). |
   137	| `set null` | an optional (`?`) reference; either `cap N by <column>` or the same single-column unique inference, whose effective bound is one | everything refused for `cascade` except the cycle rule (set null does not recurse), and a column that **carries authority or meaning anywhere in the schema**: `immutable`, `written by`, a `sequence` parent, the root of a recorded or maintained path (`.column.field`), read by **any** rule of **any** table — the child's own read and write rules (directly or as the first hop of `.column.field`), every other table's `exists`/`created` probe that keys or equates on it, and every rule's hop that passes through it (`.task.column`) — named by the child's `sync` audience or horizon index, or named by any `cap` other than `cap N by <column>` alone. (Another table's sync audience can depend on the column only through a `read through` capture of the child's read rule, which the read-rule exclusion already covers.) |
   138	
   139	Rationale for the `set null` exclusions: each one is a place where the
   140	column's value is more than "which parent this row has". Clearing a column a
   141	rule reads can grant or remove authority (`update <- .assignee = null`, or
   142	another table's `exists grants[document = .id, folder = null]`), and the
   143	parent's deleter was never authorized to change anybody's authority. An
   144	immutable or field-owned column promises nobody else writes it. A recorded
   145	or maintained path stores a fact resolved through the reference. A sync
   146	audience or horizon would move the row between partitions. What remains is
   147	the column that only says where a row is filed (a category, a folder used for
   148	display, a "related to"). A reference the author's rules read chooses
   149	`cascade`, `restrict` or `keep` instead. A self-reference may be `set null`;
   150	it does not recurse.
   151	
   152	**A cap on a `set null` column does not count null.** `cap N by category`
   153	bounds each category's rows; rows whose `category` is null belong to no
   154	parent and are not a group. This is new semantics only for a column that
   155	declares `set null` (a cap on any other nullable column keeps counting its
   156	null group as today), and it is what makes the cap a bound on the
   157	reference's children rather than a limit that the set-null writes would
   158	themselves overflow. Because the null group is then unbounded, **such a cap
   159	never proves a population bound** (a loop's bound, a page's completeness,
   160	mutation admission): those proofs ignore it, as they ignore an index that is
   161	not unique. (A proof that the pinned value is non-null could recover the bound
   162	for one parent's group; §10 records it.) Cap enforcement, activation's group validation, and a device's
   163	cap proofs skip the null group of that column; changing the action away from
   164	`set null` re-validates the cap at activation, null group included.
   165	
   166	The unique inference has the same per-parent scope. It applies to required
   167	and optional references: a plain unique reference has at most one row for each
   168	non-null parent id. An optional unique reference may still have an unbounded
   169	null group. Referential actions probe only a concrete non-null parent id, so
   170	that null group is never counted in the action reservation and the inference
   171	never proves a table population bound. When both declarations exist, the
   172	effective bound is the smaller of the explicit cap and one.
   173	
   174	### 2.3 The reference index
   175	
   176	Every reference whose action probes or writes its children is probed by its
   177	column. The binder reuses a plain index whose leading columns are the
   178	reference (then, for an expiring child, its **effective** deadline column: a
   179	`read through` child's captured `$deadline`, which is the earlier of its own
   180	and its parents' deadlines, else its `expire at` column); otherwise it
   181	synthesizes an engine-named one: `[column, id]`, or
   182	`[column, deadlineColumn, id]` for an expiring child, so one seek skips
   183	an expired backlog (as `read through`'s child index does, LLP 3000.014 §6):
   184	the live rows are exactly `[id, null]` (never expires) and `[id]` with the
   185	deadline after now, so both seeks start at the live suffix and no expired row
   186	is ever visited.
   187	A `read through` reference uses its existing child index. The same index
   188	serves `cap N by <column>`. A `keep` reference gets none.
   189	
   190	## 3. What a delete does
   191	
   192	A delete of row `p` of table `P` — `delete P[id]`, `delete row`, a unique-key
   193	`delete P[key = …]`, a job, `POST /seed`'s delete, or `snapback4 data` —
   194	runs these steps in the deleting transaction, on every host:
   195	
   196	1. **Find and authorize `p`**, as today, with one addition: when any
   197	   `restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` reference names `P`, the caller needs
   198	   **read authority on `p`** as well as delete authority, for every delete
   199	   attempt, with or without children. A caller who may delete but not read
   200	   gets the ordinary hidden-target refusal. This is LLP 3000.014 §3.1's
   201	   rule, generalized from `read through` children to every referenced table,
   202	   and it keeps step 3 from probing a hidden row's children. The system
   203	   principal passes both rules, as it does every rule.
   204	2. **Reserve.** Charge the reservation `R(P)` of §5.1 on every meter, draw
   205	   its row count from the request's physical authorization allowance, and
   206	   publish the schema-fixed trace of §4.2.
   207	3. **Close.** Starting from `p`, follow every `cascade` reference to the
   208	   live rows that reference a reached row, and repeat: the **closure** `S`
   209	   is `p` plus every row reached. (`S` is finite: the cascade graph is
   210	   acyclic and each edge has an explicit or inferred effective bound.) Steps 3–5 stream the referencing rows
   211	   through the reference index (§2.3) a bounded page at a time and keep only
   212	   identities; no image outlives its page.
   213	4. **Restrict.** For every row `s` in `S` and every `restrict` reference
   214	   into `s`'s table, look for a live row that references `s` **and is not
   215	   itself in `S`**: the probe streams past the rows of `S` that name `s` —
   216	   `p` included, which may name itself — to the first live row outside `S`
   217	   (each row of `S` names one target per reference, so a delete's probes
   218	   visit each row of `S` at most once, plus one witness per probe). Every
   219	   such probe runs. If any is occupied, refuse with
   220	   the **first occupied reference in schema order** of
   221	   `(child table, column)` — never the first found while walking hidden
   222	   rows:
   223	
   224	   `E_REFERENCED: projects at <site> is still referenced through comments.task (on delete restrict); delete or retarget those rows first, or declare the reference's action (guide writes)`
   225	
   226	   "Live" means present and not expired. A row inserted earlier in the same
   227	   transaction counts; one deleted earlier in it does not. Because rows in

    78	        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
    79	            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),

    98	// @ref LLP 3000.007.003#3.0 — identity adoption covers every surviving typed reference, including dormant storage.
    99	pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(
   100	    tx: &Tx<'_>,
   101	    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
   102	) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {

   107	        "SELECT v.t,v.id,v.column_name,v.data,c.definition FROM _dormant_values v JOIN _catalog k ON k.num=v.t JOIN _dormant_columns c ON c.table_name=k.name AND c.column_name=v.column_name ORDER BY v.t,v.id,v.column_name"
   108	    )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?, row.get::<_,String>(4)?)))?
   109	        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?;
   110	    for (t, id, column, data, definition) in cells {

   112	        let mut value: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;

   117	    }

   120	        "SELECT r.t,r.id,r.data,d.definition FROM _dormant_rows r JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=r.t JOIN _dormant_tables d ON d.table_name=c.name ORDER BY r.t,r.id"
   121	    )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?)))?
   122	        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?;
   123	    for (t, id, data, definition) in rows {
   124	        let table: Table = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
   125	        let mut row: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;

   130	    }

   132	    let narrowed = if super::narrowed::present(tx.conn())? {
   133	        tx.conn().prepare(
   134	            "SELECT t,id,data,definition FROM _dormant_narrow_rows ORDER BY t,id"
   135	        )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?)))?
   136	            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?
   137	    } else { Vec::new() };
   138	    for (t, id, data, definition) in narrowed {
   139	        let table: Table = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
   140	        let mut row: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;

   169	    )?;

   171	    references(kind, value, &mut refs);

   195	        params![t, id, column, parent_t, parent_id, if invalid {2} else {0}],
   196	    )?;

   198	}
   199	pub(super) fn capture_through_parent(

//! One wire fence for engine semantics an older decoder must not ignore.
//! Constraint is strictly parsed by 0.2.33, unlike Schema's optional fields.
use super::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize, Serializer};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

// Private remote derive: the schema has one wire field list, and callers
// cannot accidentally invoke an unchecked inherent Schema::deserialize.
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(remote = "Schema")]
struct Wire {
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    receipts: Vec<ReceiptFamily>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    receipt_dependencies: BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<String>>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    source_reservations: BTreeMap<String, reservations::WriteReservation>,
    #[serde(skip)]
    legacy_receipt_prediction: bool,
    #[serde(skip)]
    legacy_semantic_capabilities: LegacySemanticCapabilities,
    tables: BTreeMap<String, Table>,
    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    #[serde(skip)]
    authored_indexes: inspection::AuthoredIndexes,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    delivery: Vec<DeliveryBinding>,
    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
    #[serde(skip)]
    delivery_lookup: crate::engine::delivery::Lookup,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    timelines: Vec<timeline::Timeline>,
    #[serde(default)]
    maintains: Vec<Maintain>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Auth::is_default")]
    auth: Auth,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    effects: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    schedules: Vec<Schedule>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    operations: BTreeMap<String, Execution>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    unique_refusals: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, UniqueRefusal>>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    action_specs: BTreeMap<String, ActionSpec>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    effect_specs: BTreeMap<String, WorkSpec>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]
    routes: BTreeMap<String, RouteSpec>,
}

// Add a capability and its schema predicate here in one line. This is both
// the derivation and the decoder's allowlist; authors never declare it.
const CAPABILITIES: &[(&str, fn(&Schema) -> bool)] = &[
    ("source-write-reservations-v2", |s| s.source_reservations.values().any(|p| p.birth.is_some())),
    ("source-write-reservations-v1", |s| !s.source_reservations.is_empty()),
    // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — older devices must not execute newly eligible
    // writes using their receipt-derived maintenance path.
    ("receipt-derived-prediction-v1", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m| s.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target))
        || s.has_receipt_columns()),
    ("rule-reference-v2", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t|
        [&t.rules.insert, &t.rules.update, &t.rules.delete].iter().any(|r| r.any_term(&|term| matches!(term, RuleTerm::ReferenceChain { .. })))
        || t.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { key, .. } if key.iter().any(|term| term.reference_source().is_some()))))),
    ("rule-reference", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| [&t.rules.insert, &t.rules.update, &t.rules.delete].iter().any(|r| r.has_reference()))),
    ("declarative-receipts-v4", |s| !s.receipts.is_empty()),
    ("owner-key-coverage", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.own_keys.is_some())),
    ("ephemeral", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.ephemeral.is_some())),
    ("field-authority", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.written_by.is_empty() || t.update_transition)),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036#11 — an older decoder refuses ordered insert rules rather than misjudging them.
    ("insert-rule-order", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| ordered(&t.rules.insert))),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036#12 — a decoder that orders only int/time in insert rules refuses a money or decimal order by name.
    ("insert-rule-order-units", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| ordered_units(t, &t.rules.insert))),
    ("row-keyed-view", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m|m.row_key.is_some())),
    // @ref LLP 3000.007.003#30-aggregate-target-identity-and-migration — older devices compute canonical-JSON
    // aggregate ids and would silently miss digest-addressed target rows.
    ("maintained-id-sha256-v1", |s| s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.row_key.is_none())),
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#8 — an older engine or device must not delete with the old (orphaning) semantics.
    ("reference-actions", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.on_delete.is_empty())),
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — pre-Wave-12 devices neither retire expiry
    // through actions nor queue an unproved same-id physical predecessor.
    ("expiry-reference-actions-v1", |s| s.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| table.is_expiring() && s.is_referenced(name))),
    ("read-through", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.through.is_some()) || s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.parent_key.is_some() || !m.aliases.is_empty())),
    // Device projections keep column metadata but omit private maintains.
    ("maintained-column", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.maintained.is_empty()) || s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.private.is_some())),
    ("recorded-attribution", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.recorded.is_empty())),
    ("sequence-by", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| !t.sequences.is_empty())),
    // @ref LLP 3000.040#4-fences-and-compatibility — an older decoder names the bounded int it cannot check.
    ("int-range", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.columns.values().any(int_range))),
    // @ref LLP 3000.040#4-fences-and-compatibility — civil keys and calendar schedules.
    ("calendar-month", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.indexes.values().any(|i| i.components.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, IndexComponent::Calendar(key) if key.civil()))))
        || s.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.computed.values().any(|key| key.civil()))),
    ("calendar-schedule", |s| s.schedules.iter().any(|schedule| schedule.months > 0)),
    ("timeline", |s| s.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.version == 1)),
    ("timeline-v2", |s| s.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.version == 2)),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.001#3 — an older device would page a merged plan as an eager merge and refuse its server cursors; it refuses the backend by name.
    ("branch-merge-v1", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_merge)),
    ("branch-membership-v1", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_membership)),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.001#15 — v2 fences metered uncapped discovery and row-id point lanes from v1 devices.
    ("branch-pages-v2", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v2)),
    ("branch-pages-v3", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v3)),
    ("branch-pages-v4", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_pages_v4)),
    ("branch-membership-v2", |s| s.operations.values().any(|o| o.branch_membership_v2)),
    // Source slots alter negative coverage, prediction and application row projection.
    ("timeline-event-slots", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.columns.keys().any(|field| timeline::is_slot(field)))),
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#2.3 — a decoder that ignored `also` would hold only the first arm and lose rows.
    ("union-audience", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.sync.as_ref().is_some_and(Sync::is_union))),
    ("time-audiences-v1", |s| s.tables.values().any(|t| t.not_before.is_some())),
];

fn int_range(kind: &ColumnType) -> bool {
    match kind {
        ColumnType::IntRange { .. } => true,
        ColumnType::Optional(inner) | ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => int_range(inner),
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn ordered_units(table: &Table, rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
    let units = |term: &RuleTerm| matches!(term, RuleTerm::Field(f) if matches!(table.columns.get(f), Some(ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. })));
    match rule {
        RuleExpr::Compare(_, l, r) => units(l) || units(r),
        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| ordered_units(table, item)),
        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered_units(table, inner),
        _ => false,
    }
}

fn ordered(rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
    match rule {
        RuleExpr::Compare(..) => true,
        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(ordered),
        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered(inner),
        _ => false,
    }
}

impl Schema {
    pub fn supported_capabilities() -> Vec<String> { CAPABILITIES.iter().map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect() }
    fn has_receipt_columns(&self) -> bool {
        self.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| table.maintained.keys().any(|field|
            self.receipt_dependencies.get(name).is_some_and(|fields| fields.contains(field))))
    }
    pub fn required_capabilities(&self) -> BTreeSet<String> {
        CAPABILITIES.iter().filter(|(_, needs)| needs(self)).map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect()
    }
}

impl Serialize for Schema {
    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
        let required = self.required_capabilities();
        // The derive's field order, omissions and bytes are unchanged for
        // ordinary schemas, including the serialized conformance corpus.
        if required.is_empty() { return Wire::serialize(self, serializer); }
        let mut wire = self.clone();
        for table in wire.tables.values_mut() {
            table.constraints.retain(|c| !matches!(c, Constraint::Recorded));
        }
        let mut carrier = wire.tables.first_entry().ok_or_else(||
            serde::ser::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: required capabilities need a table carrier"))?;
        carrier.get_mut().constraints.push(Constraint::Capabilities(required));
        Wire::serialize(&wire, serializer)
    }
}

impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Schema {
    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
        // The private remote derive uses the ordinary
        // streaming serde codec. No JSON-value or content-buffer replay.
        let mut schema = Wire::deserialize(deserializer)?;
        let mut declared = BTreeSet::new();
        let mut carriers = 0;
        let mut legacy = false;
        for table in schema.tables.values_mut() {
            let mut recorded = 0;
            table.constraints.retain(|constraint| {
                if let Constraint::Capabilities(names) = constraint {
                    carriers += 1;
                    declared.extend(names.iter().cloned());
                    false
                } else if matches!(constraint, Constraint::Recorded) {
                    recorded += 1;
                    false
                } else { true }
            });
            if recorded > 1 || (recorded != 0 && table.recorded.is_empty()) {
                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: invalid legacy Recorded marker"));
            }
            if recorded != 0 { legacy = true; declared.insert("recorded-attribution".into()); }
        }
        for name in &declared {
            if !CAPABILITIES.iter().any(|(known, _)| name == known) {
                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: unsupported engine capability {name}; upgrade the engine/device")));
            }
        }
        let mut required = schema.required_capabilities();
        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — RY already serialized the dependency closure.
        // RP stamps every emitted schema so old devices refuse its new prediction
        // facts, but an RP reader must still open RY's kept backend/database.
        // All other capabilities and the carrier shape remain exact.
        let legacy_receipt_prediction = !declared.contains("receipt-derived-prediction-v1")
            && required.remove("receipt-derived-prediction-v1");
        // The price carrier can be absent in an old projection. Missing prices
        // are fenced per program, rather than bricking a kept store.
        for cap in ["source-write-reservations-v1", "source-write-reservations-v2"] {
            if declared.contains(cap) { required.insert(cap.into()); }
            else { required.remove(cap); }
        }
        // Stores written before the digest migration have no carrier for this
        // capability. Admit that persisted schema for server-side rebuilding;
        // its next serialization stamps the capability, so old devices refuse.
        let mut legacy_semantic_capabilities = BTreeSet::new();
        if !declared.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1")
            && required.remove("maintained-id-sha256-v1") {
            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("maintained-id-sha256-v1".into());
        }
        // Kept pre-Wave-12 schemas need the server's new expiry action path,
        // then stamp the device fence on their next published projection.
        if !declared.contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1")
            && required.remove("expiry-reference-actions-v1") {
            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("expiry-reference-actions-v1".into());
        }
        // Before the shared fence, the binder emitted Recorded on F2 tables
        // even when the same schema also declared timelines. Only that legacy
        // representation infers its full requirements; modern carriers remain
        // exact, including when mixed with a legacy marker.
        if legacy && carriers == 0 {
            // A legacy marker only covers the capabilities that predate the fence.
            // New semantics must never inherit permission from this escape hatch.
            declared = required.iter().filter(|name| matches!(name.as_str(),
                "maintained-column" | "recorded-attribution" | "timeline" | "timeline-v2")).cloned().collect();
        }
        if declared != required || carriers + usize::from(legacy) != usize::from(!required.is_empty()) {
            return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: schema requires {required:?}, but declares {declared:?} in {carriers} carriers")));
        }
        let had_prices = !schema.source_reservations.is_empty();
        schema.prepare_receipt_dependencies();
        // Opening an old blob preserves its wire shape. Complete visible
        // declarations can still price a write on demand; hidden ones cannot.
        if !had_prices { schema.source_reservations.clear(); }
        schema.legacy_receipt_prediction = legacy_receipt_prediction
            || (!declared.contains("source-write-reservations-v1") && !schema.receipts.is_empty());
        schema.legacy_semantic_capabilities = legacy_semantic_capabilities.into();
        Ok(schema)
    }
}
