// Linux counterpart of schema-capabilities.test.mjs's published-engine fence.
// Include DDL (indexes/triggers/columns), every table and every stored value.
// The refusal contract covers schema/rows, integrity and freelist count.
// WAL identity is asserted for the small no-spill cases below; a large rolled
// back migration may change free-page contents or retain uncommitted frames
// (LLP 3000.033 §1.3).
fn sqlite_dump(path: &std::path::Path) -> Vec<(String, Vec<String>)> {
    let db = rusqlite::Connection::open_with_flags(path, rusqlite::OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY).unwrap();
    let mut tables = vec!["sqlite_schema".to_string()];
    tables.extend(db.prepare("SELECT name FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'table' ORDER BY name").unwrap()
        .query_map([], |r| r.get::<_, String>(0)).unwrap().map(Result::unwrap));
    let mut snapshot = tables.into_iter().map(|name| {
        let mut stmt = db.prepare(&format!("SELECT * FROM \"{}\"", name.replace('"', "\"\""))).unwrap();
        let columns = stmt.column_count();
        let mut rows = stmt.query_map([], |r| (0..columns).map(|i| r.get::<_, rusqlite::types::Value>(i)).collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<_>>>())
            .unwrap().map(|r| format!("{:?}", r.unwrap())).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        rows.sort();
        (name, rows)
    }).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    let integrity: String = db.query_row("PRAGMA integrity_check", [], |r| r.get(0)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(integrity, "ok");
    let free: i64 = db.query_row("PRAGMA freelist_count", [], |r| r.get(0)).unwrap();
    snapshot.push(("PRAGMA integrity_check/freelist_count".into(), vec![integrity, free.to_string()]));
    snapshot
}

fn legacy_device(path: &std::path::Path, mode: &str) {
    drop(snapback4_device::native::Device::open(path, Some(plain())).unwrap());
    let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(path).unwrap();
    db.execute("INSERT INTO r(t,id,data) SELECT num,'kept',?1 FROM _catalog WHERE name = 't'",
        [serde_json::to_string(&object([("id", Value::Id("kept".into()))])).unwrap()]).unwrap();
    db.execute_batch("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _read_sessions;").unwrap();
    let has_scope: bool = db.query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pragma_table_info('_session_mint_bindings') WHERE name = 'scope')", [], |r| r.get(0)).unwrap();
    if has_scope { db.execute_batch("ALTER TABLE _session_mint_bindings DROP COLUMN scope;").unwrap(); }
    db.execute_batch(&format!("PRAGMA journal_mode = {mode};")).unwrap();
}

fn future_backend() -> Backend {
    let mut future = plain();
    future.generation = 2;
    future.schema.tables.get_mut("t").unwrap().constraints.push(
        snapback4_core::schema::Constraint::Capabilities(["future-derivation".into()].into()));
    future
}

#[test]
fn legacy_native_open_and_refused_adoption_preserve_complete_store() {
    for mode in ["WAL", "DELETE"] {
        let host = common::Sqlite::new("refused-legacy-adoption");
        let path = host.path(mode);
        legacy_device(&path, mode);
        let before = sqlite_dump(&path);
        let mut device = snapback4_device::native::Device::open(&path, None).unwrap();
        let answer = call::call(&mut device, json!({"op":"adopt", "backend":future_backend()}));
        assert_eq!(answer["denied"]["code"], "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY");
        drop(device);
        assert_eq!(sqlite_dump(&path), before, "opening then refusing adoption must not add auth storage");
    }
}

#[test]
fn refused_native_open_preserves_missing_tables_indexes_columns_and_meta() {
    for mode in ["WAL", "DELETE"] {
        let host = common::Sqlite::new("refused-legacy-open");
        let path = host.path(mode);
        legacy_device(&path, mode);
        let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(&path).unwrap();
        db.execute("UPDATE _meta SET value = ?1 WHERE key = 'device:backend'", [serde_json::to_string(&future_backend()).unwrap()]).unwrap();
        // Exercise the older migrations too, not just _read_sessions.

            ALTER TABLE _jobs DROP COLUMN domain; DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key = 'store_id';
            CREATE INDEX _log_row_seq ON _log(seq);").unwrap();
        drop(db);
        let before = sqlite_dump(&path);
        for opening in [Opening::Kept, Opening::Install(plain()), Opening::Initial(plain())] {
            let error = snapback4_device::native::Device::open_with(&path, opening).err().expect("refused open");
            assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY");
            assert_eq!(sqlite_dump(&path), before);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn refused_store_version_and_server_adoption_preserve_complete_store() {
    use snapback4_core::{Engine, Store};
    for mode in ["WAL", "DELETE"] {
        let host = common::Sqlite::new("refused-server-open");
        let path = host.path(mode);
        let (schema, programs) = (plain().schema, plain().programs);
        drop(Engine::new(Store::open(&path).unwrap(), schema.clone(), programs.clone()).unwrap());
        let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(&path).unwrap();
        db.execute_batch(&format!("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _read_sessions; DROP TABLE _change_evidence;
            DROP TABLE _effect_steps; DROP INDEX _sessions_expiry; CREATE INDEX _log_row_seq ON _log(seq);
            INSERT INTO _meta VALUES ('release','1');
            ALTER TABLE _jobs DROP COLUMN domain; DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key = 'store_id'; PRAGMA journal_mode = {mode};")).unwrap();
        drop(db);
        let before = sqlite_dump(&path);
        // Selecting an obsolete release must refuse before attachment upgrades.
        assert_eq!(Engine::attach_release(Store::open(&path).unwrap(), 999).err().expect("refused attachment").code(), "E_GENERATION");
        assert_eq!(sqlite_dump(&path), before);
        // The release mismatch refuses from inside activation, after DDL work.
        let error = Engine::new_release(Store::open(&path).unwrap(), schema, programs, 2, Some(999)).err().expect("refused adoption");
        assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_GENERATION");
        assert_eq!(sqlite_dump(&path), before);
        let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(&path).unwrap();
        db.execute("UPDATE _generations SET schema = 'invalid json'", []).unwrap();
        drop(db);
        let before = sqlite_dump(&path);
        assert_eq!(Engine::open(Store::open(&path).unwrap()).err().expect("refused stored schema").code(), "E_STORE");
        assert_eq!(sqlite_dump(&path), before);
        let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(&path).unwrap();
        db.execute("UPDATE _meta SET value = 'future-store' WHERE key = 'version'", []).unwrap();
        drop(db);
        let before = sqlite_dump(&path);
        assert_eq!(Store::open(&path).err().expect("refused store version").code(), "E_STORE");
        assert_eq!(sqlite_dump(&path), before);
    }
}

#[test]
fn refused_open_preserves_uncheckpointed_database_and_wal() {
    let host = common::Sqlite::new("refused-surviving-wal");
    let path = host.path("store");
    legacy_device(&path, "WAL");
    let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(&path).unwrap();
    db.set_db_config(rusqlite::config::DbConfig::SQLITE_DBCONFIG_NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE, true).unwrap();
    db.execute_batch("PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0; UPDATE _meta SET value='future-store' WHERE key='version';").unwrap();
    drop(db); // Deliberately retain committed frames with no live connection.
    let wal = std::path::PathBuf::from(format!("{}-wal", path.display()));
    let before = (std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), std::fs::read(&wal).unwrap());
    assert!(before.1.len() > 32, "fixture must retain committed WAL frames");
    let error = snapback4_core::Store::open(&path).err().expect("unsupported store");
    assert!(error.to_string().contains("future-store"));
    assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&path).unwrap(), before.0, "refused connection must not checkpoint");
    assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&wal).unwrap(), before.1, "refused connection must retain WAL bytes");
}

#[test]
fn native_open_recovery_refusals_roll_back_installation() {
    for mode in ["WAL", "DELETE"] {
        for refusal in ["overflow", "malformed", "native_cleanup"] {
            let host = common::Sqlite::new("refused-open-recovery");
            let path = host.path(refusal);
            legacy_device(&path, mode);
            let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(&path).unwrap();
            if mode == "WAL" {
                db.set_db_config(rusqlite::config::DbConfig::SQLITE_DBCONFIG_NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE, true).unwrap();
                db.execute_batch("PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0").unwrap();
            }
            db.execute_batch("DROP TABLE _effect_steps;").unwrap();
            if refusal == "native_cleanup" {
                db.execute_batch("INSERT INTO _meta VALUES ('device:native','invalid');
                    CREATE TRIGGER refuse_native_cleanup BEFORE DELETE ON _meta WHEN old.key = 'device:native'
                    BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'native cleanup refused'); END;").unwrap();
            } else {
                db.execute_batch("INSERT INTO _meta VALUES ('device:declaration:capture','{}');").unwrap();
                db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO _meta VALUES ('device:send_revision',?1)",
                    [if refusal == "overflow" { "9007199254740991" } else { "invalid" }]).unwrap();
            }
            drop(db);
            let before = sqlite_dump(&path);
            let wal_path = std::path::PathBuf::from(format!("{}-wal", path.display()));
            let wal = std::fs::read(&wal_path).ok();
            if mode == "WAL" { assert!(wal.as_ref().is_some_and(|w| w.len() > 32)); }
            let error = snapback4_device::native::Device::open(&path, None).err().expect("recovery must refuse");
            assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_STORE", "{refusal}: {error}");
            assert_eq!(sqlite_dump(&path), before, "{mode}/{refusal}: no installed upgrades or metadata changes");
            assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&wal_path).ok(), wal, "{mode}/{refusal}: unchanged WAL bytes");
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn spill_sized_native_refusal_preserves_committed_state_with_free_pages() {
    for mode in ["WAL", "DELETE"] {
        let host = common::Sqlite::new("refused-migration-spill");
        let path = host.path(mode);
        legacy_device(&path, mode);
        let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(&path).unwrap();
        db.execute_batch("ALTER TABLE _ops ADD COLUMN args TEXT; BEGIN IMMEDIATE;").unwrap();
        let payload = format!("\"{}\"", "x".repeat(8192));
        for n in 0..1500 {
            db.execute("INSERT INTO _ops(principal,id,seq,outcome,args) VALUES ('bob',?1,1,?2,'legacy')",
                rusqlite::params![n.to_string(), payload]).unwrap();
        }
        db.execute_batch("DROP TABLE _effect_steps;
            INSERT INTO _meta VALUES ('device:declaration:capture','{}');
            INSERT OR REPLACE INTO _meta VALUES ('device:send_revision','9007199254740991'); COMMIT;
            CREATE TABLE free_page_fixture(data BLOB);
            INSERT INTO free_page_fixture VALUES (zeroblob(4194304));
            DROP TABLE free_page_fixture;").unwrap();
        drop(db); // Checkpoint the large fixture before retaining a small WAL.
        if mode == "WAL" {
            let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(&path).unwrap();
            db.set_db_config(rusqlite::config::DbConfig::SQLITE_DBCONFIG_NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE, true).unwrap();
            db.execute_batch("PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0; INSERT INTO _meta VALUES ('sg:sentinel','retained committed WAL');").unwrap();
        }
        let before = sqlite_dump(&path);
        let bytes = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
        let wal_path = std::path::PathBuf::from(format!("{}-wal", path.display()));
        let wal = std::fs::read(&wal_path).ok();
        let error = snapback4_device::native::Device::open(&path, None).err().expect("late recovery refusal");
        assert!(error.to_string().contains("send revision overflow"), "{error}");
        let after_bytes = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(after_bytes.len(), bytes.len());
        // SQLite deliberately omits freelist leaves from rollback journals.
        // Enforce the precise exception: only pre-existing free leaves may differ.
        let free = freelist_leaves(&bytes);
        assert!(free.len() > 1000, "fixture must have committed free pages");
        let page_size = u16::from_be_bytes([bytes[16], bytes[17]]) as usize;
        let changed = bytes.chunks(page_size).zip(after_bytes.chunks(page_size)).enumerate()
            .filter_map(|(n, (before, after))| (before != after).then_some(n as u32 + 1)).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        assert!(changed.iter().all(|page| free.contains(page)), "{mode}: allocated pages changed: {changed:?}");
        if mode == "DELETE" { assert!(!changed.is_empty(), "exercise freelist leaf reuse and spill"); }
        else { assert!(changed.is_empty(), "WAL spill does not write the main file"); }
        eprintln!("{mode}: {} free leaves; {} changed free pages; schema/rows, integrity and freelist count unchanged", free.len(), changed.len());
        assert_eq!(sqlite_dump(&path), before, "{mode}: every schema entry and value survives, including legacy args and missing _effect_steps");
        if let Some(wal) = wal {
            assert!(wal.len() > 32 && wal.len() < 64 * 1024, "start with a small committed WAL");
            let after = std::fs::read(&wal_path).unwrap();
            assert!(after.len() > 8 * 1024 * 1024, "fixture must actually spill beyond the native cache: {} bytes", after.len());
            assert!(after.starts_with(&wal), "committed uncheckpointed frames survive; only uncommitted frames are appended");
            eprintln!("refused legacy migration: main {} bytes identical; WAL {} -> {} bytes; full logical dump identical", bytes.len(), wal.len(), after.len());
        } else {
            assert_eq!(mode, "DELETE");
        }
        // A later accepting open still performs the real migration and capture
        // recovery. Rollback must not leave an unrecoverable physical store.
        let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(&path).unwrap();
        db.execute("UPDATE _meta SET value='0' WHERE key='device:send_revision'", []).unwrap();
        drop(db);
        drop(snapback4_device::native::Device::open(&path, None).unwrap());
        let db = rusqlite::Connection::open(&path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(db.query_row("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM _ops", [], |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0)).unwrap(), 1500);
        assert!(!db.query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pragma_table_info('_ops') WHERE name='args')", [], |r| r.get::<_, bool>(0)).unwrap());
        assert!(db.query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_schema WHERE name='_effect_steps')", [], |r| r.get::<_, bool>(0)).unwrap());
        assert_eq!(db.query_row("SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='device:send_revision'", [], |r| r.get::<_, String>(0)).unwrap(), "1");
    }
}

fn freelist_leaves(bytes: &[u8]) -> std::collections::BTreeSet<u32> {
    let word = |offset| u32::from_be_bytes(bytes[offset..offset + 4].try_into().unwrap());
    let size = u16::from_be_bytes([bytes[16], bytes[17]]) as usize;
    let mut trunk = word(32);
    let mut leaves = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
    while trunk != 0 {
        let offset = (trunk as usize - 1) * size;
        for n in 0..word(offset + 4) as usize { assert!(leaves.insert(word(offset + 8 + n * 4))); }
        trunk = word(offset);
    }
    leaves
}

//! One logical allowance for work whose shape can depend on unreadable rows.
use super::runner::Runner;
use std::cell::{Cell, RefCell};

// @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — one physical allowance per request, nested work included.
pub(super) const AUTHORIZATION_WALK_LIMIT: usize = 8192;
use crate::{
    assets::Asset,
    error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError}, meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter}, rows::{AcquiredBoundary, Bounds, Dir, PrefetchRequest, Rows}, schema::{Index, Table}, value::Value,
};

// Only this module mints the capability; it cannot be constructed or cloned
// by callers, and the borrowed token cannot escape the guarded closure.
pub struct Authorization { probes: Cell<u64>, remaining_probes: u64 }

impl Authorization {
    fn internal() -> Self { Self { probes: std::cell::Cell::new(0), remaining_probes: u64::MAX } }
    // The candidate's declared probe allowance is checked before authorization
    // executes. The enclosing scope commits this logical count on every exit.
    pub(super) fn admit_probes(&self, probes: u64) -> bool {
        let total = self.probes.get().saturating_add(probes);
        self.probes.set(total);
        total <= self.remaining_probes
    }

}


// No Rows implementation, Deref or raw accessor: row reads require the
// unforgeable token even when a caller has access to Runner's store facade.
pub(crate) struct GuardedRows<'a> { raw: &'a dyn Rows, remaining: Cell<usize>, authorizing: Cell<bool>, reference_prepaid: Cell<bool>, revision: Cell<u64>, lookup_cache: RefCell<Option<(String, String, Vec<Value>, Option<Value>)>> }
impl<'a> GuardedRows<'a> {
    pub(crate) fn new(raw: &'a dyn Rows) -> Self { Self { raw, remaining: Cell::new(AUTHORIZATION_WALK_LIMIT), authorizing: Cell::new(false), reference_prepaid: Cell::new(false), revision: Cell::new(0), lookup_cache: RefCell::new(None) } }
    pub(super) fn revision(&self) -> u64 { self.revision.get() }
    pub(super) fn remaining(&self) -> usize { self.remaining.get() }
    fn limit(&self, table: &str, requested: usize) -> Result<usize, RuntimeError> {
        if !self.authorizing.get() || self.reference_prepaid.get() { return Ok(requested); }
        if self.remaining.get() == 0 { return Err(RuntimeError::AuthorizationBudget { table: table.into(), effect: crate::schema::Effect::Read }); }
        Ok(requested.min(self.remaining.get()))
    }
    fn charge(&self, fetched: usize) {
        if self.authorizing.get() && !self.reference_prepaid.get() { self.remaining.set(self.remaining.get().saturating_sub(fetched)); }
    }
    /// Return the walk allowance of a fetched row the store stepped over as
    /// expired: such rows are absent, so they cannot exhaust a read's walk.
    pub(super) fn refund(&self, fetched: usize) {
        if self.authorizing.get() { self.remaining.set(self.remaining.get() + fetched); }
    }
    pub(crate) fn get(&self, _authorization: &Authorization, table: &str, id: &str) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
        self.limit(table, 1)?;
        let row = self.raw.get(table, id)?;
        self.charge(usize::from(row.is_some()));
        Ok(row)
    }
    /// A key-only witness still consumes the shared physical authorization allowance.
    pub(crate) fn index_head(&self, _authorization: &Authorization, table: &str, index: &str, prefix: &[Value], bounds: &Bounds, dir: Dir) -> Result<Option<Vec<Value>>, RuntimeError> {
        self.limit(table, 1)?;
        let key = self.raw.index_head(table, index, prefix, bounds, dir)?;
        self.charge(usize::from(key.is_some()));
        Ok(key)
    }
    pub(crate) fn lookup(&self, _authorization: &Authorization, table: &str, name: &str, index: &Index, key: &[Value]) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
        // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — repeated unchanged points share decoded storage,
        // while every logical read still prepays its complete rule.
        if let Some((cached_table, cached_index, cached_key, row)) = &*self.lookup_cache.borrow()
            && cached_table == table && cached_index == name && cached_key == key { return Ok(row.clone()); }
        self.limit(table, 1)?;
        let row = self.raw.lookup(table, name, index, key)?;
        self.charge(usize::from(row.is_some()));
        *self.lookup_cache.borrow_mut() = Some((table.into(), name.into(), key.to_vec(), row.clone()));
        Ok(row)
    }
    pub(crate) fn scan(&self, _authorization: &Authorization, table: &str, name: &str, prefix: &[Value], bounds: &Bounds, dir: Dir, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<(Value, Vec<u8>)>, RuntimeError> {
        let permitted = self.limit(table, limit)?;
        let rows = self.raw.scan(table, name, prefix, bounds, dir, permitted)?;
        self.charge(rows.len());
        if permitted < limit && rows.len() == permitted { return Err(RuntimeError::AuthorizationBudget { table: table.into(), effect: crate::schema::Effect::Read }); }
        Ok(rows)
    }
    #[cfg(feature = "server-search")]
    pub(crate) fn scan_selected(&self, _authorization: &Authorization, table: &str, name: &str, prefix: &[Value], bounds: &Bounds, dir: Dir, fields: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<(Value, Vec<u8>)>, RuntimeError> {
        self.limit(table, 1)?;
        let rows = self.raw.scan_selected(table, name, prefix, bounds, dir, fields)?;
        self.charge(rows.len());
        Ok(rows)
    }
    pub(crate) fn scan_metered(&self, _authorization: &Authorization, table: &str, name: &str, prefix: &[Value], bounds: &Bounds, dir: Dir, limit: usize, meter: &mut Meter) -> Result<Vec<(Value, Vec<u8>)>, RuntimeError> {
        let permitted = self.limit(table, limit)?;
        let rows = InternalLedger::with_meter(meter, |meter, _| {
            self.raw.scan_metered(table, name, prefix, bounds, dir, permitted, _authorization, meter)
        })?;
        self.charge(rows.len());
        if permitted < limit && rows.len() == permitted { return Err(RuntimeError::AuthorizationBudget { table: table.into(), effect: crate::schema::Effect::Read }); }
        Ok(rows)
    }
    pub(crate) fn count_prefix(&self, _authorization: &Authorization, table: &str, name: &str, prefix: &[Value], limit: u64) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        // This scalar adapter is used only by non-expiring, non-private
        // caps. It fetches no candidate rows and keeps its declared cap bound.
        self.raw.count_prefix(table, name, prefix, limit)
    }

    pub(crate) fn cap_count(&self, _authorization: &Authorization, table: &str, by: &[String], group: &[Value]) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> { self.raw.cap_count(table, by, group) }

    pub(crate) fn sequence_value(&self, _authorization: &Authorization, parent: &str, id: &str) -> Result<i64, RuntimeError> { self.raw.sequence_value(parent, id) }
    pub(crate) fn provisional_sequence_floor(&self, _authorization: &Authorization, parent: &str, id: &str) -> Result<i64, RuntimeError> { self.raw.provisional_sequence_floor(parent, id) }
    pub(crate) fn set_sequence(&self, parent: &str, id: &str, value: i64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> { self.raw.set_sequence(parent, id, value) }
    pub(crate) fn sequence_ids(&self, parent: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, RuntimeError> { self.raw.sequence_ids(parent) }
    pub(crate) fn rewrite_sequence_ids(&self, ids: &std::collections::BTreeMap<String, std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> { self.raw.rewrite_sequence_ids(ids) }
    pub(crate) fn put(&self, name: &str, table: &Table, row: &Value, old: Option<&Value>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> { self.revision.set(self.revision.get().wrapping_add(1)); self.lookup_cache.borrow_mut().take(); self.raw.put(name, table, row, old) }
    pub(crate) fn delete(&self, name: &str, table: &Table, old: &Value) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> { self.revision.set(self.revision.get().wrapping_add(1)); self.lookup_cache.borrow_mut().take(); self.raw.delete(name, table, old)
    }

        self.raw.time_audience_pending(name, id) }
    pub(crate) fn time_audience_published(&self, name: &str, id: &str) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        self.raw.time_audience_published(name, id) }
    pub(crate) fn holds_assets(&self) -> bool { self.raw.holds_assets() }
    pub(crate) fn widen_change_evidence(&self) { self.raw.widen_change_evidence() }
    /// Draw a schema-fixed number of rows from the request's physical
    /// allowance up front, so later authorization work exhausts it at a point
    /// independent of the rows a delete's actions reach (LLP 3000.039 §4.2).
    pub(crate) fn draw(&self, table: &str, rows: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let rows = usize::try_from(rows).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
        if self.remaining.get() < rows { self.remaining.set(0); return Err(RuntimeError::AuthorizationBudget { table: table.into(), effect: crate::schema::Effect::Delete }); }
        self.remaining.set(self.remaining.get() - rows);
        Ok(())
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#5.1 — reserved action hooks spend the physical draw once; ordinary root probes remain outside this scope.
    pub(super) fn reference_prepaid(&self, prepaid: bool) -> bool { self.reference_prepaid.replace(prepaid) }
    pub(crate) fn asset(&self, id: &str) -> Result<Option<Asset>, RuntimeError> { self.raw.asset(id) }
    pub(crate) fn claim_asset(&self, id: &str, by: &str, table: &str, row: &str, column: &str) -> Result<Asset, RuntimeError> { self.raw.claim_asset(id, by, table, row, column) }
    pub(crate) fn release_asset(&self, id: &str, #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")] table: &str, #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")] row_id: &str, #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")] column: &str, now: i64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> { #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")] { self.raw.release_asset(id, table, row_id, column, now) } #[cfg(not(feature = "sqlite"))] { self.raw.release_asset(id, now) } }
    pub(crate) fn effect_once(&self, effect: &str, key: &str) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> { self.raw.effect_once(effect, key) }
    pub(crate) fn provisional_id_after(&self, table: &str, after: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> { self.raw.provisional_id_after(table, after) }
    pub(crate) fn has_provisional(&self, table: &str) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> { self.raw.has_provisional(table) }
    pub(crate) fn provisional_groups(&self, table: &str, fields: &[String]) -> Result<Option<Vec<Vec<crate::value::Value>>>, RuntimeError> { self.raw.provisional_groups(table, fields) }
    pub(crate) fn provisional_row(&self, table: &str, row: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> { self.raw.provisional_row(table, row) }
    pub(crate) fn search_retained_row(&self, table: &str, row: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> { self.raw.search_retained_row(table, row) }
    pub(crate) fn retained_row(&self, table: &str, row: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> { self.raw.retained_row(table, row) }
    pub(crate) fn retained_group(&self, table: &str, index: &str, prefix: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> { self.raw.retained_group(table, index, prefix) }
    /// Device acquisition facts carry no row payload, like retained_row.
    pub(crate) fn current_row(&self, table: &str, row: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> { self.raw.current_row(table, row) }
    pub(crate) fn current_group(&self, table: &str, index: &str, prefix: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> { self.raw.current_group(table, index, prefix) }
    pub(crate) fn recording_covered(&self, table: &str, row: &Value, viewer: &str, now: i64, scope: &Authorization, meter: &mut Meter) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> { InternalLedger::with_meter(meter, |meter, _| {
            self.raw.recording_covered(table, row, viewer, now, scope, meter)
        }) }
    pub(crate) fn acquired_boundary(&self, table: &str, index: &str, prefix: &[Value]) -> Result<Option<AcquiredBoundary>, RuntimeError> { self.raw.acquired_boundary(table, index, prefix) }
    pub(crate) fn prefetch_enabled(&self) -> bool { self.raw.prefetch_enabled() }
    #[allow(dead_code)] // Used by the native prefetch planner; absent on web.
    pub(crate) fn prefetch(&self, requests: &[PrefetchRequest]) { self.raw.prefetch(requests) }
}

pub(super) struct PrepaidState {
    mark: crate::meter::MeterMark,
    ceilings: Ceilings,
    cut: Cut,
    authorizing: bool,
    nested: bool,
}

impl Runner<'_> {
    // @ref LLP 3000.015#1 — declaration-only scratch is admitted before any
    // candidate/witness access. The logical heap retains only disclosed output.
    pub(super) fn authorized_scratch<T: Default>(&mut self, bytes: u64, allowance: &[(MeterKind, u64)], work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
        self.reserved_scratch(bytes, allowance, true, work)
    }

    /// Count certification follows an admitted member and source-group verdict.
    /// Nested authorization still shares any enclosing physical allowance.
    pub(super) fn disclosed_scratch<T: Default>(&mut self, bytes: u64, allowance: &[(MeterKind, u64)], work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
        self.reserved_scratch(bytes, allowance, false, work)
    }

    pub(super) fn reserved_scratch<T: Default>(&mut self, bytes: u64, allowance: &[(MeterKind, u64)], physical: bool, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
        if self.device_work_active || self.context.is_system() { return self.prepaid_scan(allowance, physical, work); }
        let mark = self.meter.mark();
        self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
        let result = self.prepaid_scan(allowance, physical, work);
        self.meter.release_row_heap(mark, bytes);
        result
    }

    pub(super) fn rule_scratch(&self, rule: &crate::schema::RuleExpr) -> u64 {
        let mut sites = Vec::new();
        super::rules::probe_sites(rule, &mut sites);
        sites.iter().map(|(table, _)| self.witness_scratch(table)).max().unwrap_or(0)
    }

    pub(super) fn witness_scratch(&self, table: &str) -> u64 {
        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table];
        let own = crate::rows::disclosed::admission(definition);
        let source = self.schema.maintain_for(table)
            .and_then(|m| self.schema.table(&m.source)).filter(|source| source.is_expiring());
        own.saturating_add(source.map_or(0, crate::rows::disclosed::admission))
    }


    /// Ordinary data reads keep their existing meter and cut semantics. This
    /// scope grants storage access without disabling or restoring any charge.
    /// Hidden authorization must use authorized_scan's prepaid reservation.
    pub(crate) fn metered_scan<T>(&mut self, scan: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
        scan(self, &Authorization::internal())
    }

    /// A rule whose logical allowance the caller has already charged, possibly
    /// to a cut, still evaluates its witnesses under the physical allowance;
    /// the caller decides what its cut means for the answer (LLP 3000.014 §5).
    pub(super) fn prepaid_witnesses<T>(&mut self, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
        let active = self.tx.authorizing.replace(self.tx.authorizing.get() || !self.context.is_system());
        let result = work(self, &Authorization::internal());
        self.tx.authorizing.set(active);
        result
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — admission depends on declared bounds, never on
    // occupants. Private scratch cannot cut the caller's prepaid scan.
    pub(crate) fn authorized_scan<T: Default>(&mut self, allowance: &[(MeterKind, u64)], scan: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
        self.prepaid_scan(allowance, true, scan)
    }

    /// Public or already-authorized data reads still reserve their logical
    /// meter; they do no authorization traversal. A nested scope cannot opt
    /// out of its enclosing authorization's physical allowance.
    pub(super) fn prepaid_scan<T: Default>(&mut self, allowance: &[(MeterKind, u64)], physical: bool, scan: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
        // This meter is the device's separate physical-work budget. Its
        // caller maps exhaustion to uncertainty, never a logical E_BOUND.
        if self.device_work_active {
            let active = self.tx.authorizing.replace(self.tx.authorizing.get() || (physical && !self.context.is_system()));
            let result = scan(self, &Authorization::internal());
            self.tx.authorizing.set(active);
            return result;
        }
        for &(kind, amount) in allowance {
            if !self.read_charge(kind, amount)? { return Ok(T::default()); }
        }
        if self.read_capped() { return Ok(T::default()); }
        let scope = Authorization { probes: Cell::new(0), remaining_probes: self.meter.ceilings.rule_probes.saturating_sub(self.meter.used.rule_probes) };
        let state = self.enter_prepaid(physical);
        let result = scan(self, &scope);
        self.leave_prepaid(state, result.as_ref().err());
        if scope.probes.get() > 0 { self.read_charge(MeterKind::RuleProbes, scope.probes.get())?; }
        result
    }

    // Kept out of the generic closure wrapper: every protected access shares
    // the same scope transition instead of instantiating its restoration code.
    #[inline(never)]
    pub(super) fn enter_prepaid(&mut self, physical: bool) -> PrepaidState {
        let nested = self.caller_heap_ceiling.is_some();
        self.caller_heap_ceiling.get_or_insert((self.meter.ceilings.heap_bytes, self.meter.used.heap_bytes));
        PrepaidState {
            mark: self.meter.mark(),
            ceilings: std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter.ceilings, Ceilings::unbounded()),
            cut: std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter.cut, Cut::Abort),
            authorizing: self.tx.authorizing.replace(self.tx.authorizing.get() || (physical && !self.context.is_system())),
            nested,
        }
    }

    #[inline(never)]
    pub(super) fn leave_prepaid(&mut self, state: PrepaidState, error: Option<&RuntimeError>) {
        self.tx.authorizing.set(state.authorizing);
        self.meter.restore(state.mark);
        self.meter.ceilings = state.ceilings;
        self.meter.cut = state.cut;
        if !state.nested { self.caller_heap_ceiling = None; }
        if let Some(RuntimeError::Bound { kind: MeterKind::HeapBytes, site, .. }) = error {
            self.meter.capped_at.get_or_insert((MeterKind::HeapBytes, site.clone()));
        }
    }

}

#[cfg(all(test, feature = "sqlite"))]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::{Context, Store, meter::Meter, schema::Schema};

    #[test]
    fn job_authority_edges_clear_raw_cache_but_keep_the_allowance() {
        let mut store = Store::memory().unwrap();
        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        let schema = Schema::default();
        let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &schema, Context::system(), Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort), 0);
        runner.tx.remaining.set(17);
        *runner.tx.lookup_cache.borrow_mut() = Some(("t".into(), "byId".into(), vec![], None));
        let child = runner.job_read_child(Context::new("user:alice", Default::default()));
        assert!(child.tx.lookup_cache.borrow().is_none());
        assert_eq!(child.tx.remaining(), 17);
        child.tx.remaining.set(13);
        *child.tx.lookup_cache.borrow_mut() = Some(("t".into(), "byId".into(), vec![], None));
        runner.finish_job_read_child(child);
        assert!(runner.tx.lookup_cache.borrow().is_none());
        assert_eq!(runner.tx.remaining(), 13);
    }

    #[test]
    fn raw_write_fetches_reserve_before_even_an_absent_candidate() {
        use crate::{
            Value,
            rows::MemoryRows, schema::{ColumnType, FieldAuthority, public_table},
        };
        let rows = MemoryRows::new();
        let mut schema = Schema::default();
        let mut table = public_table([("id".into(),ColumnType::Id),("owner".into(),ColumnType::Principal),
            ("secret".into(),ColumnType::Text { max: 1000000 })].into(), Default::default());
        table.indexes.insert("byId".into(),crate::schema::Index::of(&["id"],true));
        table.written_by.insert("secret".into(),FieldAuthority { owner:"owner".into(),audience:false });
        schema.tables.insert("records".into(),table);
        for lookup in [false,true] {
            let mut runner = Runner::new(&rows,&schema,Context::new("alice",Default::default()),
                Meter::new(Ceilings {heap_bytes:32,..Default::default()},Cut::Abort),0);
            let result = if lookup {
                let index=&schema.tables["records"].indexes["byId"];
                runner.lookup_stored("records","byId",index,&[Value::Id("absent".into())],false)
            } else { runner.metered_scan(|runner, scope|runner.fetch(scope,"records","absent")) };
            assert!(matches!(result,Err(RuntimeError::Bound {kind:MeterKind::HeapBytes,..})),"lookup={lookup}: {result:?}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn scratch_keeps_only_the_fixed_peak_on_success_and_failure() {
        let rows = crate::rows::MemoryRows::new();
        let schema = Schema::default();
        for hidden in [0,1000000] {
            for refuses in [false,true] {
                let mut runner=Runner::new(&rows,&schema,Context::new("alice",Default::default()),Meter::new(Ceilings::default(),Cut::Abort),0);
                let result=runner.authorized_scratch(4096,&[(MeterKind::RuleProbes,2)],|runner,_| {
                    runner.meter.heap(hidden)?;
                    if refuses { Err(RuntimeError::Input("internal test error".into())) } else { Ok(()) }
                });
                assert_eq!(result.is_err(),refuses);
                assert_eq!(runner.meter.used.heap_bytes,0);
                assert_eq!(runner.meter.heap_peak,4096);
                assert_eq!(runner.meter.used.rule_probes,2);
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn allowance_alone_decides_admission_and_every_exit_keeps_it() {
        let mut store = Store::memory().unwrap();
        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        let schema = Schema::default();
        for cut in [Cut::Cap, Cut::Abort] {
            for hidden_work in [0, 1, 8193] {
                for refuses in [false, true] {
                    let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &schema, Context::new("alice", Default::default()), Meter::new(Ceilings { examined: 2, rule_probes: 2, heap_bytes: 8, ..Default::default() }, cut), 0);
                    let result = runner.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::Examined, 2), (MeterKind::RuleProbes, 2)], |runner, _| {
                        runner.meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, hidden_work)?;
                        runner.meter.charge(MeterKind::RuleProbes, hidden_work)?;
                        runner.meter.heap(hidden_work * 1024)?;
                        if refuses { Err(RuntimeError::Rule { table: "private".into(), effect: crate::schema::Effect::Insert }) }
                        else { Ok(()) }
                    });
                    assert_eq!(result.is_err(), refuses);
                    assert_eq!(runner.meter.used.examined, 2);
                    assert_eq!(runner.meter.used.rule_probes, 2);
                    assert_eq!(runner.meter.used.heap_bytes, 0);
                    assert_eq!(runner.meter.heap_peak, 0);
                    assert!(runner.meter.capped_at.is_none());
                    assert_eq!(runner.meter.ceilings.examined, 2);
                    assert_eq!(runner.meter.cut, cut);
                    let result = runner.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::Examined, 1)], |_, _| -> Result<(), RuntimeError> { panic!("admission must precede all occupant access") });
                    if cut == Cut::Abort { assert!(matches!(result, Err(RuntimeError::Bound { kind: MeterKind::Examined, actual: 3, ceiling: 2, .. }))); }
                    else { assert!(result.is_ok()); assert!(runner.meter.capped_at.is_some()); }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Standalone physical accounting has its own meter. Its token is borrowed
/// only for `run`, never constructible on a caller ledger or returned by it.
pub struct InternalLedger(crate::meter::Meter);
pub struct InternalMeter<'a>(&'a mut Meter);
impl InternalMeter<'_> {
    pub fn heap(&mut self, bytes: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> { self.0.heap(bytes) }
    pub fn charge(&mut self, kind: MeterKind, amount: u64) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> { self.0.charge(kind, amount) }
    pub fn at(&mut self, site: &str) { self.0.at(site); }
    pub fn step(&mut self, steps: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> { self.0.step(steps) }
    /// Release temporary allocations without exposing the saved heap counter.
    pub fn scratch<T>(&mut self, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> T) -> T {
        let mark = self.0.mark();
        let result = work(self);
        self.0.release_heap(mark);
        result
    }
    pub fn examined_room(&self, rows: usize) -> bool { self.0.room(MeterKind::Examined, rows as u64) }
    pub(crate) fn room(&self, kind: MeterKind, amount: u64) -> bool { self.0.room(kind, amount) }
    pub(crate) fn guarded(&self) -> u64 { self.0.scratch }
    pub(crate) fn add_scratch(&mut self, bytes: u64) -> u64 { self.0.scratch = self.0.scratch.saturating_add(bytes); self.0.scratch }
}
impl InternalLedger {
    pub(crate) fn with_meter<T>(meter: &mut crate::meter::Meter, work: impl FnOnce(&mut InternalMeter<'_>, &Authorization) -> T,
    ) -> T {
        work(&mut InternalMeter(meter), &Authorization::internal())
    }
    pub fn new(meter: crate::meter::Meter) -> Self { Self(meter) }
    pub fn run<T>(&mut self, work: impl FnOnce(&mut InternalMeter<'_>, &Authorization) -> T) -> T {
        work(&mut InternalMeter(&mut self.0), &Authorization::internal())
    }
}

#[cfg(all(test,feature="sqlite"))]
mod row_view_tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::{Context, Schema, meter::Meter, rows::MemoryRows};
    #[test]
    fn internal_work_cannot_change_reserved_receipt_or_cut() {
        let rows=MemoryRows::new(); let schema=Schema::default();
        for hidden in [0,1,17<<20] {
            for error in [false,true] {
                let mut r=Runner::new(&rows,&schema,Context::new("alice",Default::default()),Meter::new(Ceilings::default(),Cut::Cap),0);
                let out=r.authorized_scratch(8192,&[(MeterKind::Examined,1),(MeterKind::Steps,1)],|r,_| {
                    r.meter.heap(hidden)?; r.meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined,hidden)?;
                    if error {Err(RuntimeError::Input("internal test error".into()))} else {Ok(())}
                });
                assert_eq!(out.is_err(),error);
                assert_eq!(r.meter.used.examined,1); assert_eq!(r.meter.used.steps,1);
                assert_eq!(r.meter.used.heap_bytes,0); assert_eq!(r.meter.heap_peak,8192);
                assert!(r.meter.capped_at.is_none()); assert_eq!(r.meter.ceilings,Ceilings::default());
            }
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
impl<'a> Runner<'a> {
    /// Fresh read state over this exact transaction; move the guarded allowance
    /// with the meter so nested queries cannot reset authorization work.
    pub(super) fn job_read_child(&mut self, context: super::Context) -> Runner<'a> {
        self.tx.lookup_cache.borrow_mut().take();
        let meter = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort));
        let mut child = Runner::new(self.tx.raw, self.schema, context, meter, self.seq);
        std::mem::swap(&mut child.tx, &mut self.tx);
        child.job_read_scope = 2;
        child
    }
    pub(super) fn finish_job_read_child(&mut self, mut child: Runner<'a>) {
        child.tx.lookup_cache.borrow_mut().take();
        std::mem::swap(&mut child.tx, &mut self.tx);
        self.meter = child.meter;
        self.read_tables.extend(child.read_tables);
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.028#3.3.1 — decoration has separate coverage, never separate
// resource or authorization allowances. Move both, including exhausted counters.
impl<'a> Runner<'a> {
    pub(super) fn decoration_child(&mut self) -> Result<Runner<'a>, RuntimeError> {
        self.meter.heap(1024 + self.context.args.values().map(super::runner::expression_heap).sum::<u64>())?;
        #[cfg(feature = "server-search")]
        self.meter.heap(self.context.search_retained_order.as_ref().map_or(0, |(keys, _)| keys.len() as u64 * 8)
            + self.context.search_retained_candidates.iter().map(|(id, _, _)| 64 + id.len() as u64).sum::<u64>())?;
        let placeholder = Meter::new(self.meter.ceilings, self.meter.cut);
        let meter = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, placeholder);
        let mut child = Runner::new(self.tx.raw, self.schema, self.context.clone(), meter, self.seq);
        std::mem::swap(&mut child.tx, &mut self.tx);
        child.device = self.device;
        child.meter.cut = Cut::Abort;
        Ok(child)
    }
    pub(super) fn finish_decoration_child(&mut self, mut child: Runner<'a>) {
        child.tx.lookup_cache.borrow_mut().take();
        std::mem::swap(&mut child.tx, &mut self.tx);
        child.meter.cut = self.meter.cut;
        self.meter = child.meter;
        self.read_tables.extend(child.read_tables);
        // Decoration expiry invalidates the value, but never changes freshness
        // or the page's completeness. Re-evaluation substitutes null after expiry.
        self.decoration_expiry = child.next_expiry.get();
    }
}

/// Text forbids C0 controls except tab, LF and CR.
pub fn disallowed_text_control(text: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    text.chars().find(|c| c.is_control() && !matches!(c, '\t' | '\n' | '\r')).map(|c| c as u32)
}

pub(crate) fn fits(kind: &ColumnType, value: Option<&Value>) -> bool {
    match (kind, value) {
        (ColumnType::Optional(_), None | Some(Value::Null)) => true,
        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), Some(value)) => fits(inner, Some(value)),
        (ColumnType::List { of, max } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, max, .. }, Some(Value::Array(values))) => values.len() <= *max as usize && values.iter().all(|value| fits(of, Some(value))),
        // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — typed references do not imply target existence
        (ColumnType::Id | ColumnType::Principal | ColumnType::Ref { .. }, Some(Value::Id(_))) => true,
        (ColumnType::Text { max }, Some(Value::String(text))) => text.chars().count() <= *max as usize,
        (ColumnType::Bytes { max }, Some(Value::Bytes(bytes))) => bytes.len() <= *max as usize,
        (ColumnType::Image { .. } | ColumnType::Video { .. } | ColumnType::File { .. }, Some(Value::Map(fields))) => fields.get("id").is_some_and(|id| matches!(id, Value::Id(_))),
        (ColumnType::Enum { variants }, Some(Value::String(value))) => variants.contains(value),
        (ColumnType::Int | ColumnType::Time | ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. }, Some(Value::Int(value))) => (I53_MIN..=I53_MAX).contains(value),
        // @ref LLP 3000.040#14-where-the-bound-is-enforced — the slot's bound is part of its type: every stored write and argument meets it here.
        (ColumnType::IntRange { min, max }, Some(Value::Int(value))) => (I53_MIN..=I53_MAX).contains(value) && (*min..=*max).contains(value),
        (ColumnType::Bool, Some(Value::Bool(_))) => true,
        (ColumnType::Json { max_bytes }, Some(value)) => canonical_json(value).len() <= *max_bytes as usize,
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// Validate the arguments and fill each omitted optional with `null`, so
/// a caller that leaves `c` out reads page one.
#[cfg(not(all(target_arch = "wasm32", feature = "web", not(feature = "sqlite"))))]
pub fn validate_inputs(schema: &Schema, program: &Program, inputs: &mut BTreeMap<String, Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    super::admission::check(schema, program)?;
    validate_arguments(schema, program, inputs)
}

// @ref LLP 3000.002#proposed-device-representation-and-codec-redesign — the web predicts a server-admitted backend; the server and native hosts still check every call.
pub(super) fn validate_device_inputs(schema: &Schema, program: &Program, inputs: &mut BTreeMap<String, Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    #[cfg(not(any(all(target_arch = "wasm32", feature = "web", not(feature = "sqlite")), feature = "web-device-check")))]
    super::admission::check(schema, program)?;
    validate_arguments(schema, program, inputs)
}

fn validate_arguments(schema: &Schema, program: &Program, inputs: &mut BTreeMap<String, Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    for (name, kind) in &program.args {
        if !inputs.contains_key(name) && (kind.is_optional() || matches!(kind, ArgType::Cursor)) {
            inputs.insert(name.clone(), Value::Null);
        }
        let value = inputs.get(name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input(format!("missing argument {name}")))?;
        validate_arg(schema, kind, value, name)?;
    }
    if let Some(extra) = inputs.keys().find(|name| !program.args.contains_key(*name)) {
        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{} takes no argument {extra}", program.name)));
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn validate_arg(schema: &Schema, kind: &ArgType, value: &Value, label: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    if !kind.bounds_valid() {
        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} has a minimum greater than its maximum")));
    }
    crate::value::validate_identities(value)?;

fn title(value: &str) -> String {
    let mut chars = value.chars();
    match chars.next() {
        Some(first) => first.to_uppercase().collect::<String>() + chars.as_str(),
        None => String::new(),
    }
}

/// The columns of a generated maintain target: `id`, `value`, and the `by`
/// columns typed as the source declares them.
pub fn maintain_target(source: &TableInfo, maintain: &MaintainDecl) -> Fallible<TableDecl> {
    const GLOBAL: &str = "$global";
    let site = maintain.site.clone();
    if source.maintained.is_some() { return Err(super::maintains::refusal(&site, "a maintain cannot use another maintain as its source", "define the view over application source rows, or use a job sweep")); }
    let mut columns = Vec::new();
    let value_type = match &maintain.column {
        None => ScalarType { kind: TypeKind::Int, optional: false },
        Some(column) => match source.columns.get(column) {
            Some(ty) if ty.optional && matches!(ty.kind, TypeKind::Int | TypeKind::IntRange { .. } | TypeKind::Decimal { .. } | TypeKind::Money { .. }) => {
                return Err(type_error(&site, format!("sum over {}.{column} cannot add null: the numeric column is optional (`?`); its numeric range is accepted", maintain.source),
                    format!("make {column} required (`{column}: {}`) and give every row a numeric contribution; if absence must stay distinct, add a required numeric contribution column default 0 and sum that column instead", crate::print::scalar_type(&ty.required()))).guide("maintains"));
            }
            Some(ty) if matches!(ty.kind, TypeKind::IntRange { .. }) => ScalarType { kind: TypeKind::Int, optional: false },
            Some(ty) if matches!(ty.kind, TypeKind::Int | TypeKind::Decimal { .. } | TypeKind::Money { .. }) => ty.required(),
            Some(ty) => return Err(type_error(&site, format!("sum over {}.{column} needs int, decimal or money, not {}", maintain.source, crate::print::scalar_type(ty)), format!("view {}: count {} by {}", maintain.name, maintain.source, maintain.keys.iter().map(|key| super::maintains::bare_key(key).map_or_else(|| crate::print::expression(key), |name| format!(".{name}"))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")))),
            None => return Err(unknown(&site, format!("sum names unknown column {}.{column}", maintain.source), name_rewrite(column, source.columns.keys().map(String::as_str), None))),
        },
    };
    columns.push(ColumnDecl { on_delete: None, sequence: None, written_by: None, readable_by_audience: false, maintained: None, default: None, name: "value".into(), type_: value_type, site: site.clone() });
    let computed = super::maintains::keys(&source, maintain)?;
    let aliases = super::maintains::inherited_aliases(source,maintain);
    if let Some(expr) = &maintain.filter { super::maintains::predicate(&source, expr)?; }
    for field in &maintain.by {
        let ty = if computed.contains_key(field) { ScalarType { kind: TypeKind::Int, optional: computed[field].column.contains('.') } } else { source.columns[aliases.get(field).unwrap_or(field)].clone() };
        columns.push(ColumnDecl { on_delete: None, sequence: None, written_by: None, readable_by_audience: false, maintained: None, default: None, name: field.clone(), type_: ty, site: site.clone() });
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.013.001#3-global-maintained-view-representation — the logical empty tuple gets one store-indexable, compiler-only discriminator.
    let group = if maintain.by.is_empty() {
        columns.push(ColumnDecl { on_delete: None, sequence: None, written_by: None, readable_by_audience: false, maintained: None, default: None, name: GLOBAL.into(), type_: ScalarType { kind: TypeKind::Bool, optional: false }, site: site.clone() });
        vec![GLOBAL.into()]
    } else { maintain.by.clone() };
    let mut indexes = vec![IndexDecl { name: "byGroup".into(), columns: group, unique: true, refusal: None, words: None, computed: BTreeMap::new(), site: site.clone() }];
    let mut names = BTreeSet::from(["byGroup".to_owned(), "byId".to_owned()]);
    for index in &maintain.indexes {
        if !names.insert(index.name.clone()) { return Err(super::maintains::refusal(&index.site, format!("duplicate maintain index {}", index.name), "use a distinct index name; byGroup and byId are generated")); }
        let index = index.clone();
        if index.columns.contains(&"value".into()) {
            // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.21 — stored order is stale; the sound server count upper-bound threshold read is not built.
            if source.decl.expire.is_some() || source.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.expiring) { return Err(Diagnostic::new(&index.site, "E_QUARRY_MAINTAIN_EXPIRE", format!("maintain {} cannot order by value because source {} expires: stored order is stale before the physical sweep, so taking stored top-N can miss a live winner; a count upper-bound threshold scan is not built", maintain.name, maintain.source), "for an entity-time window over a non-expiring source, use the Trending predicate in guide feeds; for expiring contributions, stream each candidate's live count and rank only a complete candidate domain; a meter cut makes the ranking incomplete").guide("feeds")); }
            // @ref LLP 3000.007#14 — ruling 41's interim retires with maintained columns.
            let value_at = index.columns.iter().position(|field| field == "value").unwrap();
            let fields = index.columns.iter().collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();

//! Generated device/server parity for commit-end lifetime retirement. Each
//! source runs through the public sync wire and both device stores, so an
//! offline prediction cannot silently omit a cascade, set-null or restrict
//! action performed by the server.

#[path = "../../snapback4-device/tests/common/mod.rs"]
mod device_common;

use device_common::{
    BoundaryMetadata, Host, Memory, Sqlite, args, compile, id, snapshot_pages, stream_page,
};
use serde_json::json;
use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, WriteState};
use snapback4_device::device::Device;

const NOW: i64 = 4_000_000_000_000;
const GENERATED_SOURCES: usize = 18;
const GENERATED_NEGATIVE_SOURCES: usize = 9;
const RUNTIME_CASES: usize = GENERATED_SOURCES * 2;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
enum Action {
    Cascade,
    SetNull,
    Restrict,
}

impl Action {
    fn word(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Cascade => "cascade",
            Self::SetNull => "set null",
            Self::Restrict => "restrict",
        }
    }

    fn optional(self) -> &'static str {
        if matches!(self, Self::SetNull) {
            " ?"
        } else {
            ""
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
enum Prelude {
    Snapshot,
    Stream,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
enum Target {
    ExpiredWithInbound,
    FutureWithInbound,
    ExpiredWithoutInbound,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum IncompleteCoverage {
    MissingChild,
    AudienceHidden,
    PartiallyAcquired,
}

impl Target {
    fn has_inbound(self) -> bool {
        !matches!(self, Self::ExpiredWithoutInbound)
    }

    fn requested_expiry(self) -> i64 {
        if matches!(self, Self::FutureWithInbound) {
            NOW + 10_000
        } else {
            NOW
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct Generated {
    seed: u64,
    action: Action,
    prelude: Prelude,
    target: Target,
    viewer: &'static str,
    decoys: usize,
    source: String,
}

fn generated_sources() -> Vec<Generated> {
    let mut generated = Vec::new();
    let mut seed = 0_u64;
    for action in [Action::Cascade, Action::SetNull, Action::Restrict] {
        for target in [
            Target::ExpiredWithInbound,
            Target::FutureWithInbound,
            Target::ExpiredWithoutInbound,
        ] {
            for prelude in [Prelude::Snapshot, Prelude::Stream] {
                let viewer = ["alice", "bob", "carol"][(seed as usize) % 3];
                let decoys = 1 + (seed as usize % 2);
                let cap = decoys + 2;
                let source = format!(
                    r#"use personas alice, bob, carol
table parents:
  until: time
  token: int
  expire at .until
  public 'generated expiry parents seed {seed}'
  insert <- allow
  update <- allow
  sync public
table children:
  parent: parents{optional} on delete {action}
  marker: int
  cap {cap} by parent
  public 'generated expiry children seed {seed}'
  insert <- allow
  sync public
mutation addChild(id: id, parent: parents, marker: int):
  insert children {{ id, parent, marker }}
mutation setExpiry(parent: parents, until: time):
  update parents[parent] {{ until }}
"#,
                    optional = action.optional(),
                    action = action.word(),
                );
                generated.push(Generated {
                    seed,
                    action,
                    prelude,
                    target,
                    viewer,
                    decoys,
                    source,
                });
                seed += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(generated.len(), GENERATED_SOURCES);
    generated
}

fn row(fields: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'static str, Value)>) -> Value {
    snapback4_core::value::object(fields)
}

fn target_parent() -> Value {
    row([
        ("id", id("target")),
        ("until", Value::Int(NOW + 5_000)),
        ("token", Value::Int(7)),
    ])
}

fn target_child(seed: u64) -> Value {
    row([
        ("id", id("target-child")),
        ("parent", id("target")),
        ("marker", Value::Int(seed as i64)),
    ])
}

fn decoy_parent(index: usize) -> Value {
    row([
        ("id", id(&format!("decoy-parent-{index}"))),
        ("until", Value::Int(NOW + 20_000 + index as i64)),
        ("token", Value::Int(100 + index as i64)),
    ])
}

fn decoy_child(index: usize) -> Value {
    row([
        ("id", id(&format!("decoy-child-{index}"))),
        ("parent", id(&format!("decoy-parent-{index}"))),
        ("marker", Value::Int(200 + index as i64)),
    ])
}

fn seed_rows(case: &Generated) -> Vec<(String, Value)> {
    let mut rows = vec![("parents".to_owned(), target_parent())];
    for index in 0..case.decoys {
        rows.push(("parents".to_owned(), decoy_parent(index)));
        let streamed_decoy =
            matches!(case.prelude, Prelude::Stream) && !case.target.has_inbound() && index == 0;
        if !streamed_decoy {
            rows.push(("children".to_owned(), decoy_child(index)));
        }
    }
    if case.target.has_inbound() && matches!(case.prelude, Prelude::Snapshot) {
        rows.push(("children".to_owned(), target_child(case.seed)));
    }
    rows
}

fn canonical(rows: Vec<Value>) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut rows = rows
        .into_iter()
        .map(|row| {
            let mut row = snapback4_core::wire::to_json(&row);
            // `pending` is device settlement metadata, not an authored field;
            // parity below compares the predicted data image with the server's
            // committed data image.
            if let Some(object) = row.as_object_mut() {
                object.remove("pending");
            }
            serde_json::to_string(&row).unwrap()
        })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    rows.sort();
    rows
}

fn device_rows<S: BoundaryMetadata>(device: &Device<S>, table: &str) -> Vec<Value> {
    device.store().raw_rows(table)
}

fn server_rows(server: &Engine, table: &str) -> Vec<Value> {
    server.store().rows(table).unwrap()
}

fn row_by_id<'a>(rows: &'a [Value], wanted: &str) -> Option<&'a Value> {
    rows.iter()
        .find(|row| row.field("id").ok() == Some(&id(wanted)))
}

fn apply_snapshot<S: BoundaryMetadata>(
    server: &mut Engine,
    device: &mut Device<S>,
    viewer: &str,
) -> (u64, usize) {
    let pages = snapshot_pages(server, viewer, 2);
    let watermark = pages.last().expect("a snapshot has a final page").watermark;
    for (index, page) in pages.iter().enumerate() {
        device.apply(page, index == 0).unwrap();
    }
    (watermark, pages.len())
}

fn server_write(
    server: &mut Engine,
    op: &str,
    viewer: &str,
    values: &[(&str, Value)],
    now: i64,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let outcome = server
        .mutate(op, None, Context::new(viewer, args(values)).at(now))
        .unwrap();
    match outcome.state {
        WriteState::Sent { .. } => Ok(()),
        WriteState::Failed { why, .. } => Err(why.code),
    }
}

fn prelude<S: BoundaryMetadata>(
    case: &Generated,
    server: &mut Engine,
    device: &mut Device<S>,
) -> (usize, usize) {
    let (watermark, snapshot_count) = apply_snapshot(server, device, case.viewer);
    let mut stream_count = 0;
    if matches!(case.prelude, Prelude::Stream) {
        let (child, parent, marker) = if case.target.has_inbound() {
            (
                "target-child".to_owned(),
                "target".to_owned(),
                case.seed as i64,
            )
        } else {
            ("decoy-child-0".to_owned(), "decoy-parent-0".to_owned(), 200)
        };
        server_write(
            server,
            "addChild",
            case.viewer,
            &[
                ("id", id(&child)),
                ("parent", id(&parent)),
                ("marker", Value::Int(marker)),
            ],
            NOW - 1,
        )
        .unwrap();
        device
            .apply(&stream_page(server, case.viewer, watermark), false)
            .unwrap();
        stream_count += 1;
    }

    for table in ["parents", "children"] {
        assert_eq!(
            canonical(device_rows(device, table)),
            canonical(server_rows(server, table)),
            "seed {} {:?}/{:?}: prelude sync differs for {table}",
            case.seed,
            case.action,
            case.prelude,
        );
    }
    (snapshot_count, stream_count)
}

fn assert_expected<S: BoundaryMetadata>(case: &Generated, server: &Engine, device: &Device<S>) {
    let device_parents = device_rows(device, "parents");
    let device_children = device_rows(device, "children");
    let server_parents = server_rows(server, "parents");
    let server_children = server_rows(server, "children");
    let label = format!(
        "seed {} {:?}/{:?}/{:?}",
        case.seed, case.action, case.target, case.prelude
    );

    assert_eq!(
        canonical(device_parents.clone()),
        canonical(server_parents.clone()),
        "{label}: parent parity"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        canonical(device_children.clone()),
        canonical(server_children.clone()),
        "{label}: child parity"
    );

    let target_parent = row_by_id(&device_parents, "target");
    let target_child = row_by_id(&device_children, "target-child");
    match (case.action, case.target) {
        (Action::Restrict, Target::ExpiredWithInbound) => {
            let parent = target_parent.expect("restrict refusal preserves its parent");
            assert_eq!(
                parent.field("until").unwrap(),
                &Value::Int(NOW + 5_000),
                "{label}"
            );
            assert_eq!(
                target_child.map(|row| row.field("parent").unwrap()),
                Some(&id("target")),
                "{label}"
            );
        }
        (_, Target::FutureWithInbound) => {
            let parent = target_parent.expect("future expiry preserves its parent");
            assert_eq!(
                parent.field("until").unwrap(),
                &Value::Int(NOW + 10_000),
                "{label}"
            );
            assert_eq!(
                target_child.map(|row| row.field("parent").unwrap()),
                Some(&id("target")),
                "{label}"
            );
        }
        (Action::Cascade, Target::ExpiredWithInbound) => {
            assert!(target_parent.is_none(), "{label}: expired parent retires");
            assert!(target_child.is_none(), "{label}: cascade retires the child");
        }
        (Action::SetNull, Target::ExpiredWithInbound) => {
            assert!(target_parent.is_none(), "{label}: expired parent retires");
            assert_eq!(
                target_child.map(|row| row.field("parent").unwrap()),
                Some(&Value::Null),
                "{label}"
            );
        }
        (_, Target::ExpiredWithoutInbound) => {
            assert!(
                target_parent.is_none(),
                "{label}: an unreferenced expired parent retires"
            );
            assert!(
                target_child.is_none(),
                "{label}: the source generated no inbound reference"
            );
        }
    }

    let target_remains = matches!(case.target, Target::FutureWithInbound)
        || matches!(
            (case.action, case.target),
            (Action::Restrict, Target::ExpiredWithInbound)
        );
    assert_eq!(
        device_parents.len(),
        case.decoys + if target_remains { 1 } else { 0 },
        "{label}: every decoy parent remains and only the expected target image survives"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        device_children
            .iter()
            .filter(|row| row.field("id").ok() != Some(&id("target-child")))
            .count(),
        case.decoys,
        "{label}: every unrelated child remains",
    );
}

fn run_case<H: Host>(host: &mut H, case: &Generated) -> (usize, usize) {
    let (mut server, backend) = compile(&case.source);
    server.seed_at(seed_rows(case), NOW - 100).unwrap();
    let store_name = format!("w12-expiry-generated-{}", case.seed);
    let mut device = host.open(&store_name, Some(backend)).unwrap();
    let counts = prelude(case, &mut server, &mut device);
    let input = json!({"parent":"target", "until":case.target.requested_expiry()});
    let predicted = device.predict("setExpiry", case.viewer, &input, NOW, vec![], 1);
    let committed = server_write(
        &mut server,
        "setExpiry",
        case.viewer,
        &[
            ("parent", id("target")),
            ("until", Value::Int(case.target.requested_expiry())),
        ],
        NOW,
    );

    if matches!(
        (case.action, case.target),
        (Action::Restrict, Target::ExpiredWithInbound)
    ) {
        assert_eq!(
            predicted.unwrap_err().code(),
            "E_REFERENCED",
            "seed {} {}",
            case.seed,
            host.label()
        );
        assert_eq!(
            committed.unwrap_err(),
            "E_REFERENCED",
            "seed {} {}",
            case.seed,
            host.label()
        );
    } else {
        assert!(
            predicted.is_ok(),
            "seed {} {}: {predicted:?}",
            case.seed,
            host.label()
        );
        assert_eq!(committed, Ok(()), "seed {} {}", case.seed, host.label());
    }
    assert_expected(case, &server, &device);
    host.close(&store_name, device);
    counts
}

fn incomplete_source(seed: u64, action: Action) -> String {
    let cap = 3 + seed as usize % 2;
    format!(
        r#"use personas alice, bob, carol
table parents:
  until: time
  expire at .until
  public 'incomplete expiry parents seed {seed}'
  update <- allow
  sync public
table children:
  parent: parents{optional} on delete {action}
  owner: principal
  cap {cap} by parent
  read <- .owner = viewer
  insert <- .owner = viewer
  sync to .owner
mutation setExpiry(parent: parents, until: time):
  update parents[parent] {{ until }}
"#,
        optional = action.optional(),
        action = action.word(),
    )
}

fn incomplete_rows(mode: IncompleteCoverage, viewer: &str) -> Vec<(String, Value)> {
    let mut rows = vec![(
        "parents".to_owned(),
        row([("id", id("target")), ("until", Value::Int(NOW + 5_000))]),
    )];
    let hidden = if viewer == "alice" { "bob" } else { "alice" };
    if matches!(
        mode,
        IncompleteCoverage::AudienceHidden | IncompleteCoverage::PartiallyAcquired
    ) {
        rows.push((
            "children".to_owned(),
            row([
                ("id", id("hidden")),
                ("parent", id("target")),
                ("owner", id(hidden)),
            ]),
        ));
    }
    if matches!(mode, IncompleteCoverage::PartiallyAcquired) {
        rows.push((
            "children".to_owned(),
            row([
                ("id", id("visible")),
                ("parent", id("target")),
                ("owner", id(viewer)),
            ]),
        ));
    }
    rows
}

fn run_incomplete_case<H: Host>(
    host: &mut H,
    seed: u64,
    action: Action,
    mode: IncompleteCoverage,
) -> usize {
    let source = incomplete_source(seed, action);
    let (mut server, backend) = compile(&source);
    let viewer = ["alice", "bob", "carol"][(seed as usize) % 3];
    server
        .seed_at(incomplete_rows(mode, viewer), NOW - 100)
        .unwrap();
    let store_name = format!("w12-expiry-incomplete-{seed}");
    let mut device = host.open(&store_name, Some(backend)).unwrap();
    let (_, pages) = apply_snapshot(&mut server, &mut device, viewer);
    let parents_before = canonical(device_rows(&device, "parents"));
    let children_before = canonical(device_rows(&device, "children"));

    let predicted = device
        .predict(
            "setExpiry",
            viewer,
            &json!({"parent":"target", "until":NOW}),
            NOW,
            vec![],
            1,
        )
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(
        predicted.code(),
        "E_PREDICT",
        "seed {seed} {action:?}/{mode:?} {} must queue an unprovable action group",
        host.label()
    );
    assert_eq!(
        canonical(device_rows(&device, "parents")),
        parents_before,
        "seed {seed} {action:?}/{mode:?}: a queued mutation changes no parent"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        canonical(device_rows(&device, "children")),
        children_before,
        "seed {seed} {action:?}/{mode:?}: a queued mutation changes no visible child"
    );

    let committed = server_write(
        &mut server,
        "setExpiry",
        viewer,
        &[("parent", id("target")), ("until", Value::Int(NOW))],
        NOW,
    );
    let has_child = mode != IncompleteCoverage::MissingChild;
    if matches!(action, Action::Restrict) && has_child {
        assert_eq!(
            committed,
            Err("E_REFERENCED".to_owned()),
            "seed {seed} {mode:?}"
        );
        assert!(row_by_id(&server_rows(&server, "parents"), "target").is_some());
    } else {
        assert_eq!(committed, Ok(()), "seed {seed} {action:?}/{mode:?}");
        assert!(row_by_id(&server_rows(&server, "parents"), "target").is_none());
        let children = server_rows(&server, "children");
        match action {
            Action::Cascade => assert!(children.is_empty(), "seed {seed} {mode:?}"),
            Action::SetNull => assert!(
                children
                    .iter()
                    .all(|row| row.field("parent").ok() == Some(&Value::Null)),
                "seed {seed} {mode:?}"
            ),
            Action::Restrict => assert!(
                children.is_empty(),
                "the missing-child control has no child"
            ),
        }
    }
    host.close(&store_name, device);
    pages
}

#[test]
fn generated_commit_end_expiry_actions_match_server_on_both_device_stores() {
    let generated = generated_sources();
    let mut memory = Memory::new();
    let mut sqlite = Sqlite::new("w12-expiry-generated");
    let mut runtime_cases = 0;
    let mut snapshot_pages_seen = 0;
    let mut stream_pages_seen = 0;
    for case in &generated {
        for counts in [run_case(&mut memory, case), run_case(&mut sqlite, case)] {
            runtime_cases += 1;
            snapshot_pages_seen += counts.0;
            stream_pages_seen += counts.1;
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(runtime_cases, RUNTIME_CASES);
    assert_eq!(
        stream_pages_seen, 18,
        "nine stream-prelude sources run on two stores"
    );
    assert!(
        snapshot_pages_seen >= runtime_cases,
        "every runtime starts from a real public-sync snapshot"
    );
    println!(
        "generated {GENERATED_SOURCES} sources; {runtime_cases} Memory/SQLite cases; {snapshot_pages_seen} snapshot pages; {stream_pages_seen} prelude stream pages; 72 independently asserted target outcomes"
    );
}

#[test]
fn generated_incomplete_action_groups_queue_without_predicted_rows() {
    let mut memory = Memory::new();
    let mut sqlite = Sqlite::new("w12-expiry-incomplete");
    let mut seed = 100_u64;
    let mut sources = 0;
    let mut runtime_cases = 0;
    let mut snapshot_pages_seen = 0;
    for action in [Action::Cascade, Action::SetNull, Action::Restrict] {
        for mode in [
            IncompleteCoverage::MissingChild,
            IncompleteCoverage::AudienceHidden,
            IncompleteCoverage::PartiallyAcquired,
        ] {
            snapshot_pages_seen += run_incomplete_case(&mut memory, seed, action, mode);
            snapshot_pages_seen += run_incomplete_case(&mut sqlite, seed, action, mode);
            sources += 1;
            runtime_cases += 2;
            seed += 1;
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(sources, GENERATED_NEGATIVE_SOURCES);
    assert_eq!(runtime_cases, GENERATED_NEGATIVE_SOURCES * 2);
    assert!(snapshot_pages_seen >= runtime_cases);
    println!(
        "generated {sources} incomplete-coverage sources; {runtime_cases} Memory/SQLite queue cases; {snapshot_pages_seen} snapshot pages; all 18 device outcomes were exact E_PREDICT with zero local changes"
    );
}

//! Expiry actions whose child writes feed a private maintained column must
//! settle on the server: the public device schema has the price but not the
//! private derivation that computes the new total (LLP 3000.007.001 §3.7).
mod common;
use common::*;
use serde_json::json;
use snapback4_core::{Context, WriteState, value::{Value, object}};
use snapback4_device::{device::{Device, StreamPage}, store::DeviceStore};

const SOURCE: &str = r#"
table groups:
  total: count children by .group
  public
  sync public
table parents:
  until: time
  expire at .until
  public
  update <- allow
  sync public
table children:
  parent: parents on delete cascade
  group: groups
  cap 4 by parent
  public
  insert <- allow
  sync public
mutation expire(parent: parents, group: groups):
  insert children { id: 'born', parent, group }
  update parents[parent] { until: 0 }
query group(id: groups):
  return groups[id] { total }
"#;

fn acquire<S: DeviceStore>(engine: &mut snapback4_core::Engine, device: &mut Device<S>) {
    let mut after = None;
    let mut first = true;
    loop {
        let page = engine.snapshot_acquisition_page_at("alice", after.as_deref(), 100, 100).unwrap();
        let next = page.next.map(|next| next.encode());
        let page: StreamPage = serde_json::from_value(json!({
            "snapshot":true, "after":after, "held":page.held, "acquisitions":page.acquisitions,
            "events":page.events.iter().map(|event| json!({"table":event.table,"kind":event.kind.word(),"id":event.id,
                "data":event.data.as_ref().map(snapback4_core::wire::to_json)})).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            "watermark":page.watermark, "more":next.is_some(), "next":next, "generation":engine.generation(),
        })).unwrap();
        device.apply(&page, first).unwrap();
        let Some(next) = next else { break };
        after = Some(next);
        first = false;
    }
}

fn run<H: Host>(host: &mut H) {
    let (mut server, backend) = compile(SOURCE);
    server.seed_at([
        ("groups".into(), object([("id", id("g"))])),
        ("parents".into(), object([("id", id("p")), ("until", Value::Int(200))])),
        ("children".into(), object([("id", id("old")), ("parent", id("p")), ("group", id("g"))])),
    ], 0).unwrap();
    let mut device = host.open("expiry-maintained-column", Some(backend)).unwrap();
    acquire(&mut server, &mut device);
    assert_eq!(device.query("group", "alice", &json!({"id":"g"}), 100).unwrap().data, object([("total", Value::Int(1))]));

    let error = device.predict("expire", "alice", &json!({"parent":"p","group":"g"}), 100, vec![], 1).unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_PREDICT", "{}: {error:?}", host.label());
    assert_eq!(device.store().raw_rows("parents").len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(device.store().raw_rows("children").len(), 1, "queued prediction publishes neither birth nor cascade");
    assert_eq!(device.query("group", "alice", &json!({"id":"g"}), 100).unwrap().data, object([("total", Value::Int(1))]));

    let from = server.seq().unwrap();
    let outcome = server.mutate("expire", None, Context::new("alice", args(&[("parent", id("p")), ("group", id("g"))])).at(100)).unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(outcome.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{outcome:?}");
    device.apply(&stream_page(&mut server, "alice", from), false).unwrap();
    assert!(device.store().raw_rows("parents").is_empty());
    assert!(device.store().raw_rows("children").is_empty());
    assert_eq!(device.query("group", "alice", &json!({"id":"g"}), 100).unwrap().data, object([("total", Value::Int(0))]));
    host.close("expiry-maintained-column", device);
}

#[test] fn expiry_maintained_column_memory() { run(&mut Memory::new()); }
#[test] fn expiry_maintained_column_sqlite() { run(&mut Sqlite::new("expiry-maintained-column")); }

pub const I53_MAX: i64 = (1_i64 << 53) - 1;
pub const I53_MIN: i64 = -I53_MAX;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Value {
    Null,
    Bool(bool),
    Int(i64),
    String(String),
    Id(String),
    Bytes(#[serde(with = "bytes_hex")] Vec<u8>),
    Row(ObjectFields),
    Array(Vec<Value>),
    Map(ObjectFields),
}

}

        self.1 = true;
        self.insert("retained".into(), Value::Bool(true));
    }
    pub fn shares_image(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        std::sync::Arc::ptr_eq(&self.0, &other.0)

}

impl Value {
    pub fn has_retained_rows(&self) -> bool {
        match self {

            _ => false,
        }
    }

- **Counter migration accepts invalid predecessor group values and loses opaque sequence custody.** [maintains.rs:65](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/maintains.rs:65) uses `fits`, which omits admission checks enforced by [validate.rs:76](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/validate.rs:76). For a text-grouped aggregate, the canonical ID `[{"String":"\u0001"}]` passes this decoder although U+0001 is forbidden in source text. That escaped JSON string is nevertheless a valid opaque dangling parent ID and can legitimately own sequence history. Adoption moves its counter to a digest and deletes the original key, while unmatched row references retain the opaque ID. Subsequent allocation under that ID restarts at 1, reusing ordinals or causing uniqueness refusals. Validate decoded components with full predecessor column admission; invalid tuples must retain their original counter keys.
